> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Scion

Scion 1.0.0 is a Unity 6 package (`me.jandson.scion`) and a .NET command line (`dotnet scion`). Your game stays
the trunk; new code arrives as small branches grafted onto it at compile time, and every change is played,
captured and compared in the real player build before it ships.

## Install

With Claude Code, add the plugin and ask it to set Scion up:

```sh
/plugin marketplace add Jand-S/scion
/plugin install scion@scion
```

By hand, add the package and the CLI, then check the setup:

```sh
openupm add me.jandson.scion
dotnet new tool-manifest
dotnet tool install --local Scion.Cli --version 1.0.0
dotnet scion init --existing
dotnet scion doctor
```

The [install page](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/install/) covers every path, including other agents and plain Git URLs.

## Grafts

Static C# methods marked `[Before]` or `[After]` hang onto existing game methods, woven into the IL at compile
time. Final builds call them directly; test builds swap them live in about a second.
[How grafts work](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/overview/).

## Trials

Deterministic recipes play in parallel copies of the real test player, headless, on a virtual clock. Each run
records a state hash, frames and images, runs checks and compares everything with approved baselines.
[How trials work](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/overview/).

## Judge

Frozen vision models turn every capture into numbers once; small heads trained in seconds on your own votes
rank results by taste. The Judge filters and orders; a person always makes the final choice.
[The Judge](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/overview/).

## Exploration

Fork a deterministic match at any turn, loop a moment of play while you tune it, bisect regressions, hunt rare
states and search tunables with guided duels. [The multiverse](/scion/41664431a8f5/explore/multiverse/).

## For AI agents

Every command prints one JSON object with a `next_step`. Agents start at
[/scion/llms.txt](/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt), which lists every page as Markdown, and at the
[For AI agents](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/) section.

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# What is Scion

Scion changes and tests a Unity game without editing the game's existing code, and lets an AI agent do it safely.
This page explains the problem, the four modules (Grafts, Trials, Judge, Exploration), the three pieces you install
(the `me.jandson.scion` package, the `dotnet scion` CLI and the agent plugin) and the adoption levels 1 to 3 that
`dotnet scion doctor` reports.

## How it works

### The problem

Reviewing a visual change the usual way is slow and serial: recompile in the editor, press Play, set up the
situation by hand, record a clip and compare by eye. One editor per project means one check at a time. An AI agent
makes it worse: effects live in large files, so every change means reading and editing big methods, and a missed
case goes unnoticed.

Scion's answer is that the editor is the slow part, not the game. A **test build** of the game is compiled once,
opened directly in the state a recipe describes, recorded, measured and closed. Many copies run at the same time,
each with a queue of recipes.

### The four modules

| Module | What it does | Start reading |
|---|---|---|
| **Grafts** | New code in small files (`[Before]` and `[After]` methods) hung on existing methods by a compile-time weaver. The agent creates files next to the game instead of editing large ones. | [How grafts work](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/overview/) |
| **Trials** | Recipes (C# classes) played by the real test player in parallel, deterministic copies. Each result has a state hash, frames, images and checks, compared with approved baselines. | [How trials work](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/overview/) |
| **Judge** | A trainable taste model: frozen vision models plus small heads trained on your votes. It ranks candidates so a person only looks at the finalists. | [The Judge](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/overview/) |
| **Exploration** | Tools built on determinism: fork a match at turn N (multiverse), loop a moment of play, bisect regressions, metamorphic tests, a rare-moment hunter and guided search. | [The multiverse](/scion/41664431a8f5/explore/multiverse/) |

Around them sit the **evaluation funnel** (state checks, objective gates, then taste) and the **Scion Standard**
(rules and analyzers that keep a game easy to graft and test).

### The three pieces

| Piece | What it is | How you get it |
|---|---|---|
| Unity package `me.jandson.scion` | Attributes, base classes, the weaver (an ILPostProcessor), the trials runner, capture and telemetry, the analyzers | Git URL with a tag, or OpenUPM |
| CLI `dotnet scion` | Builds the test player, runs trials in parallel, compares, approves, trains the Judge, serves MCP | `dotnet tool install --local Scion.Cli` |
| Agent plugin `scion` | The skill, the hooks, the MCP server entry and the `scion-triage` subagent for Claude Code; an `AGENTS.md` block for other agents | `/plugin install scion@scion`, or [agent setup](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/setup/) |

### How one change flows

```text
agent edits scion/grafts/CritShake.cs
  -> dotnet scion graft check        Roslyn + weaver rules, no Unity, < 1 s
  -> dotnet scion graft build        DLL compiled against the test build
  -> dotnet scion graft inject       swapped into running copies at the next recipe boundary
  -> dotnet scion trial run --warm   recipes replayed, hash and frames compared
  -> dotnet scion trial show         verdict, report.md, window.png
  -> a person approves               dotnet scion trial approve ... (changed needs a terminal)
  -> dotnet scion graft promote      the graft moves into the game; the final build calls it directly
```

### Adoption levels

| Level | Needs | Unlocks |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Grafts** | The package | Grafts with automatic anchors, `graft check`, the project index |
| **2. Trials** | An adapter that turns a recipe into game state | Parallel recipes, captures, checks, baselines, the Judge |
| **3. Multiverse** | A deterministic rules core with a command log, registered as an `ISimulation` | Forking a match by turn, proof that visuals do not change rules, matches turned into recipes, balance specs, the rare-moment hunter |

`dotnet scion doctor` prints the current level (`adoption_level`) and what is missing for the next one
(`adoption_next`). `dotnet scion diagnose` turns that into a plan with file and line.

## Key terms

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Graft | A `static void` method marked `[Before]` or `[After]` that the weaver calls from a game method. |
| Anchor | A game method rewritten by the weaver so grafts run around it. |
| Test build | The Mono player with `SCION_SLOTS` and `SCION_TRIALS`: swappable slots, trials, virtual time. Never shipped. |
| Final build | The IL2CPP player you ship: grafts are direct calls, no trials code. |
| Recipe | A `TrialRecipe` class that describes one scene to reproduce. |
| Adapter | Your class that turns a recipe into game state and drives the capture. |
| Baseline | The approved result of a recipe, kept in git under `scion/baselines/`. |
| Verdict | `same`, `within`, `px_changed`, `changed`, `new` or `stale`: how a run compares with its baseline. |

The [glossary](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/glossary/) defines every term the docs use.

## Guarantees and limits

- Grafts change only presentation. Rules change in the game's core through `RuleModifier<T>`, so a rule never
  depends on code the weaver adds. The analyzer SCN003 enforces it.
- Nothing from the test build reaches players: the final build carries grafts as direct calls and refuses test
  defines (SCN121).
- Results are reproducible on the same machine and build: game time advances a fixed step per frame, clocks,
  screen and random sources are virtual, and particles, animators and UI Toolkit are driven by the recipe clock.
- Pixels may differ across GPUs and drivers; baselines are kept per platform, and images are compared with a
  perceptual tolerance.
- The CLI never calls an AI model. Agents read its JSON and files; evaluators that use a model run as separate
  processes or export and import files.
- Approving a result that replaces an approved one needs a person at a terminal.

## See also

- [Requirements](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/requirements/)
- [Install](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/install/)
- [Quickstart](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/quickstart/)

# Requirements

This page lists what Scion 1.0.0 needs: the Unity version, the .NET SDK for the `dotnet scion` CLI, the supported
operating systems, the Mono and IL2CPP backends for the test and final builds, and the memory, disk and git LFS that
parallel trials use. `dotnet scion doctor` checks every item here and says which one fails.

## Software

| Component | Requirement | Checked by `doctor` |
|---|---|---|
| Unity | 6000.3 or any later Unity 6 release (`"unity": "6000.3"` in the package manifest) | `unity` |
| Unity package dependency | `com.unity.nuget.mono-cecil` 1.11.4 (installed automatically) | `unity` |
| Unity modules | Mono for the test build of your target platform; IL2CPP for the final build | `build`, `defines` |
| .NET SDK | 10.0 or later, for the CLI (`Scion.Cli` targets `net10.0`) and for specs and graft DLLs | `dotnet` |
| git | 2.30 or later on the `PATH`, for approvals (`git add`), `build_stale`, `bisect` and `rule_digest` | `git` |
| git LFS | Needed when baselines keep images (`*.png` under `scion/baselines/`) | `git` |
| Optional: `com.unity.pipeline` | Lets the CLI build while the editor has the project open | `pipeline` |

Scion has no dependency on Netcode for GameObjects, URP or any render pipeline. It works with the built-in
renderer, URP and HDRP. When your game uses Netcode for GameObjects, the optional `SCION_NETCLOCK` define keeps its
tick on the recipe clock ([Netcode clock](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/netclock/)).

## Operating systems

| OS | CLI | Test and final builds | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| macOS 14 or later (Apple silicon or Intel) | yes | `osx` | Headless capture uses Metal offscreen rendering. |
| Windows 10 or 11, x64 | yes | `win` | Paths with spaces are supported; `~` means `%USERPROFILE%`. |
| Linux x64 (Ubuntu 22.04 or later) | yes | `linux` | Set `unity.editor` in `scion.local.json` when the editor is not installed by the Unity Hub. |

## Scripting backends

| Build | Backend | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Test build (`dotnet scion build test`) | Mono | Slots are swappable delegates and injection loads assemblies at run time; both need a JIT. `ScionBuild.BuildTestPlayer` forces Mono and restores your setting afterwards. |
| Final build (`dotnet scion build final`) | IL2CPP (or the project setting) | Grafts become direct static calls; nothing is registered at run time. |

A build with `SCION_SLOTS` on IL2CPP fails with [SCN120](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/builds-and-injection/#scn120).

## Project layout

- Your game code is in an assembly definition (`.asmdef`). `Scion.Runtime` is not auto-referenced, so the default
  `Assembly-CSharp` cannot see it. `dotnet scion init` adds the reference to the assemblies you name.
- At least one scene is enabled in **File > Build Profiles > Scene List**. Scion's builds use exactly those scenes.
- For level 3 features, the rules live in an assembly without engine references (`noEngineReferences: true`), so
  the CLI can run them in plain .NET.

## Machine sizing

Numbers measured on a 10-core Apple M5 with 16 GB, a tactics game with network host in each copy, headless
capture at 1280x720 and 30 fps.

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| RAM per player copy | about 0.5 to 0.7 GB (about 0.96 GB for a single copy) |
| Recipe cost inside a running copy | 0.33 to 0.50 s for a 2 s scene; a copy starts in under 1 s after the game loads |
| 120 captures (5 recipes x 24 rounds) | 27 s with 6 headless copies; 67 s with 1 copy |
| Best copy count | 4 to 6 headless copies on that machine; `doctor` suggests a number from cores and free RAM |
| Disk per round of 120 captures | about 600 MB in the run folder (raw frames are deleted unless `--frames` or `-scion-raw`) |
| Graft DLL build (`graft build`) | 0.3 to 0.6 s |
| Weaver time inside a Unity build | under 1 s |
| Graft call cost, final build | not measurable (the graft is inlined) |
| Graft call cost, test build slot | about 1 to 3 ns |

`trial run` deletes run folders beyond `trials.keep_runs` (10 by default), so disk use stays bounded. Keep
`trials.out` outside git (the default `.scion/runs` is in `.gitignore` after `dotnet scion init`).

## Judge hardware

The Judge runs on the CPU, or on the GPU through ONNX Runtime when one is available (CoreML on macOS, DirectML on
Windows, CUDA on Linux). Computing embeddings for 10,000 images takes about 5 to 10 minutes on an M5; training a head
takes seconds; judging one image takes 10 to 50 ms. Eye models take 0.4 to 1.6 GB of disk each in
`~/.scion/models/`. See [Models and licenses](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/models/).

## See also

- [Install](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/install/)
- [doctor](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/doctor/)
- [Parallel copies](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/parallel/)
- [FAQ](/scion/41664431a8f5/help/faq/)

# Install

This tutorial installs Scion 1.0.0 into a Unity project: the `me.jandson.scion` package (Git URL or OpenUPM), the
`Scion.Cli` .NET tool (`dotnet scion`), the project files that `dotnet scion init` writes (`scion.json`, folders,
`.gitignore` lines, the `.asmref` for grafts) and the integration with your AI agent. Every path ends with
`dotnet scion doctor`, which proves the setup works.

## Before you begin

- Unity 6000.3 or later, with the Mono and IL2CPP modules for your platform ([Requirements](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/requirements/)).
- The .NET 10 SDK: `dotnet --version` prints 10 or later.
- git, and git LFS if you will keep image baselines.
- The project root is a git repository. Run every command below from it.

There are three ways in, and they converge:

| Path | You do | Scion does |
|---|---|---|
| A. Claude Code | `/plugin install scion@scion`, then ask "install Scion in this project" | Runs steps 1 to 5 below, shows the `--dry-run` preview first and asks you to confirm |
| B. Codex, Cursor, Copilot or another agent | Steps 1 to 3 by hand, then step 4 for your agent | Gives your agent the MCP server and the `AGENTS.md` block |
| C. By hand or in CI | Steps 1 to 3 and 5 | Nothing else |

## Steps

### 1. Add the package

Pick one source. Both pin the version with a tag.

**Git URL.** Add this line to the `dependencies` of `Packages/manifest.json`:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "me.jandson.scion": "https://github.com/Jand-S/scion.git?path=/Packages/me.jandson.scion#v1.0.0"
  }
}
```

**OpenUPM.** With the [OpenUPM CLI](https://openupm.com/docs/getting-started-cli.html) installed:

```sh
openupm add me.jandson.scion@1.0.0
```

Unity downloads the package and its dependency `com.unity.nuget.mono-cecil`. From the next compilation on, the
weaver processes every assembly that references `Scion.Runtime`.

### 2. Install the CLI

The CLI is a local .NET tool, pinned in the repository's tool manifest so every clone and CI job uses the same
version:

```sh
dotnet new tool-manifest            # only if .config/dotnet-tools.json does not exist yet
dotnet tool install --local Scion.Cli --version 1.0.0
dotnet scion --version
```

```text
1.0.0
```

On another clone, `dotnet tool restore` installs the version the manifest names. Keep the CLI version equal to the
package version: a graft DLL built by one version is refused by a player of another
([SCN131](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/builds-and-injection/#scn131)), and `doctor` warns with `version_mismatch`.

### 3. Set up the project

`dotnet scion init` adds Scion's files without moving anything. Preview first:

```sh
dotnet scion init --existing --dry-run
```

<!-- validate: cli/init -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"init","ok":true,"dry_run":true,"created":["scion.json","scion/grafts/","scion/recipes/","scion/baselines/","Assets/Orchard/Grafts/Orchard.Grafts.asmref",".config/dotnet-tools.json"],"changed":[".gitignore",".gitattributes","Packages/manifest.json"],"skipped":["ProjectSettings/ScionSettings.json"],"adoption_level":1,"next_step":"run without --dry-run: dotnet scion init --existing"}
```

Then apply it:

```sh
dotnet scion init --existing
```

What `init` writes:

| File or folder | Content |
|---|---|
| `scion.json` | CLI configuration with defaults for your project ([Configuration](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/configuration/)) |
| `ProjectSettings/ScionSettings.json` | Weaver, build and analyzer settings; `main_assembly` set to your game assembly |
| `scion/grafts/`, `scion/recipes/`, `scion/baselines/` | Draft grafts, extra recipes and match files, approved baselines |
| `<grafts folder>/<Game>.Grafts.asmref` | Makes the promoted grafts folder compile into your game assembly |
| `.gitignore` | `.scion/` (runs, builds, caches) and `scion.local.json` |
| `.gitattributes` | `scion/baselines/**/*.png filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text` |
| Your game `.asmdef` | A reference to `Scion.Runtime` (and `Scion.Trials`, `Scion.Injection` for test-only code) |

`init` is idempotent: run it again and it reports everything as `skipped`. To start a project from a genre
template instead, see [Start a new project](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/new-project/).

### 4. Connect your agent

**Claude Code.** Install the plugin. It brings the `scion` skill, the hooks, the MCP server and the
`scion-triage` subagent:

```sh
/plugin marketplace add Jand-S/scion
/plugin install scion@scion
```

**Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot and others.** Add the MCP server to your agent's configuration and the Scion block
to `AGENTS.md`. The exact files per agent are on [Set up your agent](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/setup/). The server is the CLI
itself:

```json
{"mcpServers":{"scion":{"command":"dotnet","args":["scion","mcp"]}}}
```

### 5. Run doctor

```sh
dotnet scion doctor
```

<!-- validate: cli/doctor -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"doctor","ok":true,"level":2,"version":"1.0.0","adoption_level":1,"adoption_next":"level 2: write an adapter and a recipe (dotnet scion new trial MyFirstTrial)","checks":[{"id":"build","status":"warn","detail":"no test build at /Users/alex/orchard/.scion/builds/test/Orchard.app","hint":"run: dotnet scion build test"},{"id":"config","status":"ok","detail":"/Users/alex/orchard/scion.json"},{"id":"unity","status":"ok","detail":"6000.3.25f1"},{"id":"machine","status":"ok","detail":"10 cores, 9.1 GB free of 16.0 GB"}],"suggested_copies":4,"next_step":"run: dotnet scion build test"}
```

Exit 0 means the setup is usable; read the `hint` of each `warn`. On a fresh project, the `build` check warns until
the first `dotnet scion build test`. Exit 3 means a check failed: fix what `error.hint` says and run `doctor` again.

## Check the result

- `dotnet scion doctor` exits 0.
- `dotnet scion --version` prints `1.0.0`, and the Unity Package Manager shows Scion 1.0.0.
- `git status` shows the files from step 3, ready to commit.
- In Unity, the console has no `Scion SCNxxx` errors after the next compilation.

Commit the new files: `scion.json`, `ProjectSettings/ScionSettings.json`, `.config/dotnet-tools.json`, the
`.asmref`, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes` and `Packages/manifest.json`.

## Update and uninstall

- **Update:** change the tag in `Packages/manifest.json` (or `openupm add me.jandson.scion@<version>`), then
  `dotnet tool update --local Scion.Cli --version <version>`. Read the [changelog](/scion/41664431a8f5/help/changelog/) first.
- **Uninstall:** `dotnet scion uninstall --dry-run` lists what it would remove; `dotnet scion uninstall` removes the
  files `init` created, the package line and the tool. It keeps `scion/baselines/` and your grafts, recipes and specs
  unless you pass `--purge`. See [init, new, uninstall](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/init/).

## Next steps

- [Quickstart](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/quickstart/): a graft, a recipe and a first approved baseline in ten minutes.
- [Add Scion to an existing game](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/existing-project/): what to do on day one and how to reach level 2.
- [For AI agents](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/): the loop, the rules and the machine-readable files.

# Quickstart

This tutorial takes about ten minutes on the Orchard Tactics sample. You build the test player with
`dotnet scion build test`, run the `SlashHit` recipe with `dotnet scion trial run`, approve its first baseline,
write the `HitFlash` graft, inject it into a running copy with `graft inject`, promote it, and review the `changed`
verdict it causes. You finish with a second recipe of your own.

## Before you begin

- Scion is installed: package, CLI and `dotnet scion doctor` passing ([Install](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/install/)).
- An empty Unity 6000.3 project in a git repository, with the CLI tool manifest. The commands below create the
  Orchard sample in it:

```sh
dotnet scion new --genre tactics --name Orchard
git add -A && git commit -m "Orchard sample"
```

`new --genre tactics` writes the Orchard game skeleton (`Assets/Orchard/Core`, `Runtime`, `Grafts`, `Trials`), a
battle scene, the `OrchardAdapter`, the `SlashHit` recipe, `scion.json` and the agent block in `CLAUDE.md`
([Start a new project](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/new-project/)).

## Steps

### 1. Build the test player

```sh
dotnet scion build test
```

<!-- validate: cli/build -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"build test","ok":true,"channel":"batchmode","seconds":31.8,"log":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/builds/test/build.log","build_id":"4c49a1e0b2f3","output":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/builds/test/Orchard.app","errors":[],"next_step":"run: dotnet scion trial run"}
```

The test build is a Mono player with the `SCION_SLOTS` and `SCION_TRIALS` defines. With the editor open the CLI
builds through it when the project has `com.unity.pipeline`; otherwise close the editor first (`editor_open`).

### 2. Run the sample recipe

```sh
dotnet scion trial run SlashHit --rounds 2
```

<!-- validate: cli/trial-run -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"trial run","ok":true,"run":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/runs/20261011-143200","build_id":"4c49a1e0b2f3","copies":2,"wall_s":6.2,"runs":{"recipes":1,"rounds":2,"total":2,"ok":2,"failed":0,"changed":0,"within":0,"px_changed":0,"new":1,"stale":0},"failed":[],"changed":[],"determinism":{"hash_stable":true,"frame_jitter":[]},"next_step":"check /Users/alex/orchard/.scion/runs/20261011-143200/q0/SlashHit/r1/report.md, then: dotnet scion trial approve --new --reason \"...\""}
```

Both rounds passed and agree on the state hash (`hash_stable: true`). `new: 1` means `SlashHit` has no baseline yet.

### 3. Read the result

```sh
dotnet scion trial show SlashHit
```

The output names `report.md` and the images. Read `report.md` first: the verdict, the checks, the timeline of marks
and the probes. Open `window.png` (12 frames around the impact) only to look at the effect itself.

### 4. Approve the first baseline

```sh
dotnet scion trial approve --new --reason "first baseline of SlashHit"
git commit -m "Baseline for SlashHit"
```

`trial approve` writes `scion/baselines/SlashHit/` and stages it with `git add`; it never commits. Anyone,
including an AI agent, may approve a `new` recipe. The next run of `SlashHit` reports `same`.

### 5. Write a graft

Create a draft graft hung after `HitPresenter.Play`, the method that presents one hit:

```sh
dotnet scion graft new HitFlash --after Orchard.Presentation.HitPresenter.Play
```

Edit `scion/grafts/HitFlash.cs`:

```csharp
using Orchard.Core;
using Orchard.Presentation;
using Scion;
using UnityEngine;

namespace Orchard.Grafts
{
    public static class HitFlash
    {
        // Runs after every HitPresenter.Play, without editing HitPresenter.
        [After(typeof(HitPresenter), nameof(HitPresenter.Play))]
        public static void After(HitPresenter presenter, HitEvent e)
        {
            Fx.Flash(presenter.UnitView(e.Target), Color.white, 0.08f);
        }
    }
}
```

Check it against the build, without Unity:

```sh
dotnet scion graft check scion/grafts/HitFlash.cs
```

A typo such as `nameof(HitPresenter.Ply)` comes back as `SCN103` with `did_you_mean: ["Play"]`.

### 6. Try it live in a running copy

Start one warm copy, compile the graft against the build, inject it and replay the recipe:

```sh
dotnet scion trial serve -j 1 --window
dotnet scion graft build
dotnet scion graft inject
dotnet scion trial run SlashHit --warm
```

The copy keeps running between commands, so each edit-build-inject-run cycle takes about a second. The flash is
visual only: the state hash stays the same as the baseline.

### 7. Promote the graft

```sh
dotnet scion graft promote HitFlash
dotnet scion build test
dotnet scion trial run SlashHit
```

`graft promote` moves the file to `Assets/Orchard/Grafts/HitFlash.cs`, where it compiles into the game. The run now
compares the images with the baseline and finds the flash:

<!-- validate: cli/trial-run -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"trial run","ok":false,"run":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/runs/20261011-150410","build_id":"8d02f1c3a7b9","copies":1,"wall_s":4.1,"runs":{"recipes":1,"rounds":1,"total":1,"ok":1,"failed":0,"changed":1,"within":0,"px_changed":0,"new":0,"stale":0},"failed":[],"changed":[{"id":"SlashHit","vs_approved":"changed","hash":"same","image":"q0/SlashHit/r1/window.png","diff":"diff/SlashHit/r1/window.diff.png"}],"determinism":{"hash_stable":true,"frame_jitter":[]},"next_step":"review: dotnet scion trial show SlashHit --grid; a person approves at a terminal"}
```

Exit code 1: `SlashHit` is `changed`. The rules did not change (`hash: same`); the image did, outside the tolerance.

### 8. Review and approve the change

```sh
dotnet scion trial show SlashHit --grid
```

`--grid` writes `grid.png` with three rows: the baseline, the current frames and the difference. If the flash is
what you wanted, a person approves it at an interactive terminal:

```sh
dotnet scion trial approve SlashHit --reason "white hit flash on every hit"
```

An AI agent cannot do this step: without a terminal the CLI stops with `human_required`. That is the point: a
result a person approved is only replaced by a person.

### 9. Write a second recipe

Add `Assets/Orchard/Trials/KnightFalls.cs`:

```csharp
using Orchard.Core;
using Scion.Trials;

namespace Orchard.Trials
{
    public sealed class KnightFalls : OrchardRecipe
    {
        public KnightFalls()
        {
            Description = "Three goblins attack a knight with 4 HP; the knight falls.";
            Attacker = UnitKind.Goblin;
            Defender = UnitKind.Knight;
            Attackers = 3;
            DefenderHp = 4;
            Ability = "stab";
            Tags = new[] { "combat", "death" };
        }

        protected override void Checks(TrialChecks c) =>
            c.Order("IMPACT", "unit_down").ProbeIs("defender_hp", hp => hp == 0, "the knight ends at 0 HP");
    }
}
```

Build, run and approve it as a `new` recipe:

```sh
dotnet scion build test
dotnet scion trial run KnightFalls --rounds 2
dotnet scion trial approve --new --reason "first baseline of KnightFalls"
```

## Check the result

- `dotnet scion trial run` exits 0 and reports `same` for `SlashHit` and `KnightFalls`.
- `scion/baselines/` holds both recipes, committed.
- `Assets/Orchard/Grafts/HitFlash.cs` is in the game; `dotnet scion build final` builds the shipping player with the
  flash as a direct call.

## Next steps

- [Write a graft](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/write/): every rule of `[Before]`, `[After]`, priorities and observers.
- [Write a recipe](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/recipes/) and [Write an adapter](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/adapters/).
- [Baselines and approval](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/baselines/): verdicts and who may approve what.
- [Live injection](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/injection/): the warm-copy loop in depth.

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Start a new project

`dotnet scion new --genre <genre>` turns an empty Unity project into a Scion project that starts at adoption level 3:
assembly definitions in the Scion Standard layers, an adapter and a recipe from the genre sample, an example graft,
a rules core registered as an `ISimulation`, `scion.json`, `ProjectSettings/ScionSettings.json` and the agent block
in `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`. The scaffold commands `dotnet scion new feature|effect|graft|trial <Name>` then add
files that compile and pass `doctor` from the first build.

## When to use

- Use it for a new game, or a prototype you want testable from day one.
- Do not use it on a game with existing code: `new` writes a full layout. Use
  [`init --existing`](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/existing-project/) instead; it only adds files.

## Before you begin

- An empty Unity 6000.3 project (created by the Unity Hub) in a git repository.
- The CLI installed in that repository (`dotnet tool install --local Scion.Cli --version 1.0.0`).
- The package added to `Packages/manifest.json` (step 1 of [Install](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/install/)). `new` adds it for you
  when it is missing.

## Steps

### 1. Preview the layout

```sh
dotnet scion new --genre tactics --name Orchard --dry-run
```

<!-- validate: cli/init -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"new","ok":true,"dry_run":true,"created":["Assets/Orchard/Core/Orchard.Core.asmdef","Assets/Orchard/Runtime/Orchard.Runtime.asmdef","Assets/Orchard/Grafts/Orchard.Grafts.asmref","Assets/Orchard/Trials/Orchard.Trials.asmdef","Assets/Orchard/Trials/OrchardAdapter.cs","Assets/Orchard/Trials/SlashHit.cs",{"more":14}],"changed":["Packages/manifest.json",".gitignore"],"skipped":[],"adoption_level":3,"next_step":"run without --dry-run: dotnet scion new --genre tactics --name Orchard"}
```

### 2. Create it

```sh
dotnet scion new --genre tactics --name Orchard
dotnet scion doctor
```

`doctor` reports `adoption_level: 3` once the first test build exists.

### 3. Build and run the sample recipe

```sh
dotnet scion build test
dotnet scion trial run
dotnet scion trial approve --new --reason "first baselines of the template"
```

### 4. Grow it with scaffolds

Each scaffold writes code that compiles, follows the [Scion Standard](/scion/41664431a8f5/standard/overview/) and comes with its
test:

```sh
dotnet scion new feature Poison        # a rule in Orchard.Core: a RuleModifier, its data row and a completeness test
dotnet scion new effect PoisonTick     # a presentation effect: a named method on the presenter, which becomes an anchor
dotnet scion new graft PoisonGlow --after Orchard.Presentation.UnitView.PlayStatus
dotnet scion new trial PoisonTicks     # a recipe for the effect, with checks
```

`new graft` is the same as [`graft new`](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/graft/): the draft lands in `scion/grafts/` and comes with a
recipe stub that exercises its anchor.

## Reference

### Genres

| Genre | Sample game | Adapter | Recipes it starts with |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tactics` | Orchard Tactics: grid, turns, 1 to 4 players co-op | `OrchardAdapter : TrialAdapter<OrchardRecipe>` | `SlashHit`, `CoopTurn`, `HudStates` |
| `action` | A top-down arena with real-time combat | `ArenaAdapter : TrialAdapter<ArenaRecipe>` | `DashHit`, `WaveClear` |
| `platformer` | A side-scrolling level with a controllable character | `LevelAdapter : TrialAdapter<LevelRecipe>` | `JumpLand`, `CoinPickup` |
| `blank` | No game code; only the layout, an empty adapter and one recipe stub | `GameAdapter : TrialAdapter<GameRecipe>` | `FirstTrial` |

### Layout it creates

```text
Assets/<Name>/
  Core/          <Name>.Core.asmdef      rules: plain C#, integers, noEngineReferences; registers ISimulation
  Runtime/       <Name>.Runtime.asmdef   presentation and input; references Scion.Runtime and Core
  Grafts/        <Name>.Grafts.asmref    compiles into <Name>.Runtime; the promoted grafts
  Trials/        <Name>.Trials.asmdef    recipes and adapter; defineConstraints SCION_TRIALS
Trials/Specs/    <Name>.Specs.csproj     specs, built and run by the CLI in plain .NET
scion/grafts/    draft grafts           scion/recipes/  extra recipes and match files
scion/baselines/ approved baselines     scion.json, ProjectSettings/ScionSettings.json
CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md                     the Scion block between <!-- scion:begin --> and <!-- scion:end -->
```

Dependencies only point down: Core depends on nothing; Runtime on Core; Grafts compile into Runtime; Trials use
Runtime as a black box and Core to compare hashes. Nothing depends on Grafts. See
[The Scion Standard](/scion/41664431a8f5/standard/overview/).

### Options

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--genre <genre>` | required | One of the genres above. |
| `--name <Name>` | the Unity product name | Prefix of folders, assemblies and namespaces. |
| `--players <n>` | `4` for `tactics`, `1` otherwise | Maximum players the co-op recipes cover. |
| `--dry-run` | off | List what would be written. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `usage` | 2 | `--genre` missing, or `new` in a project that already has `Assets/<Name>/`. | Pick another `--name`, or use `init --existing`. |
| `bad_value` | 2 | Unknown genre. | Use a genre from `did_you_mean`. |
| `config_not_found` | 3 | No Unity project here (`ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt` missing). | Run it at the root of the Unity project. |
| `out_not_writable` | 3 | A target file cannot be written. | Fix permissions and run again; `new` is idempotent. |

## Examples

### A two-player platformer

```sh
dotnet scion new --genre platformer --name Hopper --players 2
dotnet scion build test && dotnet scion trial run
```

### Add a status effect end to end

```sh
dotnet scion new feature Burn
dotnet scion new effect BurnTick
dotnet scion new trial BurnTicks
dotnet scion build test && dotnet scion trial run BurnTicks
```

## See also

- [init, new, uninstall](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/init/)
- [Add Scion to an existing game](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/existing-project/)
- [The Scion Standard](/scion/41664431a8f5/standard/overview/)
- [Enforcement](/scion/41664431a8f5/standard/enforcement/)

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Add Scion to an existing game

This guide adopts Scion in a game that already exists. `dotnet scion init --existing` adds files and never moves
yours; `dotnet scion diagnose` scans your assemblies and reports the adoption level, the blockers with file and line,
and a plan. Level 1 (grafts) works the same day; level 2 costs one adapter; level 3 needs a deterministic rules core.
You prove determinism by running the same recipe twice and comparing hashes.

## When to use

- Use it when the game has code, scenes and its own folder layout that must stay as they are.
- Do not use it for a new, empty project: [`new --genre`](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/new-project/) gives you level 3 directly.

## Before you begin

- The package and the CLI are installed ([Install](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/install/), steps 1 and 2).
- Your game code is in assembly definitions. If it is all in `Assembly-CSharp`, create one `.asmdef` for the game
  code first: grafts compile into an assembly through an `.asmref`, and `Scion.Runtime` is not auto-referenced.

## Steps

### 1. Add Scion's files

```sh
dotnet scion init --existing --dry-run
dotnet scion init --existing
```

`init` asks which assembly is your game (it proposes the one with the most scripts) and writes `scion.json`,
`ProjectSettings/ScionSettings.json`, the grafts folder with its `.asmref`, the `scion/` folders and the ignore
rules. Nothing of yours moves.

### 2. Get the report

```sh
dotnet scion diagnose
```

<!-- validate: cli/diagnose -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"diagnose","ok":true,"adoption_level":1,"assemblies":["Orchard.Core","Orchard.Runtime"],"counts":{"SCN301":41,"SCN302":3,"SCN303":1,"SCN305":2},"blockers":[{"file":"Assets/Orchard/Runtime/Ai/Planner.cs","line":88,"code":"SCN305","message":"Planner.Pick depends on an unordered collection or query (Dictionary<int, Unit>)."},{"file":"Assets/Orchard/Runtime/Battle/Battlefield.cs","line":20,"code":"singleton","message":"Battlefield.Current is global state; one battle per process."}],"singletons":["Orchard.Runtime.Battlefield.Current","Orchard.Presentation.CameraRig.Instance"],"plan":["Write an adapter: dotnet scion diagnose --adapter writes a skeleton.","Sort the planner candidates by id (SCN305).","Move the battle rules to Orchard.Core with noEngineReferences for level 3."],"adapter_skeleton":null,"report":"/Users/alex/orchard/Library/Scion/diagnose.md","next_step":"write the adapter skeleton: dotnet scion diagnose --adapter"}
```

The full report is in `Library/Scion/diagnose.md`: the level, the blockers worst first, the singletons that would
block the [mosaic](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/mosaic/), large files that mix rules and presentation, and the plan.

### 3. Level 1: write a graft today

Grafts need nothing but the package. Find an anchor and hang a graft on it:

```sh
dotnet scion anchor list --search hit
dotnet scion graft new HitFlash --after Orchard.Presentation.HitPresenter.Play
```

Then follow [Write a graft](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/write/). Without an adapter you verify grafts in the editor or a build;
with one (level 2) you verify them in recipes.

### 4. Level 2: write the adapter

```sh
dotnet scion diagnose --adapter
```

writes `Assets/<Game>/Trials/<Game>Adapter.cs`, a `TrialAdapter<TRecipe>` skeleton with a recipe base class and one
recipe. The real cost of an adapter is knowing three things about your game:

1. **When the scene is ready.** `Prepare` waits for the loaded level; `Run` waits for the setup to settle.
2. **How to reset global state.** `Teardown`, and a `TrialSession.Boundary` handler for statics.
3. **Every random source.** `UnityEngine.Random` and `new System.Random()` are seeded by Scion; any other generator
   (a custom PRNG, a seeded service) must take `TrialSession.RunSeed` or the recipe `Seed`.

A one-scene game without networking needs 30 to 50 lines; a networked tactics game about 300. See
[Write an adapter](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/adapters/).

### 5. Prove determinism

Run the same recipe several times, in one copy and across copies:

```sh
dotnet scion trial run SlashHit --rounds 4 --check
```

`determinism.hash_stable: true` means every round gave the same state hash. When it is `false`, `determinism.tsv`
names the first frame and the first column that differs (`state`, `tick`, `rng`, `unscaled`, `time`, `px`,
`frames`). See [Verify determinism](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/verify/).

### 6. Level 3: register the simulation

Level 3 needs the rules in an assembly without engine references and a command log. Implement
`Scion.Core.ISimulation` over your rules and register it:

```csharp
[assembly: Scion.Core.Simulation(typeof(Orchard.Core.OrchardSimulation))]
```

`doctor` then reports `adoption_level: 3`, and the multiverse, balance specs, metamorphic tests and the rare-moment
hunter work. See [Core API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/core/).

## Reference

| Level | Proof | Time for a typical game |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Grafts | `graft check` passes and a graft fires in the editor | The same day |
| 2. Trials | A recipe passes 4 rounds with `hash_stable: true` | 1 to 3 sessions (the adapter) |
| 3. Multiverse | `doctor` reports level 3; a captured match replays to the same hash in plain .NET | Depends on how separate rules and presentation already are |

`init --existing` options: `--dry-run`, `--game-assembly <name>` (skip the question), `--grafts-folder <path>`
(default `Assets/<Game>/Grafts`). `diagnose` options: `--adapter` (write the skeleton), `--assembly <name>` (repeat
to scan only some). See [init](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/init/) and [diagnose](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/diagnose/).

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `usage` | 2 | `init` without `--existing` in a project that has scripts. | Add `--existing`. |
| `config_invalid` | 3 | An existing `scion.json` has a bad key. | Fix the key named in the message; `init` never overwrites it. |
| `no_simulation` | 3 | A level 3 command found no `[assembly: Simulation]`. | Register an `ISimulation` (step 6). |
| `SCN202`, `SCN203` | 3 | The adapter is not valid, or two adapters handle the same recipe type. | See [Trials diagnostics](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/trials/). |

## Examples

### Graft-only adoption

A team that only wants grafts stops after step 3. `scion.json` still exists, so `graft check` and the hooks work;
`doctor` reports level 1 with `adoption_next` naming the adapter.

### Find the first non-deterministic system

```sh
dotnet scion trial run KnightFalls --rounds 6 --check --jitter 20
```

`--jitter 20` sleeps up to 20 ms of real time per frame from the second round on, so code that follows the wall clock
shows up as a `diff` line in `determinism.tsv`.

## See also

- [diagnose](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/diagnose/)
- [Find non-determinism](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/diagnose/)
- [Write an adapter](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/adapters/)
- [The Scion Standard](/scion/41664431a8f5/standard/overview/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# For AI agents

This is the start page for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot and others) that work on a
game with Scion. It gives the loop (`graft check`, `graft inject`, `trial run`, `trial show`, `trial approve --new`),
the rules every agent must follow, the reading order that keeps token use low, and the machine-readable files:
`llms.txt`, the Markdown twin of every page, the JSON Schemas and the docs inside the installed package.

## When to use

- Read this page before your first Scion command in a project, and whenever a command's result surprises you.
- For one exit code or error code, go straight to [What to do next](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/next-action/).

## Rules

These rules are also at the top of [/scion/llms.txt](/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt). Follow them in every session:

- Run `dotnet scion doctor` first. Exit 0 means usable; exit 3 means fix what `error.hint` says.
- Every command prints one JSON object on stdout (`schema_version`, `ok`, `next_step`, `error` on exits 2 and 3). Parse it; do not scrape text. Follow `next_step`.
- Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 a check failed, 2 usage error (see `did_you_mean`), 3 environment. Next actions: `https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/next-action.md`
- You may approve only `new` baselines (`trial approve --new --reason "..."`). Never approve `changed`, `stale` or `px_changed`, and never edit `scion/baselines/` by hand: ask a person.
- Read `report.md` only for failed or changed recipes; open images only when pixels changed or the task is visual.

Two more that follow from the design:

- Grafts are visual only. A change to damage, range, turn order or any other rule goes into the game's core as a
  `RuleModifier<T>`, never into a graft ([Grafts are visual only](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/visual-only/)).
- Never fake a terminal (`script`, `expect`, a pseudo-TTY) to get past `human_required`. Tell the person what changed
  and give them the command from `next_step`.

## Steps

### 1. Orient yourself

```sh
dotnet scion doctor
dotnet scion index
```

`index` prints the project index (under 2 KB): Scion version, adoption level, graft folders, anchor categories,
recipe names and the commands. With the Claude Code plugin it arrives on its own at session start.

### 2. Find where to hang the change

```sh
dotnet scion anchor list --search hit
dotnet scion anchor show presentation.hit
```

`anchor show` returns the signature and a ready graft declaration (`example`). Never guess a signature.

### 3. Write and check the graft

```sh
dotnet scion graft new CritShake --after Orchard.Presentation.HitPresenter.Play
dotnet scion graft check scion/grafts/CritShake.cs
```

Apply every `hint` and `did_you_mean` until `graft check` exits 0. With the plugin, the `PostToolUse` hook runs the
check after each edit and returns the errors to you.

### 4. Try it in the real build

```sh
dotnet scion trial serve -j 2
dotnet scion graft build && dotnet scion graft inject
dotnet scion trial run SlashHit KnightFalls --warm
```

Warm runs compare state hashes and frame counts. For images, run a cold run with the graft:
`dotnet scion trial run SlashHit --grafts <dll from graft build>`.

### 5. Read the results

Follow [Reading results](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/reading-results/): the JSON, then `report.md` of failed or changed recipes,
then images only when pixels changed or the task is visual.

### 6. Hand over

- New recipes: `dotnet scion trial approve --new --reason "..."`, then commit the staged baselines.
- Changed recipes: stop and report. Give the person `trial show --changed` output, the reason and the exact approve
  command from `next_step`.
- Promote a graft only when the person agrees: `dotnet scion graft promote CritShake`.

## Reference

### Machine-readable files

| File | URL | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Page index | [/scion/llms.txt](/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt) | Every page as a link to its Markdown, with one line each; the rules first |
| Full docs | [/scion/llms-full.txt](/scion/41664431a8f5/llms-full.txt) | Every page in one file, in sidebar order |
| Section files | `/scion/<section>/llms-full.txt` | One section in one file, for example [/scion/grafts/llms-full.txt](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/llms-full.txt) |
| Markdown twin | `<page URL>.md` or `<page URL>/index.md` | The page as Markdown with frontmatter (`title`, `type`, `url`, `related`) |
| JSON Schemas | [JSON Schemas](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/schemas/) | Every file format and every CLI output, draft 2020-12 |

### Version-matched local docs

The installed package carries the Markdown of its own version. Prefer it over the website when the project may not
run the latest version:

```text
Packages/me.jandson.scion/Documentation~/site/src/content/docs/                        embedded or local package
Library/PackageCache/me.jandson.scion@<hash>/Documentation~/site/src/content/docs/    Git URL or OpenUPM package
```

`dotnet scion mcp` serves the same files through its `docs_search` and `docs_read` tools.

### Token budget

| Read | Cost |
|---|---|
| A command's JSON | under 1.5 KB, always |
| `report.md` of one recipe | about 1,200 tokens |
| `window.png` (12 frames) | about 1,000 tokens |
| `context.png` (6 frames) | about 1,900 tokens |
| 120 captures opened blindly | about 1 million tokens: never do this |

With more than about 5 images to look at, hand them to the `scion-triage` subagent, which returns one line per
recipe ([The Scion skill](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/skill/)).

## Errors

| Signal | Next action |
|---|---|
| Exit 1, `failed[]` | Read `failed[].report`, fix, run again. |
| Exit 1, `changed[]` | Explain the change with `trial show --changed`; ask a person to approve or fix it. |
| Exit 2 | Fix the call with `error.hint` and `did_you_mean`; never retry unchanged. |
| Exit 3 | Fix the environment with `error.hint`; `doctor` names the failing check. |

Every signal, with its exact next action: [What to do next](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/next-action/).

## Examples

### A complete session

```sh
dotnet scion doctor
dotnet scion anchor list --search shake
dotnet scion graft new CritShake --after Orchard.Presentation.HitPresenter.Play
dotnet scion graft check scion/grafts/CritShake.cs
dotnet scion build test
dotnet scion trial run --grafts .scion/grafts/ScionGrafts_51c2.dll
dotnet scion trial show --changed
```

The run reports `SlashHit` as `changed` with `hash: same`: only pixels moved. The agent reports to the person:
"CritShake adds a 0.3 shake on critical hits; SlashHit changed in pixels only (window.png). To accept, promote the
graft, rebuild, run and approve at your terminal: `dotnet scion trial approve SlashHit --reason "crit shake"`."

## See also

- [Set up your agent](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/setup/)
- [What to do next](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/next-action/)
- [Reading results](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/reading-results/)
- [MCP server](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/mcp/)

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Set up your agent

This guide connects an AI coding agent to Scion. Claude Code gets everything from the `scion` plugin (skill, hooks,
MCP server, `scion-triage` subagent). Codex, Cursor and GitHub Copilot get the `dotnet scion mcp` server in their MCP
configuration and the Scion block in `AGENTS.md`. Any other agent reads `/scion/llms.txt`, uses GitMCP or Context7, or
calls the CLI directly. `dotnet scion init --agent <name>` writes the files for you.

## When to use

- Use it once per project and agent, after [Install](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/install/).
- Agents that only run shell commands need nothing more than the CLI and the `AGENTS.md` block; MCP is optional.

## Before you begin

- `dotnet scion doctor` passes in the project.
- Run the commands below from the project root.

## Steps

### Claude Code

Install the plugin from the Scion marketplace:

```sh
/plugin marketplace add Jand-S/scion
/plugin install scion@scion
```

The plugin brings the [skill](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/skill/), the four [hooks](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/hooks/), the
[MCP server](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/mcp/) and the `scion-triage` subagent. It does not edit your repository. Optionally, keep
the project index in `CLAUDE.md` too:

```sh
dotnet scion index --write CLAUDE.md
```

If the project uses `AGENTS.md`, make `CLAUDE.md` import it with a line `@AGENTS.md`, and write the block there
instead.

### Codex

```sh
dotnet scion init --agent codex
```

writes the Scion block into `AGENTS.md` and prints the MCP entry to add to `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.scion]
command = "dotnet"
args = ["scion", "mcp"]
```

Codex reads `AGENTS.md` at the start of every task, and the MCP server gives it one tool per command.

### Cursor

```sh
dotnet scion init --agent cursor
```

writes `AGENTS.md` and `.cursor/mcp.json`:

```json
{"mcpServers":{"scion":{"command":"dotnet","args":["scion","mcp"]}}}
```

### GitHub Copilot

```sh
dotnet scion init --agent copilot
```

writes `AGENTS.md` and `.vscode/mcp.json` for agent mode in VS Code:

```json
{"servers":{"scion":{"type":"stdio","command":"dotnet","args":["scion","mcp"]}}}
```

### Any other agent

- Give it the shell: every command prints one JSON object, and the [rules](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/) cover the rest.
- Point it at [/scion/llms.txt](/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt), or at the version-matched Markdown inside the package
  (`Library/PackageCache/me.jandson.scion@<hash>/Documentation~/site/src/content/docs/`).
- For agents that speak MCP but cannot run local tools, use GitMCP: add the remote server
  `https://jand-s.gitmcp.io/scion`, which reads `llms.txt` and serves the docs.
- Context7 indexes the Scion repository; ask for `me.jandson.scion` docs by name.

## Reference

### The AGENTS.md block

`init --agent` and `index --write AGENTS.md` keep this block between markers, regenerated on each run. Text outside
the markers is yours.

```md
<!-- scion:begin -->
## Scion

This project uses Scion 1.0.0 (adoption level 3). Docs: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt
- Run `dotnet scion doctor` first. Every command prints one JSON object; follow `next_step`.
- New presentation code goes in grafts (`scion/grafts/*.cs`, `[Before]`/`[After]`); rules change in Orchard.Core with `RuleModifier<T>`.
- Find anchors with `dotnet scion anchor list --search <word>`; check grafts with `dotnet scion graft check <file>`.
- Run recipes with `dotnet scion trial run`; read `report.md` of failed or changed recipes only.
- Approve only `new` baselines (`dotnet scion trial approve --new --reason "..."`); never edit `scion/baselines/`.
<!-- scion:end -->
```

### Files per agent

| Agent | Instructions | MCP configuration | Written by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | plugin skill; optional `CLAUDE.md` block | plugin | `/plugin install scion@scion` |
| Codex | `AGENTS.md` | `~/.codex/config.toml` (printed, not written) | `init --agent codex` |
| Cursor | `AGENTS.md` | `.cursor/mcp.json` | `init --agent cursor` |
| GitHub Copilot | `AGENTS.md` | `.vscode/mcp.json` | `init --agent copilot` |

### Scoped rules for Claude Code

The plugin also installs path-scoped rules that load only when the agent touches matching files. You can add your
own in `.claude/rules/` with a `paths:` frontmatter:

```md
---
paths:
  - "Assets/Orchard/Grafts/**"
  - "scion/grafts/**"
---
Grafts here are visual only. Use the Fx facade (Fx.Shake, Fx.Flash, Fx.Sound) instead of calling CameraRig or
AudioHub directly, so trials record every effect.
```

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bad_value` | 2 | Unknown agent name in `--agent`. | Use `claude`, `codex`, `cursor` or `copilot`. |
| `out_not_writable` | 3 | `AGENTS.md` or the MCP file cannot be written. | Fix permissions; the command is idempotent. |
| `version_mismatch` (warning) | 0 | The plugin, the CLI and the package are not the same version. | Update the one `doctor` names. |

## Examples

### Two agents on one project

```sh
dotnet scion init --agent codex --agent cursor
git add AGENTS.md .cursor/mcp.json && git commit -m "Scion agent setup"
```

Both agents read the same `AGENTS.md` block; each has its own MCP file.

# The Scion skill

The Claude Code plugin ships one skill, `scion`, one subagent, `scion-triage`, and path-scoped rules. This page lists
what each contains and when it loads, so you can predict what the agent knows. Other agents get the same content from
`AGENTS.md` and the MCP `docs_read` tool.

## The scion skill

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Name | `scion` |
| Loads when | The task mentions Scion, the test build, trials, recipes, baselines, grafts, anchors, visual regression, a state hash or frame count that changed, or checking a gameplay change in the real build |
| Files | `SKILL.md` (the loop and the rules, about 120 lines) and `reference/cli.md` (every command, option, output field and code) |
| Version | Same as the plugin; the plugin and the CLI must match the package version |

What `SKILL.md` covers, in order:

1. What Scion is in four lines (grafts, trials, baselines, the CLI).
2. Setup once per clone: `dotnet tool restore`, `dotnet scion doctor`.
3. The loop: edit, `graft check`, `build test` or `graft inject`, `trial run`, read the JSON, `trial show`, approve.
4. The fields of the `trial run` JSON and the verdicts.
5. The approval rules: agents approve only `new`; `changed`, `stale` and `px_changed` need a person.
6. The live loop with warm copies (`trial serve`, `graft inject`, `trial run --warm`).
7. Exit codes and the common error codes with their fix.
8. Reading order and the image budget.

The skill is facts and commands, not a long tutorial: every detail it does not hold is one `docs_read` call away.

## The scion-triage subagent

`scion-triage` reads images so the main agent does not have to. Use it when more than about 5 images need a look.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Input | A run folder and a list of recipe ids (usually `changed[]` of a `trial run`) |
| Reads | `compare.json`, each recipe's `report.md`, then `window.png` or `grid.png` |
| Returns | One line per recipe: id, verdict, what changed in the frames, whether it looks intended, and the file it looked at |
| Never does | Approve, edit files or run commands other than `trial show` |

Example return:

```text
SlashHit      changed   white flash on the goblin, frames 12-14; looks intended (HitFlash)   diff/SlashHit/r1/grid.png
FireballArea  within    no visible change                                                     q1/FireballArea/r1/window.png
KnightFalls   changed   knight falls one frame later; hash same; check HitStop                diff/KnightFalls/r1/grid.png
```

## Scoped rules

The plugin installs rules in its own folder that load only when the agent reads or edits matching paths:

| Rule | Paths | Says |
|---|---|---|
| `grafts` | `**/Grafts/**`, `scion/grafts/**` | Grafts are visual; use `Fx`; run `graft check`; no rule state |
| `recipes` | `**/Trials/**`, `scion/recipes/**` | Recipes are data; set properties in the constructor; seed every RNG |
| `baselines` | `scion/baselines/**` | Never edit; only `trial approve` writes here |
| `core` | the folders of `rule_paths` | Integers only, no `float` (SCN004); changes go through `RuleModifier<T>` |

Projects add their own in `.claude/rules/*.md` with a `paths:` frontmatter ([Set up your agent](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/setup/)).

## Keeping it current

- `dotnet scion doctor` warns `version_mismatch` when the plugin, the CLI and the package differ.
- `/plugin update scion` updates the plugin; the CLI and the package update as in [Install](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/install/).
- For agents without the plugin, `dotnet scion index --write AGENTS.md` refreshes the `AGENTS.md` block.

## See also

- [Set up your agent](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/setup/)
- [Hooks](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/hooks/)
- [Reading results](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/reading-results/)
- [MCP server](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/mcp/)

# Hooks

The Scion plugin registers four Claude Code hooks: `SessionStart` runs `dotnet scion index --hook`, `PostToolUse` on
`Edit|Write` runs `dotnet scion graft check --hook`, `PreToolUse` on `Bash` runs `dotnet scion guard --approve --hook`
and `PreToolUse` on `Edit|Write` runs `dotnet scion guard --hook`. This page gives their configuration, their input and
output, and their failure rules. Each hook finishes in under a second and does nothing outside a Scion project.

## Configuration

The plugin installs this configuration. Without the plugin, put the same block in `.claude/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "SessionStart": [
      { "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "dotnet scion index --hook", "timeout": 5 }] }
    ],
    "PostToolUse": [
      { "matcher": "Edit|Write", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "dotnet scion graft check --hook", "timeout": 5 }] }
    ],
    "PreToolUse": [
      { "matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "dotnet scion guard --approve --hook", "timeout": 5 }] },
      { "matcher": "Edit|Write", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "dotnet scion guard --hook", "timeout": 5 }] }
    ]
  }
}
```

Each hook reads the event JSON that Claude Code writes on stdin and prints the hook JSON that Claude Code expects on
stdout. Outside a Scion project (no `scion.json` above the working folder), each one exits 0 and prints nothing.

## SessionStart: index

`dotnet scion index --hook` injects the project index as context, written as facts, under 2 KB:

```json
{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","additionalContext":"This project uses Scion 1.0.0 (adoption level 3). Grafts: Assets/Orchard/Grafts (promoted), scion/grafts (drafts). Anchor categories: presentation (14), hud (9), camera (3). Recipes: SlashHit, FireballArea, KnightFalls, CoopTurn (4 players), HudStates, UnitGallery. Commands: dotnet scion anchor list|show, graft new|check|build|inject, trial run|show|approve. Approve only new baselines."}}
```

The index lists categories and counts, not every anchor: the agent asks `anchor list` for details. See
[Project index and manifest](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/project-index/).

## PostToolUse: graft check

After an `Edit` or `Write`, `dotnet scion graft check --hook` checks the edited file when it is under
`grafts.promoted` or `grafts.staging`, and ignores every other file. Errors return to the agent as context, with
the fix:

```json
{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PostToolUse","additionalContext":"Scion graft check: scion/grafts/CritShake.cs(7,6): SCN103 HitPresenter.Ply does not exist. Hint: Did you mean 'Play'?"}}
```

A file without problems produces no output. The check reads the test build's DLLs with Mono.Cecil and compiles the
file with Roslyn; it does not start Unity.

## PreToolUse Bash: approval guard

Before a `Bash` call, `dotnet scion guard --approve --hook` looks for `scion trial approve` in the command. Any other
command passes untouched. For an approval it runs the approve as `--dry-run` and decides:

| The approval would replace | Decision | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Only `new` recipes | allow | The command runs. |
| Any `changed`, `stale` or `px_changed` recipe | ask | Claude Code asks the person, showing the reason. |
| A run made with `--grafts`, or a refused recipe | deny | The command does not run; the reason says why. |

```json
{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"This approves SlashHit (changed: image) and replaces a baseline a person approved. Review: dotnet scion trial show SlashHit --grid"}}
```

The CLI itself also refuses such approvals without a terminal (`human_required`); the guard explains it before the
command runs.

## PreToolUse Edit and Write: baseline guard

`dotnet scion guard --hook` denies any `Edit` or `Write` to a file under `trials.baselines` (`scion/baselines/**`),
`scion.manifest.json` or `GRAFTS.md`, and explains the right command:

```json
{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"scion/baselines/ is written only by dotnet scion trial approve. GRAFTS.md and scion.manifest.json are generated: edit the [Anchor] in the .cs file and run dotnet scion gen."}}
```

## Failure rules

| Hook | Time limit | When the CLI fails or times out |
|---|---|---|
| index | under 1 s (5 s timeout) | Fails open: no context, the session starts normally |
| graft check | under 1 s for one file | Fails open: no output |
| approval guard | under 1 s | Fails open: the CLI still refuses with `human_required` |
| baseline guard | under 100 ms (no build access) | Fails closed: an edit under `scion/baselines/` is denied |

Run any hook by hand to see what it does: `echo '{"tool_name":"Write","tool_input":{"file_path":"scion/baselines/SlashHit/baseline.json"}}' | dotnet scion guard --hook`.

## See also

- [index, guard](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/index-and-guard/)
- [graft](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/graft/)
- [Baselines and approval](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/baselines/)
- [Set up your agent](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/setup/)

# MCP server

`dotnet scion mcp` is a Model Context Protocol server over stdio, built into the CLI. It exposes one tool per CLI
command (`scion_trial_run`, `scion_graft_check` and so on) that returns the same JSON envelope as the command, plus
`docs_search` and `docs_read` over the Markdown docs of the installed package version. For agents that cannot run
local processes, GitMCP serves the website docs at `https://jand-s.gitmcp.io/scion`.

## Configuration

The server runs from the project root, like every command, and needs nothing else. Per client:

**Claude Code** (the plugin registers it; by hand):

```sh
claude mcp add scion -- dotnet scion mcp
```

**Codex** (`~/.codex/config.toml`):

```toml
[mcp_servers.scion]
command = "dotnet"
args = ["scion", "mcp"]
```

**Cursor** (`.cursor/mcp.json`) and any client that uses the `mcpServers` shape:

```json
{"mcpServers":{"scion":{"command":"dotnet","args":["scion","mcp"]}}}
```

**VS Code with GitHub Copilot** (`.vscode/mcp.json`):

```json
{"servers":{"scion":{"type":"stdio","command":"dotnet","args":["scion","mcp"]}}}
```

## Tools

Every command tool takes the command's options as a JSON object (snake_case names, positional arguments as
`patterns` or `ids`) and returns the command's envelope as structured content and as text. The exit code is in
`exit_code`. Tool descriptions repeat the first line of the command's help.

| Tool | Command | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `scion_doctor` | `doctor` | |
| `scion_build_test`, `scion_build_final` | `build test`, `build final` | Long: progress goes to MCP progress notifications |
| `scion_trial_list` | `trial list` | |
| `scion_trial_run` | `trial run` | Progress notifications per finished pair |
| `scion_trial_show` | `trial show` | |
| `scion_trial_approve` | `trial approve` | No terminal: only `new` recipes can be approved (`human_required` otherwise) |
| `scion_trial_serve` | `trial serve` | |
| `scion_trial_diff` | `trial diff` | |
| `scion_trial_eval` | `trial eval` | `export` and `import` modes for agent evaluators |
| `scion_anchor_list`, `scion_anchor_show` | `anchor list`, `anchor show` | |
| `scion_graft_new`, `scion_graft_check`, `scion_graft_build`, `scion_graft_inject`, `scion_graft_restore`, `scion_graft_disable`, `scion_graft_promote` | `graft ...` | |
| `scion_bisect` | `bisect` | Long |
| `scion_diagnose` | `diagnose` | |
| `scion_index`, `scion_gen` | `index`, `gen` | |
| `scion_judge_list`, `scion_judge_show`, `scion_judge_train`, `scion_judge_run` | `judge ...` | `judge vote` is for people and has no tool |
| `scion_multiverse_run`, `scion_multiverse_show` | `multiverse ...` | |
| `scion_hunt_run`, `scion_search_run` | `hunt run`, `search run` | Long |

Commands that need a person or never end have no tool: `trial loop`, `graft watch`, `judge vote`, `uninstall`.

Example call and result:

```json
{"name":"scion_trial_run","arguments":{"patterns":["SlashHit"],"rounds":2}}
```

```json
{"structuredContent":{"schema_version":1,"command":"trial run","ok":true,"exit_code":0,"run":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/runs/20261011-143200","copies":2,"runs":{"recipes":1,"rounds":2,"total":2,"ok":2,"failed":0,"changed":0,"within":0,"px_changed":0,"new":0,"stale":0},"failed":[],"changed":[],"determinism":{"hash_stable":true,"frame_jitter":[]},"next_step":"nothing changed"},"isError":false}
```

`isError` is true for exit codes 2 and 3; exit code 1 is a normal result with `ok: false`.

## Docs tools

| Tool | Arguments | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `docs_search` | `query` (text), `limit` (default 8) | `[{title, path, url, snippet}]`, best first, from the docs of the installed package version |
| `docs_read` | `path` (a page id such as `grafts/anchors`, or a URL of this site) | The page as Markdown, with its frontmatter |

The docs come from `Documentation~/site/src/content/docs/` inside the package, so they always match the version the
project runs. `docs_read` with an anchor (`grafts/anchors#automatic-anchors`) returns only that section.

## GitMCP

GitMCP turns the public site into a remote MCP server with no setup: `https://jand-s.gitmcp.io/scion`. It reads
`/scion/llms.txt` first and serves pages on request. Use it when the agent runs in the cloud and cannot start
`dotnet scion mcp`; it documents the latest release, not necessarily the version installed in your project.

## Limits

- One server per project and agent session; it runs commands one at a time and queues the rest.
- Long commands report MCP progress; a client that cancels a call stops the command as Ctrl-C would.
- The server never calls an AI model and never approves anything a terminal rule protects.

## See also

- [mcp](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/mcp/)
- [Set up your agent](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/setup/)
- [For AI agents](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/)

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# What to do next

Look up the exit code and the signal a Scion command returned, and do the action in the last column. The signals are
the envelope fields (`error.code`, `warnings[].code`, `failed[]`, `changed[]`, `vs_approved`, `determinism`), the
`SCNxxx` ids of diagnostics and the control-protocol errors. Every code links to its full entry in
[Error and warning codes](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/). When two rows apply, handle the higher exit code first.

## Exit 0

| Signal | Meaning | Next action |
|---|---|---|
| `warnings` empty | Done. | Follow `next_step`. |
| `vs_approved: same` | Hash, frames and images match the baseline. | Nothing to do. |
| `vs_approved: new` | The recipe has no baseline yet. | Read its `report.md`; if it shows what the recipe should, `dotnet scion trial approve --new --reason "..."` and commit the staged files. |
| `vs_approved: within` | Pixels differ, inside the recipe's tolerance. | Nothing to approve. Mention it if the task was visual. |
| `vs_approved: px_changed` | Pixel hashes changed for a recipe that keeps no images. Informative. | Open `window.png` only if the task is visual; if intended, a person may approve it. |
| `vs_approved: stale` | The baseline was approved on another platform, Unity version, fps or player arguments; images were not compared. | Tell the person; a person approves on this platform when the result looks right. |
| warning [`build_stale`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#build_stale) | Sources or rule files changed after the build. | `dotnet scion build test`, then run again before trusting the result. |
| warning [`build_info_missing`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#build_info_missing) | No `scion-build.json` next to the build. | `dotnet scion build test`. |
| warning [`frame_jitter`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#frame_jitter) | A frame count is one off its baseline (allowed). | Nothing; if it repeats, see [Verify determinism](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/verify/). |
| warning [`px_unstable`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#px_unstable) | Pixels vary between rounds of this run. | Treat `px_changed` as noise; see [Particles, animators, UI and physics](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/control/). |
| warning [`low_memory`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#low_memory) | Fewer copies fit in free RAM than requested. | Use `suggested_copies` from `doctor` for `-j`. |
| warning [`version_mismatch`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#version_mismatch) | CLI, package and plugin versions differ. | Update the one the message names. |
| warning [`recycle`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#recycle) | A warm copy loaded 50 graft DLLs. | `dotnet scion trial serve --stop`, then `trial serve` again. |
| other warnings | Something did not stop the command. | Read its entry in [Error and warning codes](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#warnings). |

## Exit 1

| Signal | Meaning | Next action |
|---|---|---|
| `failed[]` | A (recipe, round) failed: timeout, `Fail`, a check, a logged error, a graft that threw. | Read `failed[].report`; fix the cause; run again. |
| `vs_approved: changed` | Hash, frames (off by more than one), images outside tolerance or the rule digest changed. | If intended: explain it with `trial show --changed` (and `--grid`) and ask a person to approve. If not: fix the code. |
| `determinism.hash_stable: false` | Rounds of one recipe disagree, or no round passed. | Check `failed[]` first. Then `dotnet scion trial run <Id> --rounds 4 --check`; read `determinism.tsv`; see [Verify determinism](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/verify/). |
| [`refused`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#refused) in `trial approve` | A selected recipe has a failed round, an unstable hash or was run with `--grafts`. Nothing was written. | Fix that recipe; `next_step` gives the command that approves the others. |
| `diagnostics[]` in `graft check` or `graft build` | Graft errors with SCN ids. | Apply each `hint` and `did_you_mean`; check again. |
| `errors[]` in `build test` | Compiler (`CSxxxx`) or Scion (`SCNxxx`) errors. | Fix the file and line; build again. |
| `spec.ok: false` in `trial run --spec` | An expectation of the spec failed. | Read `spec.json`; never edit the spec to make it pass. |

## Exit 2

| Signal | Meaning | Next action |
|---|---|---|
| [`usage`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#usage), [`unknown_command`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#unknown_command), [`unknown_option`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#unknown_option), [`bad_value`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#bad_value) | Wrong call. | Use `did_you_mean` and `error.hint`, or `<command> --help`. Never retry unchanged. |
| [`no_match`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#no_match) | No recipe, run or anchor with that name. | `dotnet scion trial list` (or `anchor list`); use `did_you_mean`. |
| [`human_required`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#human_required) | The approval replaces a baseline a person approved, and there is no terminal. | Stop. Tell the person what changed and the exact command from `next_step`. Never fake a terminal. |
| [`not_supported`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#not_supported) | The build lacks the define the command needs (control op without `SCION_SLOTS` or `SCION_TRIALS`). | `dotnet scion build test`. |
| [`missing_out`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#missing_out), [`unknown_flag`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#unknown_flag) | A player started by hand got a bad command line. | Fix the `-scion-*` flags; see [Player command line](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/player-flags/). |

## Exit 3

| Signal | Meaning | Next action |
|---|---|---|
| [`config_not_found`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#config_not_found) | No `scion.json` above the current folder. | `cd` into the project, or `dotnet scion init`. |
| [`config_invalid`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#config_invalid) | A bad key, type or JSON line. | Fix the key the message names; validate with [`scion-config.schema.json`](/scion/41664431a8f5/schemas/v1/scion-config.schema.json). |
| [`build_not_found`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#build_not_found), [`build_wrong_mode`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#build_wrong_mode) | No usable test build. | `dotnet scion build test`. |
| [`unity_not_found`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#unity_not_found) | The project's Unity version is not installed. | Install it, or set `unity.editor` in `scion.local.json`. |
| [`editor_open`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#editor_open) | The editor holds the project and has no `com.unity.pipeline`. | Close the editor, or add `com.unity.pipeline` to the project. |
| [`unity_failed`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#unity_failed) | Unity ended without building and without a compiler error. | Read the log named in the message. |
| [`player_crashed`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#player_crashed), [`copy_timeout`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#copy_timeout), [`watchdog`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#watchdog) | A copy died or stalled. | Read `q<i>/player.log`; rebuild if the build is old; raise `--timeout` only for slow recipes. |
| [`no_adapter`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#no_adapter), [`prepare_failed`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#prepare_failed) | No valid adapter, or an adapter's `Prepare` failed. | Read `error.message` (it names SCN202 or SCN203 when relevant) and the player log. |
| [`capture_broken`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#capture_broken) | Frame capture failed. | Read the player log; run once with `--window` to compare. |
| [`out_not_writable`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#out_not_writable), [`no_free_port`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#no_free_port) | The machine blocks the run. | Fix permissions or `trials.out`; close programs that hold ports, or use fewer copies. |
| [`shard_ignored`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#shard_ignored) | The build predates sharding. | `dotnet scion build test`. |
| [`no_copies`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#no_copies) | `graft inject`, `--warm` or `trial loop` found no warm copy. | `dotnet scion trial serve -j 2`. |
| [`no_simulation`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#no_simulation), [`not_forkable`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#not_forkable) | A level 3 command without an `ISimulation`. | Register one; see [Add Scion to an existing game](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/existing-project/). |
| [`mosaic_unsupported`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#mosaic_unsupported) | `--mosaic` with an adapter that is not an `IMosaicAdapter`. | Run without `--mosaic`, or see [Mosaic](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/mosaic/). |
| [`model_missing`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#model_missing) | A Judge eye model is not downloaded and the machine is offline. | Connect once, or copy the model into `~/.scion/models/`. |
| [`SCN130`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/builds-and-injection/#scn130) | The graft DLL was built for another build. | `dotnet scion graft build`, then inject again. |
| [`SCN131`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/builds-and-injection/#scn131) | The graft DLL or the build has another Scion ABI. | Use the same Scion version for the CLI and the build. |
| [`SCN202`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/trials/#scn202), [`SCN203`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/trials/#scn203) | Invalid adapter, or two adapters for one recipe type. | Fix the adapter as the hint says. |
| [`interrupted`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#interrupted) | Ctrl-C stopped the command. | Run it again. |
| [`internal_error`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#internal_error) | A bug in Scion. | Report it with the stack trace; do not loop. |

## Exit 125

| Signal | Meaning | Next action |
|---|---|---|
| A `bisect` step | The step cannot be judged: the build, the recipe or its rounds broke at that commit. | Nothing: `bisect` skips the commit and goes on. |

## Control protocol

| Signal | Meaning | Next action |
|---|---|---|
| [`busy`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#busy) | A queue is already running in that copy. | Wait for it, or send `quit`. |
| [`bad_token`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#bad_token) | Wrong or stale token. | Re-read `control.json` of that copy. |
| [`not_supported`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#not_supported) | The copy lacks `SCION_SLOTS` or `SCION_TRIALS`. | Rebuild with `dotnet scion build test`. |
| [`bad_json`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#bad_json), [`line_too_long`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#line_too_long), [`unknown_op`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#unknown_op), [`bad_args`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#bad_args), [`shutting_down`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#shutting_down) | A malformed request, or the copy is quitting. | Fix the request; see [Control protocol](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/control-protocol/). |

## Diagnostics

| Signal | Next action |
|---|---|
| `SCN001`-`SCN005` | Standard warnings and SCN003 (error). [Standard diagnostics](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/standard/). |
| `SCN101`-`SCN114` | Graft errors; apply the hint. [Graft diagnostics](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/grafts/). |
| `SCN120`-`SCN131` | Build mode and injection. [Build and injection diagnostics](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/builds-and-injection/). |
| `SCN201`-`SCN203` | Recipes and adapters. [Trials diagnostics](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/trials/). |
| `SCN301`-`SCN307` | Determinism scan, in `diagnose` only. [Determinism diagnostics](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/determinism/). |

## See also

- [Error and warning codes](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/)
- [Exit codes](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/exit-codes/)
- [Reading results](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/reading-results/)
