# Reading results

A trial run writes far more than an agent should read. This guide gives the reading order (the `trial run` JSON, then
`report.md` of failed or changed recipes, then `window.png` only when pixels changed or the task is visual, then
`context.png`, never `frames/`), the image rules that keep a 1-texel shake visible to a vision model, the motion pack
for judging feel, the two-pass review and what each step costs in tokens.

## When to use

- After every `dotnet scion trial run`, `trial run --warm` or `trial loop` pass.
- When reviewing a visual change: hit effects, HUD states, rooms, animations.

## Steps

### 1. Read the JSON

The envelope is always under 1.5 KB. Decide from it alone whether anything needs a look:

| Field | Look further when |
|---|---|
| `failed[]` | not empty: read each `report` |
| `changed[]` | not empty: these recipes differ from their baseline |
| `runs.new` | above 0: read `report.md` before approving |
| `determinism.hash_stable` | `false`: see [What to do next](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/next-action/) |
| `warnings[]` | not empty |

Paths inside lists are relative to `run`; `next_step` uses absolute paths.

### 2. Read report.md of failed and changed recipes only

`dotnet scion trial show --failed` and `trial show --changed` print the paths. Each recipe's `report.md` (about 1,200
tokens) has the verdict, the checks that did not pass, the images with their frames, the timeline of marks, the
probes, notes and logged errors. Most failures are explained here, without an image.

### 3. Open window.png only for pixel changes or visual tasks

Open an image when `changed[].hash` is `same` (only pixels moved), when the verdict is `px_changed` or `within` and the
task is visual, or when the task itself is about the look. `window.png` holds up to 12 consecutive frames around the
impact, 3 columns, numbered with their game time and marks. Prefer `grid.png` from `trial show <Id> --grid` for a
`changed` recipe: baseline, current and difference rows in one image.

### 4. Open context.png only if the window is not enough

`context.png` shows 6 key frames chosen by the marks (announcement, action, impact, peak of the number, death,
after), 3 by 2. It answers "what happened before and after"; the window answers "how did the hit feel".

### 5. Never open frames/

`frames/NNNN.png` exists only with `--frames`, and a recipe has dozens to hundreds of them. Open single frames only
when a person asks for them.

### 6. Delegate when there are many images

With more than about 5 images to judge, give the run folder and the ids to the `scion-triage` subagent (Claude Code)
or a separate agent. It returns one line per recipe ([The Scion skill](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/skill/)).

## Reference

### Image rules

Scion writes every image so a vision model sees what matters without recompression:

| Rule | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Longest side | at most 2000 px for sheets (`window.png`, `context.png`, `sheet.png`); at most 1568 px for motion pack images, which crop the action area | Above about 1568 px some readers recompress images as JPEG, which erases 1-texel shake: use `--motion` when shake matters |
| File size | under 500 KB | Same |
| Images per request | at most 20 | API limit of most vision models |
| Scaling of crops | 2x nearest neighbor | Pixel art keeps its pixels |
| Frame labels | `f07 +117ms IMPACT` on each cell | The model knows time and events without guessing |
| Fixed crosshair | drawn on `window.png` when `--motion` is on | Reveals camera shake |

Sheets for people (`sheet.png`, `preview.gif`) may be larger; agents should not open `preview.gif` (models read only
its first frame).

### The motion pack

Vision models are poor at fine motion even when they see every frame. For feel (hit-stop, shake, flash, easing),
run with `--motion` and read the numbers first:

| File | Content | Tokens |
|---|---|---|
| `metrics.json` | Measured hit-stop, shake, flash, anticipation and number easing, with targets | about 300 |
| `report.md` | Per-frame timeline plus a measured, target and status table | about 1,200 |
| `window.png` | 12 frames around the impact, 2x nearest neighbor, numbered, with a crosshair | about 1,000 |
| `motion-diff.png` | The same layout with the frame-to-frame difference amplified (a black cell is a hit-stop frame) | about 1,000 |
| `tracks.png` | Luminance, camera offset, 1 - SSIM and number height over time, with lines at the marks | about 1,250 |
| `context.png` | 6 key frames | about 1,900 |

See [The motion pack](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/motion-pack/).

### Two-pass review

For a visual judgment, do two passes:

1. **Blind:** only the images. "Describe the impact frame by frame." About 4,000 tokens.
2. **With numbers:** `tracks.png`, `metrics.json` and `report.md`; check where the description and the numbers
   disagree. About 7,500 tokens.

For A/B choices, see [A/B comparisons](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/ab-comparison/): variants aligned on the impact, blind labels,
asked in both orders.

## Errors

| Situation | Next action |
|---|---|
| `report.md` missing for a failed pair | The copy crashed: read `q<i>/player.log` (`player_crashed`). |
| `window.png` missing | The recipe never called `MarkImpact` and had no cut; read `report.md` and the recipe. |
| An image is blank or magenta | The `blank` or `magenta` check failed too; it is in `report.md`. |
| `grid.png` missing | The recipe keeps no images (`Tolerance = null`); compare `window.png` of both runs with `trial diff`. |

## Examples

### Deciding without an image

```json
{"changed":[{"id":"KnightFalls","vs_approved":"changed","hash":"changed","image":"q1/KnightFalls/r1/window.png"}]}
```

`hash: changed` means the rules changed. The image will not explain why: read `report.md`, the probes and the diff of
the rule code first.

### A pixel-only change

```json
{"changed":[{"id":"SlashHit","vs_approved":"changed","hash":"same","image":"q0/SlashHit/r1/window.png","diff":"diff/SlashHit/r1/window.diff.png"}]}
```

`hash: same`: the rules did not change. Open `grid.png` (`trial show SlashHit --grid`) to see the visual change and
report it to the person.

## See also

- [What to do next](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/next-action/)
- [Capture and outputs](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/capture/)
- [The motion pack](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/motion-pack/)
- [report.md](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/report-md/)

# Project index and manifest

Agents learn a Scion project in three layers: the **index** (under 2 KB, always loaded), the **commands** they query on
demand (`anchor list`, `trial list`), and the **rules** the hooks enforce. This page covers the index that
`dotnet scion index` prints, the `<!-- scion:begin -->` block it keeps in `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`, and the
manifest that `dotnet scion gen` generates from the code: `scion.manifest.json` for tools and `GRAFTS.md` for people.

## The index

`dotnet scion index` writes a short description of the project as facts, not instructions, so it never reads like a
prompt injection. It lists categories and counts, never every anchor:

```text
This project uses Scion 1.0.0 (adoption level 3).
Grafts: new presentation code in Assets/Orchard/Grafts/*.cs (promoted) and scion/grafts/*.cs (drafts), hung on anchors with [Before]/[After].
Anchor categories: presentation (14), hud (9), camera (3), audio (4).
Rules change in Orchard.Core with RuleModifier<T>; tunables: 7 visual, 3 rule.
Recipes: SlashHit, FireballArea, KnightFalls, CoopTurn (4 players), HudStates, UnitGallery. Specs: SlimeIsThreatening, DifficultyCurve.
Commands: dotnet scion anchor list|show, graft new|check|build|inject|promote, trial run|show|approve, doctor.
The manifest is queried through commands, not read whole.
```

Anchor categories come from the first segment of `[Anchor]` ids (`presentation.hit` is in `presentation`); anchors
without an id count under their type's namespace. With `--hook` the same text is wrapped as Claude Code
`SessionStart` context ([Hooks](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/hooks/)).

## The block in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md

`dotnet scion index --write <file>` keeps the index plus the agent rules between two markers. Everything outside the
markers is yours and never touched:

```md
<!-- scion:begin -->
## Scion
This project uses Scion 1.0.0 (adoption level 3). Docs: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt
...
<!-- scion:end -->
```

If the project keeps its instructions in `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` should import it with the line `@AGENTS.md`, so
Claude Code and the other agents read the same block.

## The manifest

`dotnet scion gen` reads the code (attributes, recipes, tunables, probes) and writes two files at the project root:

| File | For | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `scion.manifest.json` | tools and agents, through commands | Every anchor with its id, target, signature and doc; every graft with file, line, kind, priority and target; every tunable with type, range, value and layer; every recipe; every probe. Schema: [`manifest.schema.json`](/scion/41664431a8f5/schemas/v1/manifest.schema.json) |
| `GRAFTS.md` | people and pull requests | A readable table of the same data, grouped by anchor |

Both are generated: nobody edits them by hand, and the baseline guard denies agent edits to them
([Hooks](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/hooks/)). The source of truth is the code: `[Anchor(Id, Doc)]`, `[Before]`/`[After]`,
`[Tunable]`, `[Probe]` and the recipe classes.

`gen` reads source with Roslyn when the Unity project has not compiled, and the build's DLLs with Mono.Cecil when a
test build exists; `generated_from` in the manifest says which.

## Keep them current in CI

```sh
dotnet scion gen && git diff --exit-code scion.manifest.json GRAFTS.md
dotnet scion graft check --strict
```

The first line fails the job when someone changed an anchor or graft without regenerating. The second fails on
warnings too. See [Run Scion in CI](/scion/41664431a8f5/cookbook/ci/).

## Querying instead of reading

Agents never read the manifest whole. They ask:

| Question | Command |
|---|---|
| Where can I hang a hit effect? | `dotnet scion anchor list --search hit` |
| What is the exact signature? | `dotnet scion anchor show presentation.hit` |
| Which grafts run on this anchor, in what order? | `dotnet scion anchor show presentation.hit` (`grafts`) |
| Which recipes exist? | `dotnet scion trial list` |
| Which tunables can I change? | `dotnet scion gen --list tunables` |

## See also

- [index, guard](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/index-and-guard/)
- [gen](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/gen/)
- [scion.manifest.json and GRAFTS.md](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/manifest/)
- [Hooks](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/hooks/)

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# How grafts work

A graft is a `static void` C# method marked `[Before]` or `[After]` that Scion's weaver hangs onto an existing game
method, its **anchor**, without editing the anchor's source. This page explains the mechanism: the weaver is a Unity
`ILPostProcessor` built on Mono.Cecil, it rewrites the IL of anchors when Unity compiles, final builds call grafts
directly (call mode) and test builds route them through swappable slots (slot mode, `SCION_SLOTS`) so new grafts can
be injected into a running game.

## How it works

![Diagram: graft source files compile into the game assembly; the weaver rewrites each anchor; the final build calls a generated dispatcher directly; the test build calls a swappable slot that injection can replace.](../../../assets/diagrams/weaver-flow.svg)

### The weaver

`Unity.Scion.CodeGen` is an `ILPostProcessor`. After Unity compiles an assembly that references `Scion.Runtime`, the
weaver:

1. finds every method marked `[Before]` or `[After]` in that assembly;
2. resolves each target method (exact signature first, then a unique prefix match);
3. checks the rules (shape, eligibility, `Call` usage) and reports violations as compile errors with file and line;
4. rewrites each anchor's IL so it calls a generated dispatcher at its start (befores) and at every return (afters).

The weaver only rewrites the assembly it is compiling. A graft must therefore compile **into the anchor's own
assembly**: you keep grafts in their own folder and point it at the game assembly with an `.asmref`
([SCN102](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/grafts/#scn102)).

### Two modes

| | Call mode (final build) | Slot mode (test build) |
|---|---|---|
| Define | none | `SCION_SLOTS` |
| Backend | IL2CPP or Mono | Mono (needs a JIT) |
| How an anchor reaches its grafts | A direct static call to `__ScionGenerated.D_<id>`, which calls the grafts in order | A static delegate field per anchor (`__ScionGenerated.F_<id>`), filled with the promoted grafts at startup |
| Run-time cost | none measurable; the dispatcher is inlined | about 1 to 3 ns per call |
| Registration, reflection, allocation | none | none per call |
| Injection | not available | `Injection.Inject` swaps slots at the next recipe boundary |
| A graft that throws | propagates like any other code | is caught, disabled alone and reported to `Faults` |

In slot mode, `[assembly: AnchorScope(typeof(T))]` gives methods a slot even when no graft targets them yet, so a
new graft can be injected there without a rebuild ([Anchors](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/anchors/)).

### Why compile time

Run-time patching (Harmony, MonoMod, detours) does not work under IL2CPP and hides errors until the code runs.
Scion's weaver gives:

- direct calls in the shipped build, which IL2CPP inlines;
- compile errors with file, line and a fix (`Did you mean 'Play'?`), also live in the IDE through the analyzers;
- one dispatcher per anchor with a fixed order, so the order never depends on load order.

The per-call context `ref Call<T>` follows the model of Mixin's `CallbackInfoReturnable`: grafts can skip the
anchor, return a value or change its result ([Call and Call\<T\>](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/call-context/)).

### Grafts are visual

The weaver does not run in plain `dotnet test`, in the rules simulator or anywhere outside Unity. A graft that
changed a rule would work in the game and vanish everywhere else, and co-op peers would disagree. So every graft is
presentation: effects, sound, camera, HUD, telemetry. Rules change in the core through `RuleModifier<T>`
([Grafts are visual only](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/visual-only/)).

## Key terms

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Graft | A `static void` method with `[Before]` or `[After]`, public or internal, non-generic. |
| Anchor | A method the weaver rewrote. Every target of a graft is one; `AnchorScope` adds more in test builds. |
| Anchor id | `B__` or `A__` plus the type, method and parameter type names, for example `A__Orchard_Presentation_HitPresenter__Play__HitEvent`. |
| Dispatcher | The generated method that calls an anchor's grafts in order (`__ScionGenerated.D_<id>`). |
| Slot | In test builds, the delegate field that holds an anchor's dispatcher; injection replaces it. |
| Promoted graft | A graft compiled into the game (`grafts.promoted` folder). |
| Draft graft | A graft in `grafts.staging` (`scion/grafts/`), compiled to a DLL and injected; it enters the game when promoted. |
| Observer | A `[Before(..., Observe = true)]` graft: always runs, cannot skip. |

## Guarantees and limits

- Removing the grafts folder leaves a game that compiles and plays as before: nothing may depend on a graft
  ([SCN110](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/grafts/#scn110)).
- Order within one call is fixed: observers, then other befores by `Priority`, then the body, then afters by
  `Priority`; ties break on the graft's full name.
- The final build contains no slots, no injection and no trials code; a final build with test defines fails
  ([SCN121](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/builds-and-injection/#scn121)).
- Some methods cannot be anchors: iterators, `async` methods, Netcode RPCs, struct methods, generic methods, methods
  with `out` parameters and a few more ([SCN105](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/grafts/#scn105)). Hang the graft on the
  plain method they call.
- Injected grafts must be `public` in a `public` type: they live in another assembly.
- Mono never unloads assemblies; a warm copy asks to be recycled after 50 injections (`InjectReport.Recycle`).

## See also

- [Write a graft](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/write/)
- [Build modes](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/build-modes/)
- [Live injection](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/injection/)
- [Architecture](/scion/41664431a8f5/contribute/architecture/)

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Write a graft

This guide writes grafts with `[Before(typeof(T), "Method")]` and `[After(typeof(T), "Method")]`: the method shape the
weaver accepts (`static void`, public or internal, not generic, SCN101), the folder with an `.asmref` that compiles it
into the target's assembly (SCN102), how parameters bind to the target (exact signature, then a unique prefix, SCN112),
and the ordering controls `Priority` and `Observe`.

## When to use

- Use a graft to add presentation to a game method without editing it: an effect, a sound, a camera move, a HUD
  change, telemetry, a trials mark.
- Do not use a graft to change a rule (damage, range, turn order, anything in the state hash). Change the core with a
  `RuleModifier<T>` ([Grafts are visual only](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/visual-only/)).

## Before you begin

- The game assembly references `Scion.Runtime` (`dotnet scion init` adds it).
- A promoted grafts folder with an `.asmref` to the game assembly, for example
  `Assets/Orchard/Grafts/Orchard.Grafts.asmref`:

```json
{"reference":"Orchard.Runtime"}
```

## Steps

### 1. Find the anchor

```sh
dotnet scion anchor list --search hit
dotnet scion anchor show presentation.hit
```

`anchor show` prints the target's signature and a declaration that binds to it.

### 2. Create the draft

```sh
dotnet scion graft new CritShake --after Orchard.Presentation.HitPresenter.Play
```

<!-- validate: cli/graft-new -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"graft new","ok":true,"file":"scion/grafts/CritShake.cs","target":"Orchard.Presentation.HitPresenter.Play","kind":"after","signature":"public static void After(HitPresenter presenter, HitEvent e, ref Call<float> c)","next_step":"edit scion/grafts/CritShake.cs, then: dotnet scion graft check scion/grafts/CritShake.cs"}
```

### 3. Write the body

```csharp
using Orchard.Core;
using Orchard.Presentation;
using Scion;
using Scion.Core;

namespace Orchard.Grafts
{
    public static class CritShake
    {
        [Tunable(0f, 1f, Doc = "Camera shake on a critical hit.")]
        public static float Strength = 0.3f;

        // After every hit: critical hits shake the camera, pause briefly and last a bit longer.
        [After(typeof(HitPresenter), nameof(HitPresenter.Play))]
        public static void After(HitPresenter presenter, HitEvent e, ref Call<float> c)
        {
            if (!e.Crit) return;
            Fx.Shake(Strength);
            Fx.HitStop(0.06f);
            c.Result += 0.06f;   // Play returns how long the hit lasts
        }
    }
}
```

### 4. Check it

```sh
dotnet scion graft check scion/grafts/CritShake.cs
```

The check runs Roslyn and the weaver rules against the test build, without Unity. Fix every diagnostic it lists.

### 5. Try and promote it

Inject it into a running copy ([Live injection](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/injection/)), or promote it and rebuild
([From draft to final build](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/lifecycle/)).

## Reference

### Before and After

| Attribute | Runs | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| `[Before(typeof(T), "Method")]` | before the target's body | watch a call, guard it, skip it, return early |
| `[After(typeof(T), "Method")]` | at every `return` of the target | react to a call, read or change its result |

Name the target with `nameof` when it is visible from the graft, and with a string when it is private:

```csharp
[After(typeof(HitPresenter), "PlayCritical")]   // private method: name as a string
public static void After(HitPresenter presenter, HitEvent e) { }
```

Both attributes allow multiple use, so one method can hang on several targets. Targets must be declared on the type
itself: a method inherited from a base class is not found ([SCN103](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/grafts/#scn103)).

### Method shape

| Rule | Diagnostic |
|---|---|
| `static void` | [SCN101](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/grafts/#scn101) |
| `public` or `internal` (injected drafts: `public`, in a `public` type) | SCN101 |
| Not generic, not in a generic type, not in a private or protected nested type | SCN101 |
| Compiled into the target's assembly (folder with an `.asmref`) | [SCN102](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/grafts/#scn102) |
| Never called by game code | [SCN110](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/grafts/#scn110) |

Name the class after the graft (`CritShake`) and the method after its side (`Before` or `After`). The graft's
identity is its full name, `Orchard.Grafts.CritShake.After`: it orders ties, names the graft in `Fx` telemetry and
decides which promoted graft an injected one replaces.

### Parameter binding

A graft's parameters mirror the target's:

1. the target instance, for instance methods (omit it for static targets);
2. the target's parameters, in order, with the same `in` and `ref` modifiers;
3. optionally, last, `ref Call` (void target) or `ref Call<T>` (target returns `T`).

**Prefixes.** A graft may stop early and declare only the first parameters:

```csharp
[After(typeof(HitPresenter), nameof(HitPresenter.Play))]
public static void After(HitPresenter presenter) => hits++;   // only the instance
```

**Overloads.** The overload whose full signature matches wins; otherwise the single overload the prefix matches.
When a prefix matches two or more overloads, it is [SCN112](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/grafts/#scn112): declare all
parameters. A signature that matches nothing is [SCN104](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/grafts/#scn104), whose hint
gives the expected signature.

**Values.** A graft sees the current parameter values: if the body reassigns a parameter, an `[After]` sees the new
value.

**Overrides.** On a virtual method, a graft fires only for the method it targets. A graft on `UnitView.Play` does not
fire when an override in `KnightView` runs without calling `base.Play`: target the override.

### Priority

`Priority` (an `int`, default 0) orders the grafts of one anchor and side: lower runs first. Ties break on the graft's
full name (ordinal), so order never depends on file or compile order.

```csharp
[After(typeof(HitPresenter), nameof(HitPresenter.Play), Priority = -10)]
public static void After(HitPresenter presenter, HitEvent e) { }
```

### Observe

`Observe = true` (only on `[Before]`) marks an observer: a graft that only watches. Observers always run, before
every `[Before]` that may skip the target, ordered by `Priority` among themselves, and may not call `Skip()` or
`Return()` ([SCN108](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/grafts/#scn108)). Use one when the graft must see every call,
including calls another graft skips, such as a trials mark:

```csharp
[Before(typeof(HitPresenter), nameof(HitPresenter.Play), Observe = true)]
public static void Before(HitPresenter presenter, HitEvent e) => TrialSession.Current?.MarkImpact();
```

### Order within one call

1. observers, by `Priority`;
2. the other `[Before]` grafts, by `Priority`; the first that skips stops the remaining befores and the body;
3. the target's body;
4. the `[After]` grafts, by `Priority`; they also run after a skip, and can read `Skipped`.

If the target throws, the `[After]` grafts do not run.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SCN101` | compile error | Not `static void`, private, generic, or in a generic or hidden type. | `public static void After(...)` in a non-generic public class. |
| `SCN102` | compile error | The file compiles into another assembly than the target. | Move it to the folder with the `.asmref`. |
| `SCN103` | compile error | The target method does not exist on that type. | Use the name from the hint. |
| `SCN104` | compile error | Parameters match no overload. | Copy the expected signature from the hint. |
| `SCN105` | compile error | The target cannot be an anchor. | Hang the graft on the plain method it calls. |
| `SCN108` | compile error | `Skip` or `Return` in an `[After]` or an observer. | Move it to a non-observer `[Before]`. |
| `SCN112` | compile error | A prefix matches several overloads. | Declare all parameters. |

In `graft check` and `build test` these come back in `diagnostics[]` or `errors[]` with exit code 1. The full list is
in [Graft diagnostics](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/grafts/).

## Examples

### A sound on every turn banner

```csharp
[Before(typeof(Hud), nameof(Hud.ShowTurn))]
public static void Before(Hud hud, int turn)
{
    Fx.Sound(turn == 1 ? "turn_first" : "turn");
}
```

### One graft on two targets

```csharp
[After(typeof(DamageNumbers), nameof(DamageNumbers.Spawn))]
[After(typeof(DamageNumbers), nameof(DamageNumbers.SpawnHeal))]
public static void After(DamageNumbers numbers, int amount, Vector3 at) => Fx.Sound("pop", at, 0.6f);
```

Both targets share the parameter list `(int amount, Vector3 at)`, so one method fits both.

## See also

- [Call and Call\<T\>](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/call-context/)
- [Anchors](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/anchors/)
- [graft (CLI)](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/graft/)
- [Grafts API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/grafts/)

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Call and Call<T>

A graft may take one extra parameter, always the last, that gives it the per-call context: `ref Call` for targets
that return `void`, `ref Call<T>` for targets that return `T`. With it a graft reads `Skipped`, skips the target with
`Skip()`, returns early with `Return(value)`, reads or replaces the result through `Result`, and hands state from a
`[Before]` to an `[After]` of the same call with `Tag`. The weaver checks the rules as SCN108, SCN109 and SCN111.

## When to use

- Use `Skip()` or `Return()` to suppress or replace presentation: skip a banner during a replay, cut an animation
  short, return a shorter duration.
- Use `Result` in an `[After]` to adjust what the target returns (a duration, a color, a position).
- Use `Tag` to measure or correlate something between the start and the end of one call.
- Do not use any of these to change rules. Skipping a rule method in a graft desynchronizes co-op peers; the analyzer
  reports writes to rule state as SCN003.

## Steps

### 1. Declare the context as the last parameter

| Target returns | Last parameter | Members |
|---|---|---|
| `void` | `ref Call c` | `Skipped`, `Skip()`, `Tag` |
| `T` | `ref Call<T> c`, with `T` equal to the return type | `Skipped`, `Result`, `Return(T)`, `Tag` |

It must be passed by `ref`; a `Call` by value, `in` or `out` is a signature error
([SCN104](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/grafts/#scn104)). A `T` that differs from the return type, or `Call` on a
target that returns a value, is [SCN109](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/grafts/#scn109).

### 2. Skip a void target

Only a `[Before]` that is not an observer may skip:

```csharp
[Before(typeof(Hud), nameof(Hud.ShowTurn))]
public static void Before(Hud hud, int turn, ref Call c)
{
    if (ReplayMode.Active) c.Skip();   // the body and later befores do not run; afters do
}
```

### 3. Return early with a value

`Return(value)` sets `Result` and skips:

```csharp
[Before(typeof(HitPresenter), nameof(HitPresenter.Play))]
public static void Before(HitPresenter presenter, HitEvent e, ref Call<float> c)
{
    if (e.Amount == 0) c.Return(0f);   // a miss presents nothing and takes no time
}
```

### 4. Change the result in an After

```csharp
[After(typeof(HitPresenter), nameof(HitPresenter.Play))]
public static void After(HitPresenter presenter, HitEvent e, ref Call<float> c)
{
    if (e.Crit) c.Result += 0.06f;
}
```

In an `[After]`, `Result` is what the target returns now, and the graft may change it; the next after sees the
changed value. In a `[Before]`, `Result` is the value returned if the target is skipped.

### 5. Hand state from Before to After

`Tag` is a `long`, 0 at the start of every call, shared by every graft of that call:

```csharp
public static class HitTiming
{
    [Before(typeof(HitPresenter), nameof(HitPresenter.Play))]
    public static void Before(HitPresenter presenter, ref Call<float> c) => c.Tag = Stopwatch.GetTimestamp();

    [After(typeof(HitPresenter), nameof(HitPresenter.Play))]
    public static void After(HitPresenter presenter, ref Call<float> c) =>
        TrialSession.Current?.Probe("hit_present_ticks", Stopwatch.GetTimestamp() - c.Tag);
}
```

When two or more befores, or two or more afters, of one anchor use `Tag`, the weaver warns
([SCN111](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/grafts/#scn111)): let one pair own it, or keep other state in your own fields.

## Reference

### Order in one call

| Step | Who runs | Can skip |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Observers (`[Before(..., Observe = true)]`), by `Priority` | no |
| 2 | Other befores, by `Priority`; the first that skips stops the rest of this step and step 3 | yes |
| 3 | The target's body | |
| 4 | Afters, by `Priority`, with `Skipped` set if step 2 skipped | no |

If the body throws, step 4 does not run. The context lives on the anchor's stack: nothing allocates.

### Members

| Member | `Call` | `Call<T>` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Skipped` | yes | yes | True after a before skipped the call. |
| `Skip()` | yes | | Skip the rest of the befores and the body. Non-observer befores only (SCN108). |
| `Result` | | yes | After: the current return value, settable. Before: the value returned on skip. |
| `Return(T value)` | | yes | `Result = value` and skip. Non-observer befores only (SCN108). |
| `Tag` | yes | yes | A `long` shared by every graft of one call; 0 at the start. |
| `Call(T result)` constructor | | yes | For tests outside Unity: a context that holds a result. |

### Cost

Measured on an Apple M5: in IL2CPP call mode, a graft without context adds nothing measurable, a `[Before]` with
`ref Call` adds about 0.5 ns and an `[After]` with `ref Call<float>` about 0.2 ns. In Mono slot mode (test builds),
the same cases cost about 2 to 7 ns; prefer `int` over `float` results in hot paths of test builds.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SCN104` | compile error | `Call` not passed by `ref`, or not the last parameter. | `ref Call c` or `ref Call<T> c`, last. |
| `SCN108` | compile error | `Skip()` or `Return()` in an `[After]` or an observer. | Use a non-observer `[Before]`, or only read `c.Skipped`. |
| `SCN109` | compile error | `Call<T>` with the wrong `T`, or `Call` on a non-void target. | Match the target's return type. |
| `SCN111` | compile warning | Several befores or afters of one anchor use `Tag`. | Let one graft own `Tag`. |

## Examples

### Skip a banner only in test runs

```csharp
[Before(typeof(Hud), nameof(Hud.ShowTurn))]
public static void Before(Hud hud, int turn, ref Call c)
{
#if SCION_TRIALS
    if (TrialSession.Current?.Recipe?.Tags.Contains("no-banner") == true) c.Skip();
#endif
}
```

### Test the result change without Unity

```csharp
var c = new Call<float>(0.5f);
CritShake.After(null, new HitEvent(attacker: 0, target: 1, amount: 9, crit: true), ref c);
Assert.Equal(0.56f, c.Result, 3);
```

See [Test grafts without Unity](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/testing/).

## See also

- [Write a graft](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/write/)
- [Grafts API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/grafts/)
- [Graft diagnostics](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/grafts/)

# Anchors

An anchor is a game method the weaver rewrites so grafts run around it. This guide covers which methods can be
anchors (SCN105), the generated anchor ids (`Anchors.Id`), stable names and descriptions with `[Anchor(Id, Doc)]`,
slots without a graft in test builds with `[assembly: AnchorScope(typeof(T), Members = ...)]`, and the commands that
find them: `dotnet scion anchor list` and `anchor show`. Errors: SCN105, SCN106, SCN107.

## When to use

- Use `anchor list` before writing any graft, to find the method to hang it on and its exact signature.
- Use `[Anchor]` on the presentation methods agents should find first: it gives them a stable id and a one-line doc.
- Use `AnchorScope` on presentation types where new grafts will be injected live, so a draft can bind there without
  a rebuild.

## Steps

### 1. Search the anchors of the build

```sh
dotnet scion anchor list --search hit
```

<!-- validate: cli/anchor-list -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"anchor list","ok":true,"build":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/builds/test/Orchard.app","total":2,"anchors":[{"id":"A__Orchard_Presentation_HitPresenter__Play__HitEvent","anchor":"presentation.hit","target":"Orchard.Presentation.HitPresenter.Play","signature":"float Play(HitEvent e)","slot":true,"doc":"Plays one hit and returns how long it lasts.","promoted":["Orchard.Grafts.HitFlash.After"]},{"id":"B__Orchard_Presentation_HitPresenter__Play__HitEvent","anchor":"presentation.hit","target":"Orchard.Presentation.HitPresenter.Play","signature":"float Play(HitEvent e)","slot":true,"doc":null,"promoted":[]}],"next_step":"create a graft: dotnet scion graft new MyGraft --after Orchard.Presentation.HitPresenter.Play"}
```

`slot: true` means the method has a slot in this test build, so a draft graft can be injected there. `promoted` lists
the grafts already compiled into the game.

### 2. Name the important anchors

```csharp
namespace Orchard.Presentation
{
    public sealed class HitPresenter : MonoBehaviour
    {
        [Anchor(Id = "presentation.hit", Doc = "Plays one hit and returns how long it lasts.")]
        public float Play(HitEvent e) { /* ... */ }
    }
}
```

`[Anchor]` is metadata for tools: the weaver ignores it, so it neither creates an anchor nor changes the IL. The id's
first segment (`presentation`) is the category the project index counts.

### 3. Give presentation types slots

```csharp
[assembly: Scion.AnchorScope(typeof(Orchard.Presentation.HitPresenter))]
[assembly: Scion.AnchorScope(typeof(Orchard.Presentation.Hud), Members = new[] { "ShowTurn", "ShowDamage" })]
[assembly: Scion.AnchorScope(typeof(Orchard.Presentation.CameraRig))]
```

Put these in any file that compiles into the assembly that declares the types (the grafts folder works). Rebuild the
test player; `anchor list` then shows `slot: true` for every eligible method of those types.

## Reference

### Automatic anchors

Every method named by a `[Before]` or `[After]` becomes an anchor in every build. In test builds (`SCION_SLOTS`),
every eligible method covered by an `AnchorScope` also gets a slot, with or without a graft. The final build ignores
`AnchorScope`: there, only methods with a promoted graft change.

### Methods that cannot be anchors

A graft on one of these is [SCN105](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/grafts/#scn105), with the reason; `AnchorScope`
skips them silently:

- constructors, abstract methods and methods without a body;
- generic methods and methods of generic types;
- methods of a struct;
- iterators and `async` methods (the anchor would only catch the creation of the state machine);
- Netcode for GameObjects RPCs (their prologue returns early on the sending side);
- methods with `[RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod]` or `[BurstCompile]`, compiler-generated methods and names that
  start with `__`;
- methods with an `out` or pointer parameter, or that return by reference, a ref struct or a pointer;
- methods of private or protected nested types, or whose parameter or return types generated code cannot access.

Hang the graft on the plain method the iterator, `async` method or RPC calls.

### Anchor ids

Each side of an anchor has an id: `B__` (before) or `A__` (after), the type's full name, the method name and the
simple names of the parameter types, with every character outside `[A-Za-z0-9_]` turned into `_`. `Anchors.Id`
computes it the same way the weaver and the injection do:

```csharp
Anchors.Id(true, "Orchard.Presentation.HitPresenter", "Play", new[] { "HitEvent" })
// "A__Orchard_Presentation_HitPresenter__Play__HitEvent"
```

Overloads whose ids collide (for example `List<int>` and `List<string>` parameters) are
[SCN106](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/grafts/#scn106) when a graft targets them, and get no slot in a scope.

### AnchorScope rules

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Where | In the assembly that defines the type; elsewhere it is [SCN107](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/grafts/#scn107). |
| `Members` omitted | Every eligible method of the type, both sides. |
| `Members` given | Only those names; an empty array gives none. Use compiled names: a property getter is `get_Name`. |
| A name that does not exist | [SCN103](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/grafts/#scn103) with the closest name. |
| A name whose overloads are all ineligible or collide | SCN105 or SCN106 (no file and line: it comes from an assembly attribute). |
| Several attributes for one type | They add up. |
| Final build | Ignored. |

### Commands

| Command | Use |
|---|---|
| `dotnet scion anchor list [--search <text>] [--type <Type>]` | Eligible anchors of the build, with slot, `[Anchor]` id, doc and promoted grafts |
| `dotnet scion anchor show <id>` | One anchor: signature, grafts in run order, a ready graft declaration |

`<id>` is an `[Anchor]` id (`presentation.hit`), a slot id (`A__...`) or `Type.Method`. See
[anchor list, anchor show](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/anchor/).

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SCN105` | compile error | The target cannot be an anchor. | Hang the graft on the method it calls. |
| `SCN106` | compile error | Overloads collide on one anchor id. | Rename one overload or change a parameter type name. |
| `SCN107` | compile error | `AnchorScope` names a type of another assembly. | Move the attribute into that assembly. |
| `SCN113` | 1 (`graft build`, `graft inject`) | The draft targets a method with no slot in this build. | Add its type to `AnchorScope`, rebuild, inject again. |
| `no_match` | 2 | `anchor show` found no anchor with that id. | Use `did_you_mean`, or `anchor list --search`. |

## Examples

### Every anchor of one type

```sh
dotnet scion anchor list --type Orchard.Presentation.CameraRig
```

### A scope limited to two methods

```csharp
[assembly: Scion.AnchorScope(typeof(Orchard.Presentation.DamageNumbers), Members = new[] { "Spawn", "SpawnHeal" })]
```

## See also

- [anchor list, anchor show](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/anchor/)
- [Write a graft](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/write/)
- [Live injection](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/injection/)
- [Grafts API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/grafts/)

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Grafts are visual only

Every graft is presentation: effects, sound, camera, HUD, telemetry, trials marks. Rules (damage, range, turn order,
anything in the state hash) change only in the game's core, through `RuleModifier<T>` registered explicitly. This page
explains why, how the analyzers SCN003 and SCN110 enforce it with the `analyzers` section of
`ProjectSettings/ScionSettings.json`, and how a state-hash A/B run proves a graft harmless before it is promoted.

## How it works

### Why rules stay out of grafts

The weaver runs only inside Unity's compilation. It does not run in `dotnet test`, in the rules simulator that balance
specs and the multiverse use, or on a dedicated server built from the core. A graft that changed a rule would work in
the game and vanish everywhere else: tests would pass on rules the game does not use, and co-op peers or replays would
disagree. So the split is fixed:

| Change | How it extends | Where it runs |
|---|---|---|
| **Visual**: juice, sound, camera, HUD, telemetry | A graft on a presentation anchor | Locally on each machine; only in Unity |
| **Rule**: damage, range, turns, AI decisions | A `RuleModifier<T>` registered in the core, with a stage, a priority and integers | Identically on every peer, in Unity and in plain .NET |

### How it is enforced

Two analyzers read `ProjectSettings/ScionSettings.json`:

```json
{"schema_version":1,"analyzers":{"rule_assemblies":["Orchard.Core"],"rule_types":["Unity.Netcode.*"],"graft_paths":["Assets/Orchard/Grafts/","../scion/grafts/"]}}
```

- [SCN003](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/standard/#scn003) (error): inside graft code, any write to a field, property,
  indexer, event or array element of a rule type, and any use of an internal member of a rule type. A rule type is
  any type in `rule_assemblies`, any type matched by `rule_types`, and any class derived from one.
- [SCN110](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/grafts/#scn110) (error): game code that refers to graft code. Nothing may
  depend on a graft, so deleting the grafts folder leaves a game that compiles and plays the same.

```csharp
[After(typeof(HitPresenter), nameof(HitPresenter.Play))]
public static void After(HitPresenter presenter, HitEvent e)
{
    presenter.Battle.State.Turn = 0;   // SCN003: Graft CritShake.After writes rule state (State.Turn); grafts are visual only.
}
```

### The proof: hash A/B

SCN003 is a heuristic: it does not see a public method that changes state (`state.Apply(cmd)`) or a write through an
alias. The safety net is the state hash. Run the recipes with and without the graft; the hash must not move:

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --rounds 2
dotnet scion trial run --rounds 2 --grafts .scion/grafts/ScionGrafts_51c2.dll
```

Any `hash: changed` in the second run means the graft touched a rule. The multiverse does the same comparison per turn
and names the first field that changed ([The multiverse](/scion/41664431a8f5/explore/multiverse/)).

### Rules change in the core

```csharp
namespace Orchard.Core
{
    public sealed class BackstabBonus : RuleModifier<DamageCalc>
    {
        public override Stage Stage => Stage.Mul;
        public override int Priority => 10;
        public override void Apply(ref DamageCalc c)
        {
            if (c.FromBehind) c.MulPermille += 500;   // +50 %, integers only
        }
    }
}
```

The core registers it explicitly (`damage.Add(new BackstabBonus())`), so the rule set is visible in code, enters the
lobby hash and runs the same in Unity, in the simulator and on every peer. See
[Core API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/core/).

## Key terms

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Graft code | Every `[Before]`/`[After]` method with its lambdas and local functions, and everything declared under `graft_paths`. |
| Rule type | A type in `rule_assemblies`, matched by `rule_types`, or derived from one. |
| Rule code | The code of the `rule_assemblies`; it also follows SCN001, SCN002 and SCN004. |
| State hash | The adapter's `StateHash`: a deterministic hash of the rules state after a recipe. |

## Guarantees and limits

- With an empty or missing `analyzers` section, SCN003 reports nothing; SCN110 still runs.
- SCN003 does not see state changes through public methods or aliases: the hash A/B run and the multiverse do.
- Test assemblies are exempt from SCN110 (those that reference `UnityEngine.TestRunner` in Unity, or `Scion.Testing`
  outside it).
- After editing `ScionSettings.json`, recompile the affected assembly; Unity does not track the file.
- To reach audio, camera or HUD from a graft, call the `Fx` facade instead of the game's systems
  ([Effects with Fx](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/fx/)).

## See also

- [Rules R1-R8](/scion/41664431a8f5/standard/rules/)
- [Core API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/core/)
- [Standard diagnostics](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/standard/)
- [Effects with Fx](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/fx/)

# Build modes

Scion has two kinds of player build. The **test build** (Mono, `SCION_SLOTS` and `SCION_TRIALS`) routes grafts
through slots, accepts injection and runs trials. The **final build** (IL2CPP or Mono, no test defines) calls grafts
directly and contains no lab code. This guide covers the defines, `dotnet scion build test|final`, the editor API
`ScionBuild`, Build Profiles, the guards SCN120 and SCN121, and the `scion-build.json` written next to every build.

## When to use

- Use the test build for everything Scion does at run time: trials, live injection, warm copies, the multiverse.
- Use the final build for players, stores and performance measurements. It is what you ship.
- Rebuild the test build after any change to game code, promoted grafts or `AnchorScope`; the CLI warns with
  `build_stale` when the build is older than the source.

## Steps

### 1. Build the test player

```sh
dotnet scion build test
```

<!-- validate: cli/build -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"build test","ok":true,"channel":"batchmode","seconds":35.2,"build_id":"4c49a1e0b2f3","output":".scion/builds/test/Orchard.app","errors":[],"next_step":"dotnet scion trial run"}
```

The CLI finds the Unity editor of the project and builds in batchmode. With the editor open and the
`com.unity.pipeline` package installed, it builds through the open editor instead; with the editor open and no
pipeline, it stops with [`editor_open`](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/#editor_open).

### 2. Build the final player

```sh
dotnet scion build final
```

The final build uses the project's backend (IL2CPP by default) and refuses any test define.

### 3. Build from your own editor script

```csharp
using Scion.Editor;
using UnityEditor;

public static class OrchardBuilds
{
    [MenuItem("Orchard/Build test player")]
    public static void Test()
    {
        ScionBuild.BuildTestPlayer(new BuildPlayerOptions
        {
            scenes = new[] { "Assets/Orchard/Scenes/Battle.unity" },
            locationPathName = ".scion/builds/test/Orchard.app",
            target = BuildTarget.StandaloneOSX,
        });
    }
}
```

`BuildTestPlayer` forces Mono, adds `ScionBuild.TestDefines` and restores the project's backend and defines in a
`finally`, so a failed build never leaves the project in test mode.

## Reference

### Defines

| Define | Set by | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| none | final build | Call mode: anchors call `__ScionGenerated.D_<id>` directly. No slots, no lab. |
| `SCION_SLOTS` | test build | Slot mode: one delegate field per anchor, `Injection`, the control server. Needs Mono. |
| `SCION_TRIALS` | test build | `Scion.Trials`, the virtual clock and screen, `SeededRandom`, captures. |
| `SCION_NETCLOCK` | you, optional | Moves the Netcode tick onto the virtual clock ([Netcode clock](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/netclock/)). |
| `SCION_VERBOSE` | you, optional | Extra `[Scion]` log lines from the weaver and the session. Off by default. |

Code that uses test-only types sits inside the matching define:

```csharp
#if SCION_TRIALS
TrialSession.Current?.Probe("damage", amount);
#endif
```

`Before`, `After`, `Call`, `Call<T>`, `Anchor`, `AnchorScope`, `Anchors`, `Faults`, `Fx` and `WallClock` exist in
every build. `Scion.Trials`, `Clock`, `VirtualScreen`, `SeededRandom` and `VirtualWaitForSecondsRealtime` need
`SCION_TRIALS`; `Injection` and `InjectReport` need `SCION_SLOTS`.

### Entry points

| Member | Use |
|---|---|
| `ScionBuild.BuildTestPlayer(BuildPlayerOptions)` | Test player from your script. |
| `ScionBuild.BuildFinalPlayer(BuildPlayerOptions)` | Final player; fails with SCN121 on test defines. |
| `ScionBuild.TestFromCommandLine()` | Batchmode: `-executeMethod Scion.Editor.ScionBuild.TestFromCommandLine -scion-build-out <dir> [-scion-build-target osx\|win\|linux]`. |
| `ScionBuild.FinalFromCommandLine()` | The same for the final build. |
| `ScionBuild.FromEditor(mode, outDir)` | Used by the CLI through the open editor; returns the JSON of `build`. |

Batchmode builds print one line the CLI reads: `BUILD_RESULT mono Succeeded errors=0 seconds=35.2`.

### Build Profiles

With Unity Build Profiles, keep one profile for the final build and let Scion build the test player: the test
defines are added only for the duration of `BuildTestPlayer`, never saved into a profile. The scenes come from the
active profile unless `BuildPlayerOptions.scenes` is set.

### What the build writes

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `<out>/<player_name>.app` (or `.exe`) | The player. `player_name` comes from `build.player_name` in `ScionSettings.json`. |
| `<out>/scion-build.json` | Build id, git commit, Unity version, backend, defines, slots and recipe names ([scion-build.json](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/scion-build-json/)). |

`build_id` is the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the main game assembly as built. Injection and baselines use
it to tell builds apart.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SCN120` | 1 | `SCION_SLOTS` on an IL2CPP build. | Build tests with `ScionBuild.BuildTestPlayer` or `dotnet scion build test`. |
| `SCN121` | 1 | Final build with `SCION_SLOTS` or `SCION_TRIALS`. | Remove the test defines or use `BuildFinalPlayer`. |
| `editor_open` | 3 | The editor is open and `com.unity.pipeline` is not installed. | Close the editor or install the pipeline package. |
| `unity_not_found` | 3 | No Unity of the project's version in the Hub path. | Set `unity.editor` in `scion.local.json`. |
| `build_wrong_mode` | 3 | A trials command found a build without `SCION_TRIALS`. | `dotnet scion build test`. |
| `build_stale` | warning | Source changed since the build. | Rebuild before trusting the run. |

## Examples

### Build into another folder

```sh
dotnet scion build test --out /tmp/orchard-test
dotnet scion trial run --build /tmp/orchard-test/Orchard.app
```

### Build in CI without the CLI

```sh
"$UNITY" -batchmode -quit -projectPath . -executeMethod Scion.Editor.ScionBuild.TestFromCommandLine -scion-build-out .scion/builds/test
```

## See also

- [build test, build final](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/build/)
- [Editor API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/editor/)
- [scion-build.json](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/scion-build-json/)
- [SCN120-SCN131](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/builds-and-injection/)

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Live injection

Injection loads a graft DLL compiled outside Unity into a running Mono test build and swaps the slots of the anchors
it targets. This guide covers `dotnet scion graft build` (compiles drafts against the build's `Managed/*.dll`),
`graft inject --to all|<pid> [--isolate]`, `graft restore`, `graft disable <slot>`, the pending state until the next
recipe boundary, `Injection.Version`, `InjectReport`, and `trial run --grafts <dll>` for injection at startup.
Errors: SCN113, SCN130, SCN131.

## When to use

- Use live injection to iterate on a draft graft in seconds, without a Unity rebuild.
- Use `trial run --grafts` to compare recipes with and without a draft in a cold run.
- Promote and rebuild when the draft is done: runs with injected grafts cannot be approved as baselines.

## Before you begin

- A test build (`dotnet scion build test`).
- Running copies with a control channel: warm copies (`dotnet scion trial serve -j 2`) or a game you started with
  `-scion-control 0`.
- Drafts in `scion/grafts/` (`grafts.staging` in `scion.json`).

## Steps

### 1. Compile the drafts against the build

```sh
dotnet scion graft build
```

<!-- validate: cli/graft-build -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"graft build","ok":true,"dll":".scion/grafts/ScionGrafts_51c2.dll","build_id":"4c49a1e0b2f3","abi":1,"grafts":["Orchard.Grafts.CritShake.After"],"seconds":1.9,"diagnostics":[],"next_step":"dotnet scion graft inject --to all"}
```

The build compiles every file in `scion/grafts/` with Roslyn and the test defines, references the build's
`Managed/*.dll`, and generates the dispatcher code the weaver would. The DLL records the target `build_id` and the
weaver `AbiVersion`.

### 2. Inject it into the running copies

```sh
dotnet scion graft inject --to all
```

<!-- validate: cli/graft-inject -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"graft inject","ok":true,"dll":".scion/grafts/ScionGrafts_51c2.dll","copies":[{"pid":4242,"version":3,"ok":true,"pending":false,"bound":["A__Orchard_Presentation_HitPresenter__Play__HitEvent"],"errors":[],"recycle":false},{"pid":4243,"version":3,"ok":true,"pending":true,"bound":["A__Orchard_Presentation_HitPresenter__Play__HitEvent"],"errors":[],"recycle":false}],"next_step":"dotnet scion trial run --warm SlashHit"}
```

A copy in the middle of a recipe answers `pending: true` and applies the swap at the next recipe boundary, so one
recipe never mixes two versions of a graft.

### 3. Run and look

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --warm SlashHit
```

### 4. Undo

```sh
dotnet scion graft restore               # every slot back to the promoted grafts
dotnet scion graft disable A__Orchard_Presentation_HitPresenter__Play__HitEvent   # empty one slot
```

## Reference

### Merge or isolate

| Mode | What one anchor runs after the injection |
|---|---|
| Default (merge) | The promoted grafts plus the injected ones. An injected graft with the same identity (`Orchard.Grafts.CritShake.After`) replaces the promoted one. Order: observers, `Priority`, full name. |
| `--isolate` | Only the injected grafts of the DLL, for the anchors the DLL touches. |

### Commands

| Command | Use |
|---|---|
| `graft build [files]` | Compile drafts (all of `scion/grafts/` by default) into `.scion/grafts/ScionGrafts_<hash>.dll`. |
| `graft inject [--to all\|<pid>] [--isolate] [--dll <file>]` | Send the DLL to copies (default `all` live copies of this build). Builds first when the drafts changed. |
| `graft restore [--to ...]` | Every slot back to the promoted grafts. |
| `graft disable <slot> [--to ...]` | Empty one slot, promoted grafts included. |
| `trial run --grafts <dll>` | Inject at startup into cold copies (`-scion-inject`). |

### From code

Inside `#if SCION_SLOTS`:

```csharp
InjectReport r = Injection.Inject("/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/grafts/ScionGrafts_51c2.dll");
if (!r.Ok) foreach (var e in r.Errors) Debug.LogWarning(e);   // "SCN113: ..."
Injection.Applied += report => Debug.Log(report.ToJson());
Injection.Restore();
Injection.Disable("A__Orchard_Presentation_HitPresenter__Play__HitEvent");
```

`Injection.Version` counts applied loads; it is the `grafts` column of `results.tsv`, so a run shows which recipes ran
with injected code.

### Rules

- An injected graft must be `public`, in a `public` type: it lives in another assembly.
- Its target must have a slot in this build: a promoted graft on it, or an `AnchorScope` that covers it (SCN113).
- A DLL built for another `build_id` is refused (SCN130); a DLL of another ABI is refused (SCN131).
- Mono never unloads assemblies. After 50 injections `InjectReport.Recycle` is true and `trial serve` restarts that
  copy at the next boundary.
- A run with injected grafts cannot be approved as a baseline: promote the graft and rebuild.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SCN113` | 1 | The target has no slot in this build. | Add its type to `AnchorScope`, rebuild, inject again. |
| `SCN130` | 1 | The DLL targets another build. | `dotnet scion graft build` against this build. |
| `SCN131` | 1 | The DLL has another weaver ABI. | Use the same Scion version for the CLI and the build. |
| `no_copies` | 3 | No live copy of this build answers. | `dotnet scion trial serve -j 2`. |
| `not_supported` | 3 | The copy was built without `SCION_SLOTS`. | Use a test build. |

## Examples

### Isolate one draft in one copy

```sh
dotnet scion graft inject --to 4242 --isolate
```

### Compare with and without a draft in cold runs

```sh
dotnet scion trial run SlashHit --rounds 2
dotnet scion trial run SlashHit --rounds 2 --grafts .scion/grafts/ScionGrafts_51c2.dll
dotnet scion trial diff 20261011-143200 20261011-143512 SlashHit
```

## See also

- [graft (CLI)](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/graft/)
- [Warm copies](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/warm-copies/)
- [Injection API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/injection/)
- [InjectReport JSON](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/inject-report/)
- [Control protocol](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/control-protocol/)

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# From draft to final build

Every graft goes through the same path: a **draft** in `scion/grafts/` (`grafts.staging`), checked without Unity,
injected or run against the test build, approved through its trials, then **promoted** into the game's grafts
folder (`grafts.promoted`) and compiled into the final build in call mode. This guide walks the path with
`graft new`, `graft check`, `graft inject`, `trial run`, `trial approve`, `graft promote` and the save loop
`graft watch`.

## When to use

- Follow it for every new graft: the draft stage is where agents and people iterate without touching the game.
- Use `graft watch` while tuning: every save rebuilds, injects and replays the recipe.
- Skip the draft stage only for trivial grafts; the trials and the approval still apply.

## Before you begin

- `scion.json` names both folders:

```json
{"schema_version":1,"grafts":{"promoted":"Assets/Orchard/Grafts","staging":"scion/grafts"}}
```

- A test build and warm copies (`dotnet scion build test`, `dotnet scion trial serve -j 2`).

## Steps

### 1. Create the draft

```sh
dotnet scion graft new DamageNumberPop --after Orchard.Presentation.DamageNumbers.Spawn
```

The file `scion/grafts/DamageNumberPop.cs` has the right signature and a body to fill in.

### 2. Check it without Unity

```sh
dotnet scion graft check scion/grafts/DamageNumberPop.cs
```

<!-- validate: cli/graft-check -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"graft check","ok":true,"files":1,"diagnostics":[],"errors":0,"warnings_count":0,"next_step":"dotnet scion graft inject --to all"}
```

### 3. Try it live

```sh
dotnet scion graft inject --to all
dotnet scion trial run --warm SlashHit FireballArea
```

### 4. Run the cold trials with the draft

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --grafts .scion/grafts/ScionGrafts_51c2.dll
```

The state hash of every recipe must stay the same (grafts are visual); images may change.

### 5. Promote

```sh
dotnet scion graft promote DamageNumberPop
```

<!-- validate: cli/graft-promote -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"graft promote","ok":true,"name":"DamageNumberPop","from":"scion/grafts/DamageNumberPop.cs","to":"Assets/Orchard/Grafts/DamageNumberPop.cs","staged":true,"next_step":"dotnet scion build test && dotnet scion trial run --changed"}
```

`promote` moves the file (with `git mv` when it is tracked), keeps the namespace and stages it. In slot mode the
weaver records every promoted graft as `[assembly: ScionPromoted(id, graft, priority, wrapper)]`, which `anchor list`
reads.

### 6. Rebuild and approve

```sh
dotnet scion build test
dotnet scion trial run
dotnet scion trial approve --changed --reason "damage numbers pop on spawn"
```

Approving `changed` needs a person at an interactive terminal ([Baselines and approval](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/baselines/)).

### 7. Ship

```sh
dotnet scion build final
```

The final build calls the promoted graft directly, with no slot and no lab code.

## Reference

### The stages

| Stage | Where | Compiled by | Runs in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | `scion/grafts/` | `graft build` (Roslyn, outside Unity) | Test builds, through injection |
| Promoted | `Assets/Orchard/Grafts/` (with the `.asmref`) | Unity and the weaver | Test builds (slots) and final builds (direct calls) |

### graft watch

```sh
dotnet scion graft watch --recipe SlashHit
```

On every save under `scion/grafts/`: `graft build`, `graft inject --to all`, `trial run --warm SlashHit`. It prints one
JSON line per cycle and stops on Ctrl-C. With `trial loop` running, each injection applies on the next pass of the
loop ([The live loop](/scion/41664431a8f5/explore/live-loop/)).

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SCN101`-`SCN112` | 1 | `graft check` found a weaver or analyzer error. | Fix the file at `file:line`. |
| `SCN113` | 1 | The draft's target has no slot in this build. | Add an `AnchorScope`, rebuild, inject again. |
| `no_match` | 2 | `graft promote` found no draft with that name. | Use `did_you_mean`. |
| `human_required` | 2 | An agent tried to approve `changed`. | Ask a person to approve at a terminal. |

## Examples

### Check a draft on every edit from an agent hook

```sh
dotnet scion graft check --hook
```

See [Hooks](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/hooks/).

### Preview a promotion

```sh
dotnet scion graft promote DamageNumberPop --dry-run
```

## See also

- [graft (CLI)](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/graft/)
- [Live injection](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/injection/)
- [Baselines and approval](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/baselines/)
- [The live loop](/scion/41664431a8f5/explore/live-loop/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# When a graft throws

A graft is code, and code throws. In slot mode (test builds) the dispatcher wraps each graft in its own `try/catch`:
the throwing graft is disabled alone, the exception goes to `Faults.Report`, the game keeps running and the current
recipe fails. In call mode (final builds) nothing is caught: the exception propagates like any other. This guide
covers both, the `Faults.Reported` event and the `fault` line in `telemetry.jsonl`.

## When to use

- Read this when a recipe fails with `graft <source> threw <Type>: <message>`.
- Subscribe to `Faults.Reported` when your own tool (a debug overlay, a crash reporter in test builds) must know.

## Steps

### 1. Read the failure

```text
SlashHit r1: graft Orchard.Grafts.CritShake.After threw NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object.
```

The recipe's `telemetry.jsonl` has the line:

```json
{"f":14,"t":1.467,"kind":"fault","source":"Orchard.Grafts.CritShake.After","type":"NullReferenceException","msg":"Object reference not set to an instance of an object."}
```

and `log.txt` has the stack.

### 2. Fix and inject again

A disabled graft comes back only when its slot is injected or restored:

```sh
dotnet scion graft inject --to all
```

### 3. Listen from your own code

```csharp
Faults.Reported += (source, e) => DebugOverlay.Show($"{source}: {e.Message}");
```

## Reference

| | Slot mode (test build) | Call mode (final build) |
|---|---|---|
| A graft throws | Caught per graft | Propagates to the caller |
| Other grafts of the anchor | Keep running | Do not run (the exception unwinds) |
| The anchor's body | Runs | Does not run if a before threw |
| The graft afterwards | Disabled for the rest of the process | Runs again on the next call |
| Report | `Faults.Report(source, e)`: a `[Scion]` warning and `Faults.Reported` | None |
| Trials | The recipe fails; `fault` in telemetry | Not applicable |

`source` is the graft's full name as `Namespace.Type.Method` (`+` between nested types). Handlers run on the thread
that reported; an exception thrown by a handler is caught and logged. `Faults.Report` is public so your own
dispatchers can use the same channel.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| recipe error `graft <source> threw <Type>` | 1 | A graft threw during the recipe. | Fix the graft; read `log.txt` for the stack. |

## Examples

### Count faults in a soak test

```csharp
int faults = 0;
Faults.Reported += (_, _) => faults++;
// ... play ...
TrialSession.Current?.Check(faults == 0, "no graft faults");
```

### Report a fault from your own code

```csharp
try { RunCustomEffect(); }
catch (Exception e) { Faults.Report("Orchard.Presentation.CustomEffect", e); }
```

## See also

- [Grafts API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/grafts/)
- [Build modes](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/build-modes/)
- [telemetry.jsonl](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/telemetry-jsonl/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Effects with Fx

`Fx` is the facade grafts use for presentation: `Fx.Sound`, `Fx.Shake`, `Fx.Text`, `Fx.Flash`, `Fx.HitStop`,
`Fx.Vfx` and `Fx.Mark`. The game implements them once in an `IFxSink` registered at boot; Trials records every call
in `telemetry.jsonl` with the graft that made it (`by`); tests replace the sink with `FxRecorder`. Grafts never
reach the game's audio, camera or HUD systems directly, so they stay visual, testable and portable.

## When to use

- Use `Fx` for any effect a graft triggers.
- Call the game's own presentation code from a graft only for things `Fx` does not cover, and keep it visual.

## Steps

### 1. Implement the sink

```csharp
using Scion;
using UnityEngine;

namespace Orchard.Presentation
{
    public sealed class OrchardFxSink : IFxSink
    {
        public void Sound(string id, Vector3? at, float volume) => AudioBank.Play(id, at, volume);
        public void Shake(float amount) => CameraRig.Current.Shake(amount);
        public void Text(string text, Vector3 at, Color color, float seconds, int size, string icon) =>
            FloatingText.Spawn(text, at, color, seconds, size, icon);
        public void Flash(Component target, Color color, float seconds) => SpriteFlash.On(target, color, seconds);
        public void HitStop(float seconds) => TimeFreeze.For(seconds);
        public void Vfx(string id, Vector3 at, float scale) => VfxPool.Play(id, at, scale);
        public void Mark(string label) { }
    }
}
```

### 2. Register it at boot

```csharp
[RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(RuntimeInitializeLoadType.BeforeSceneLoad)]
static void InstallFx() => Fx.Sink = new OrchardFxSink();
```

### 3. Call Fx from grafts

```csharp
[After(typeof(HitPresenter), nameof(HitPresenter.Play))]
public static void After(HitPresenter presenter, HitEvent e)
{
    Fx.Sound(e.Crit ? "hit_crit" : "hit", presenter.transform.position);
    Fx.Text(e.Amount.ToString(), presenter.TargetPosition, e.Crit ? Color.yellow : Color.white);
}
```

## Reference

### Verbs

| Verb | Signature | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Sound` | `(string id, Vector3? at = null, float volume = 1f)` | Play a sound by id, optionally positioned. |
| `Shake` | `(float amount)` | Shake the camera, 0 to 1. |
| `Text` | `(string text, Vector3 at, Color color, float seconds = 1.1f, int size = 12, string icon = null)` | Floating text. |
| `Flash` | `(Component target, Color color, float seconds)` | Tint a target briefly. |
| `HitStop` | `(float seconds)` | Freeze presentation briefly. |
| `Vfx` | `(string id, Vector3 at, float scale = 1f)` | Spawn an effect by id. |
| `Mark` | `(string label)` | A mark in the capture timeline (`frames.tsv`, `IMPACT`). |

`IFxSink` has one method per verb with the same parameters and no defaults. With no sink, every verb does nothing.

### What Trials records

In test builds Trials decorates the sink. Every call writes one line to `telemetry.jsonl` and then calls your sink:

```json
{"f":14,"t":1.467,"kind":"fx","verb":"Shake","args":[0.3],"by":"Orchard.Grafts.CritShake.After"}
```

`by` is `Fx.Source`, written by the slot dispatcher around each graft; calls from game code have `"by": null`.
`Fx.Mark` also adds the label to the frame's `marks` column, like `TrialSession.Mark`.

### Rules for the sink

- Keep it thin: map the verb to the game's system and return.
- Do not change rule state in it: it runs from grafts, which are visual.
- Use ids, not asset references, so recipes, telemetry and tests can name the effect.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| none from `Fx` | | A missing sink makes every verb a no-op. | Register `Fx.Sink` at boot; check with `Fx.Sink != null`. |

## Examples

### A heal number

```csharp
[After(typeof(DamageNumbers), nameof(DamageNumbers.SpawnHeal))]
public static void After(DamageNumbers numbers, int amount, Vector3 at) =>
    Fx.Text("+" + amount, at, new Color(0.4f, 1f, 0.5f), size: 14, icon: "leaf");
```

### Assert an effect in a recipe

```csharp
protected override void Checks(TrialChecks c) => c.Marked("IMPACT").ProbeIs("shake_calls", v => v >= 1, "crit shakes");
```

## See also

- [Fx API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/fx/)
- [Test grafts without Unity](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/testing/)
- [Telemetry, probes and sensors](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/telemetry/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Test grafts without Unity

A graft is a static method, so it can be tested like one: call it with arguments and a `Call<T>`, and record its
effects with `FxRecorder`. The `Scion.Testing` NuGet package brings `Scion.Runtime` compiled for .NET, `FxRecorder`
and `FxCall`, so a plain `dotnet test` project tests grafts in milliseconds, without Unity and without a license.

## When to use

- Use unit tests for the graft's logic: which effects it calls, with which arguments, and how it changes the result.
- Use trials for what the player sees: timing, pixels, the state hash.

## Before you begin

- .NET 10 SDK.
- The grafts and the types they use compile outside Unity (only `UnityEngine` value types such as `Vector3` and
  `Color` are provided by `Scion.Testing`). Grafts that read a `MonoBehaviour` take `null` as the instance in tests.

## Steps

### 1. Create the test project

```sh
dotnet new xunit -o Tests/Orchard.Grafts.Tests
dotnet add Tests/Orchard.Grafts.Tests package Scion.Testing --version 1.0.0
```

Link the graft sources into the project:

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Include="../../Assets/Orchard/Grafts/*.cs" />
  <Compile Include="../../Assets/Orchard/Core/HitEvent.cs" />
</ItemGroup>
```

### 2. Write the test

```csharp
using Orchard.Core;
using Orchard.Grafts;
using Scion;
using Scion.Testing;
using Xunit;

public class CritShakeTests
{
    [Fact]
    public void Crit_shakes_and_lengthens_the_hit()
    {
        var fx = new FxRecorder();
        Fx.Sink = fx;
        var c = new Call<float>(0.5f);

        CritShake.After(null, new HitEvent(attacker: 0, target: 1, amount: 9, crit: true), ref c);

        Assert.Equal(0.56f, c.Result, 3);
        Assert.Contains(fx.Calls, x => x.Verb == "Shake" && (float)x.Args[0] == CritShake.Strength);
    }
}
```

### 3. Run it

```sh
dotnet test Tests/Orchard.Grafts.Tests
```

## Reference

| Member | Use |
|---|---|
| `new Call<T>(T result)` | A context whose `Result` starts at `result`, as the target returned it. |
| `new Call()` | A context for void targets. `Skipped` reads false until a graft calls `Skip()`. |
| `FxRecorder.Calls` | Every `Fx` call in order: `Verb`, `Args`, `Source`. |
| `FxRecorder.Clear()` | Forget the recorded calls. |
| `Clock.Advance(delta)` | Move the virtual clock in tests that read `Time`. |

The weaver does not run in `dotnet test`: the test calls the graft method directly, so the order between grafts and
`Priority` are not exercised. Trials cover that.

Test assemblies that reference `Scion.Testing` are exempt from SCN110, so tests may call grafts.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SCN110` | compile error | A non-test assembly calls a graft. | Reference `Scion.Testing` in the test project, or move the call into a test. |

## Examples

### A skip in a Before

```csharp
var c = new Call();
ReplayMode.Active = true;
TurnBanner.Before(null, 3, ref c);
Assert.True(c.Skipped);
```

### No effect on a normal hit

```csharp
var fx = new FxRecorder(); Fx.Sink = fx;
var c = new Call<float>(0.5f);
CritShake.After(null, new HitEvent(0, 1, 4, crit: false), ref c);
Assert.Empty(fx.Calls);
Assert.Equal(0.5f, c.Result);
```

## See also

- [Testing API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/testing/)
- [Effects with Fx](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/fx/)
- [Call and Call\<T\>](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/call-context/)

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Tunables and presets

A tunable is a static numeric field marked `[Tunable(min, max)]`: a number someone will want to tune, such as a shake
strength, a hit-stop length or a damage multiplier. Scion lists every tunable (`dotnet scion gen --list tunables`),
lets recipes and runs override them (`tunable:CritShake.Strength`), saves sets of values as **feel presets** in
`scion/presets/`, blends presets, and adds the values of rule tunables to the lobby hash so co-op peers agree.
SCN005 reports a numeric tunable without a range.

## When to use

- Use `[Tunable]` on every number in a graft or the core that someone will tune by eye or by search.
- Use presets to keep named feels (`heavy`, `snappy`) and compare them in trials and judge duels.
- Use guided search when the space is too big to tune by hand ([Guided search](/scion/41664431a8f5/explore/guided-search/)).

## Steps

### 1. Declare the tunable

```csharp
public static class CritShake
{
    [Tunable(0f, 1f, Doc = "Camera shake on a critical hit.")]
    public static float Strength = 0.3f;

    [Tunable(0f, 0.2f, Doc = "Hit-stop on a critical hit, in seconds.")]
    public static float Stop = 0.06f;
}
```

A tunable is a `static` field of type `int`, `float`, `double` or `bool`. Numeric tunables need a range; `bool`
tunables take none.

### 2. Override it in a recipe

```csharp
public sealed class SlashHitFeel : SlashHit
{
    protected override IEnumerable<TrialArgs> Variants()
    {
        yield return new TrialArgs { { "tunable:CritShake.Strength", 0.3f } };
        yield return new TrialArgs { { "tunable:CritShake.Strength", 0.8f }, { "tunable:CritShake.Stop", 0.1f } };
    }
}
```

### 3. Override it for one run

```sh
dotnet scion trial run SlashHit --set tunable:CritShake.Strength=0.8
```

### 4. Save and use a preset

`scion/presets/heavy.json`:

<!-- validate: preset -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"name":"heavy","description":"Slow, weighty hits.","tunables":{"CritShake.Strength":0.8,"CritShake.Stop":0.1,"HitFlash.Seconds":0.12}}
```

```sh
dotnet scion trial run SlashHit --preset heavy
dotnet scion trial run SlashHit --preset "base + 0.7 heavy + 0.3 snappy"
```

## Reference

### Names

A tunable's name is `<Type>.<Field>` with the type's simple name (`CritShake.Strength`). When two types share a
simple name, use the full name (`Orchard.Grafts.CritShake.Strength`). In recipe arguments and `--set`, prefix it with
`tunable:`.

### Order of overrides

From weakest to strongest: the field's initial value, the preset, the recipe's arguments, `--set`. A value outside
the range is clamped and reported as a warning in `result.json`.

### Blends

`base + 0.7 heavy + 0.3 snappy` computes, for each tunable, `base + 0.7 × (heavy − base) + 0.3 × (snappy − base)`,
clamped to the range. `base` is the initial values. `bool` tunables take the value of the heaviest preset that sets
them. Weights are decimals with a dot.

### Rule tunables

Tunables declared in a rule assembly (`analyzers.rule_assemblies`) change rules, so every peer must have the same
values. Their values enter `Tunables.LobbyHash`, which the game compares when a client joins; a host and a client
with different rule tunables refuse to play. Presentation tunables (in grafts) stay local to each machine.

### Listing

```sh
dotnet scion gen --list tunables
```

prints every tunable with its type, range, default and doc, and `scion gen` writes them into
`scion.manifest.json` ([gen](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/gen/)).

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SCN005` | compile warning | A numeric `[Tunable]` without a range. | `[Tunable(min, max)]`. |
| `bad_value` | 2 | `--set` names an unknown tunable or a value of the wrong type. | Use `gen --list tunables`; read `did_you_mean`. |
| `no_match` | 2 | `--preset` names a file that does not exist in `scion/presets/`. | List `scion/presets/`. |

## Examples

### A rule tunable in the core

```csharp
namespace Orchard.Core
{
    public static class Balance
    {
        [Tunable(500, 2000, Doc = "Critical damage multiplier, in permille.")]
        public static int CritPermille = 1500;
    }
}
```

### Compare three feels side by side

```sh
dotnet scion trial run SlashHit --variants base,heavy,snappy --mosaic 3
```

## See also

- [Core API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/core/)
- [Taste heads and feel presets](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/presets/)
- [Guided search](/scion/41664431a8f5/explore/guided-search/)
- [gen](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/gen/)
