> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# How trials work

Trials are Scion's automated test lab. A **recipe** describes one situation to play (a slash at 3 tiles, a co-op
turn, a HUD state); the game's **adapter** knows how to play it; the **test build** of the game plays a queue of
recipes headless and writes captures, telemetry and a verdict for each. The CLI launches N copies of that one build
in parallel, splits the queue between them and compares every result with the approved **baseline**.

## How it works

![Diagram: dotnet scion trial run starts three copies of the test build; each plays its shard of the queue and writes its folder; the CLI compares the results with scion/baselines and writes summary.json.](../../../assets/diagrams/run-flow.svg)

### One build, many copies

There is no special test scene and no test runner: the test build is the game, compiled with `SCION_SLOTS` and
`SCION_TRIALS`. Started with `-scion-trials`, it creates a `TrialSession`, discovers every `TrialRecipe` class,
picks an adapter for each, plays the queue and, with `-scion-quit`, exits with a code (0 ok, 1 a recipe failed,
2 usage, 3 environment).

`dotnet scion trial run` does the orchestration:

1. reads `scion.json`, finds the test build and checks it was built in the right mode;
2. starts `-j N` copies (default: the `doctor` suggestion from cores and free memory), each with `-scion-shard i/N`
   and its own `q<i>/` folder;
3. waits for them, with a watchdog for copies that stop making progress;
4. compares each (recipe, round) with `scion/baselines/` and writes `summary.json`, `summary.tsv` and `compare.json`;
5. prints a short JSON with the counts, the failures, the changes and the `next_step`.

### Recipes, rounds and shards

Each recipe expands into one or more **ids** (variants, modes and seeds). The queue is every (id, round) pair; a
shard `i/n` plays exactly the pairs assigned to it, round-robin over (round, id). Rounds of the same id in one
process are compared with each other: the same state hash every round is the first determinism check.

### Captures

During a recipe the adapter marks a **cut** (`BeginCut`/`EndCut`): every frame rendered in the cut is hashed and
can be saved. The session writes `window.png` (up to 12 frames around the impact), `context.png` (6 frames across
the cut), named stills and, for static trials, `sheet.png`. Capture is offscreen and works in `-batchmode`; time is
virtual, so the same recipe gives the same frames on any machine.

### Verdicts

| Verdict | Meaning | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `same` | Hash, frame count and images match the baseline. | 0 |
| `within` | Images differ but inside the tolerance. | 0 |
| `px_changed` | Hash and frames match; pixel hashes differ and the recipe compares no images. Informative. | 0 |
| `changed` | Hash, frame count (beyond ±1) or images outside the tolerance differ. | 0 (it is a review signal, not a failure) |
| `new` | No `baseline.json` for this id. | 0 |
| `stale` | The baseline is for another platform, fps, Unity or player args; images are suspended, the hash still counts. | 0 |

A recipe that fails (timeout, `Fail`, a check, an error in the log, a graft that threw) exits 1 whatever its verdict.

### The adapter is the only game-specific code

Everything above is generic. The game writes recipes (data) and one or more adapters (how to load a scene, start a
battle, issue a command, read a state hash). The more the game follows the [Scion Standard](/scion/41664431a8f5/standard/overview/),
the thinner the adapter.

## Key terms

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Recipe | A `TrialRecipe` subclass: the data of one situation. |
| Id | One concrete instance of a recipe: `SlashHit`, `SlashHit[Distance=3]@360p#7`. |
| Adapter | The game's `TrialAdapter<TRecipe>` that plays recipes of a type. |
| Round | One play of an id; `--rounds 2` plays every id twice. |
| Copy | One process of the test build. |
| Shard | The share `i/n` of the queue one copy plays. |
| Group | The copies that play one co-op recipe together (a host and its clients). |
| Run | One `trial run`: a folder under `trials.out` named by its start time. |
| Cut | The frames between `BeginCut` and `EndCut`. |
| Baseline | The approved hash, frames and images of an id, in `scion/baselines/`. |

## Guarantees and limits

- The same build, recipe and seed give the same state hash on every machine and every round; frame counts may differ
  by one until the Netcode clock is virtual ([Netcode clock](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/netclock/)).
- Copies never write into each other's folders; the CLI never writes inside a copy's folder.
- Images are compared per platform (OS, graphics API, size, capture); the hash is compared everywhere.
- A copy that makes no progress for 120 seconds of real time is ended (`watchdog`, exit 3).
- Runs beyond `trials.keep_runs` (default 10) are deleted at the start of the next run.

## See also

- [Quickstart](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/quickstart/)
- [Write a recipe](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/recipes/)
- [Write an adapter](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/adapters/)
- [Baselines and approval](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/baselines/)
- [trial run](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/trial-run/)

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Write a recipe

A recipe is data: a `TrialRecipe` subclass whose constructor sets what to play and how to capture it. The session
creates one instance of every concrete recipe class through its public parameterless constructor (SCN201). This
guide covers the members (`Name`, `Id`, `Variant`, `Tags`, `Description`, `Seed`, `Fps`, `TailSeconds`,
`TimeoutSeconds`, `Players`, `Explicit`, `Control`, `Tolerance`), the overrides (`Checks`, `Setup`, `Variants`,
`Mask`), cutting the capture by event, and recipes compiled outside Unity with `--recipes`.

## When to use

- Write one recipe per situation a person would want to look at after a change: one hit, one ability, one turn,
  one screen.
- Keep recipes short (a few seconds of game time): many short recipes parallelize better than one long one.
- Put the fields every recipe of the game shares in one base class, played by one adapter.

## Before you begin

- An assembly for trials code with `defineConstraints: ["SCION_TRIALS"]`, so it only compiles into test builds
  (`Orchard.Trials`), or `#if SCION_TRIALS` around the code.
- An adapter for the recipe's base type ([Write an adapter](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/adapters/)).

## Steps

### 1. A base type with the game's fields

```csharp
using Scion.Trials;

namespace Orchard.Trials
{
    public abstract class OrchardRecipe : TrialRecipe
    {
        public string Attacker = "knight";
        public string Defender = "skeleton";
        public int DefenderHp = 20;
        public int Distance = 1;
        public string Ability = "slash";
    }
}
```

### 2. One recipe

```csharp
namespace Orchard.Trials
{
    public sealed class SlashHit : OrchardRecipe
    {
        public SlashHit()
        {
            Description = "The knight slashes a skeleton next to it.";
            Tags = new[] { "combat", "melee" };
            Seed = 7;
            TailSeconds = 1f;
        }

        protected override void Checks(TrialChecks c) =>
            c.Marked("IMPACT").Frames(20, 90).ProbeIs("damage", d => d > 0, "the slash deals damage");
    }
}
```

### 3. Cut the capture around the action

The adapter decides when the interesting part starts and ends:

```csharp
session.BeginCut();                 // frames from here on are captured
battle.Issue(Command.Attack(recipe.Ability, target));
yield return session.WaitUntil(() => battle.Idle, "attack finished");
yield return session.WaitSeconds(recipe.TailSeconds);
session.EndCut();
```

The moment that matters is marked from a trials-only observer graft, so `window.png` centers on it:

```csharp
[Before(typeof(HitPresenter), nameof(HitPresenter.Play), Observe = true)]
public static void Before(HitPresenter presenter, HitEvent e) => TrialSession.Current?.MarkImpact();
```

### 4. List and run it

```sh
dotnet scion trial list
dotnet scion trial run SlashHit --rounds 2
```

## Reference

### Members

| Member | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Name` | `string`, virtual get | class name | What `--only` patterns match; the base of `Id`. |
| `Id` | `string`, set by the session | `Name` | The instance id, with variant, mode and seed: `SlashHit[Distance=3]@360p#7`. |
| `Variant` | `string`, set by the session | `null` | The variant arguments, `Distance=3`. |
| `Mode` | `string`, set by the session | `null` | The mode, `360p`. |
| `Tags` | `IReadOnlyList<string>`, protected set | empty | Labels for `--tag` filters. |
| `Description` | `string`, protected set | `null` | One line: what the recipe shows. |
| `Seed` | `int`, protected set | 1 | Seeds `UnityEngine.Random` and `SeededRandom` at the start of the recipe. |
| `Fps` | `int`, protected set | 30 | Capture rate; game time advances exactly `1/Fps` per frame. |
| `TailSeconds` | `float`, protected set | 0.5 | Game seconds to keep capturing after the action; the adapter uses it. |
| `TimeoutSeconds` | `float`, protected set | 30 | Limit for `Run`, in game seconds. |
| `Players` | `int`, protected set | 1 | 1 to 4; co-op recipes run in groups ([Co-op trials](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/coop/)). |
| `Explicit` | `bool`, protected set | `false` | Runs only when a pattern names its exact `Id` or `Name`. |
| `Control` | `DeterminismControl`, protected set | `All` | What the session makes deterministic ([Particles, animators, UI and physics](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/control/)). |
| `Tolerance` | `ImageTolerance`, protected set | `ImageTolerance.Default` | Image comparison; `null` compares no images ([Image comparison](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/image-comparison/)). |
| `Checks(TrialChecks c)` | protected virtual | none | Declares checks ([Checks](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/checks/)). |
| `Setup()` | protected virtual | none | Runs after variant arguments are applied. |
| `Variants()` | protected virtual | `null` | Yields `TrialArgs`, one per variant ([Variants, modes and seeds](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/variants/)). |
| `Mask(artifact, rect, why)` | protected | | A region image comparison ignores, in normalized coordinates. |

`Seed` is per recipe; `TrialSession.RunSeed` (`--seed`) is per run, and the adapter maps it to the game's world
seed, so another run seed tries another world with the same recipes.

### Recipes from a DLL

Recipes compiled outside Unity load at startup:

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --recipes scion/recipes/bin/Orchard.Recipes.dll
```

The DLL references the game's assemblies from the build's `Managed/` folder. A recipe whose `Name` equals a
built-in one replaces it, so a new or changed recipe never needs a game rebuild. `trial list` also lists the
sources in `scion/recipes/` (`trials.recipes_staging`).

### Recipes that must not run by default

Set `Explicit = true` for recipes that fail on purpose (to test a check), take minutes, or need a special machine.
They run only when named: `dotnet scion trial run KnightFallsSlow`.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SCN201` | 1 (selected) or log warning | The recipe has no public parameterless constructor. | Add `public SlashHit() { ... }`. |
| `no_match` | 2 | No recipe matches the pattern. | Use `did_you_mean`, or `trial list`. |
| recipe error `timeout (30s): <what>` | 1 | `Run` passed `TimeoutSeconds`. | Read the `what`; raise the timeout only if the game really needs it. |

## Examples

### Three attackers

```csharp
public sealed class FireballArea : OrchardRecipe
{
    public FireballArea()
    {
        Attacker = "mage"; Ability = "fireball"; Distance = 4;
        Description = "A fireball hits three skeletons in an area.";
        Tags = new[] { "combat", "area" };
    }
    protected override void Checks(TrialChecks c) => c.Marked("IMPACT", atLeast: 3);
}
```

### A unit going down

```csharp
public sealed class KnightFalls : OrchardRecipe
{
    public KnightFalls()
    {
        Attacker = "skeleton"; Defender = "knight"; DefenderHp = 3;
        Description = "A skeleton finishes a wounded knight.";
    }
    protected override void Checks(TrialChecks c) => c.Order("IMPACT", "unit_down").ProbeIs("defender_hp", hp => hp == 0, "the knight falls");
}
```

## See also

- [Write an adapter](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/adapters/)
- [TrialSession](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/session/)
- [Checks](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/checks/)
- [Recipes API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/recipes/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Write an adapter

The adapter is the game's only Trials-specific code: it prepares the game once, plays each recipe (load, set up,
act, wait), cleans up and reports a hash of the rules state. Derive from `TrialAdapter<TRecipe>` and register it with
`[assembly: TrialAdapter(typeof(...))]`. This guide covers `Prepare`, `Run`, `Teardown`, `StateHash`, how a recipe
picks its adapter, the coroutine rules, and the reset and seeding every adapter must do. Errors: SCN202, SCN203.

## When to use

- Write one adapter per family of recipes that start the same way: battles, HUD screens, menus.
- Use `ITrialAdapter` directly only when the choice depends on something other than the recipe's type.
- For screens and items that need no action, derive recipes from `StaticTrial<TItem>` and skip the adapter
  entirely ([Static trials](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/static-trials/)).

## Steps

### 1. Write the adapter

```csharp
using System.Collections;
using Orchard.Core;
using Orchard.Runtime;
using Scion.Trials;

[assembly: TrialAdapter(typeof(Orchard.Trials.OrchardAdapter))]

namespace Orchard.Trials
{
    public sealed class OrchardAdapter : TrialAdapter<OrchardRecipe>
    {
        string hash;
        public override string StateHash => hash;

        public override IEnumerator Prepare(TrialSession s)
        {
            s.Sensor("state", () => Battle.Current?.State.Hash64 ?? 0L);
            s.Sensor("tick", () => Battle.Current?.State.Tick ?? 0L);
            yield return s.WaitUntil(() => Boot.Ready, "boot scene loaded");
        }

        protected override IEnumerator Run(OrchardRecipe r, TrialSession s)
        {
            hash = null;
            var battle = Battle.Start(new BattleSetup(r.Attacker, r.Defender, r.DefenderHp, r.Distance, seed: s.RunSeed));
            yield return s.WaitUntil(() => battle.Ready, "battle ready");
            s.Still("before");
            yield return null;

            int hp = battle.State.Unit(1).Hp;
            s.BeginCut();
            battle.Issue(Command.Ability(r.Ability, attacker: 0, target: 1));
            yield return s.WaitUntil(() => battle.Idle, "ability resolved");
            yield return s.WaitSeconds(r.TailSeconds);
            s.EndCut();

            s.Probe("damage", hp - battle.State.Unit(1).Hp);
            s.Probe("defender_hp", battle.State.Unit(1).Hp);
            hash = battle.State.Hash64.ToString("X16");
        }

        protected override IEnumerator Teardown(OrchardRecipe r, TrialSession s)
        {
            Battle.End();
            yield return s.WaitUntil(() => Battle.Current == null, "battle cleared");
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. Reset global state between recipes

Every recipe must start from the same state, whatever ran before it in the queue:

- end and unload what `Run` created in `Teardown`;
- reset statics and singletons the game keeps (`Time.timeScale`, caches, pools) in `Teardown` or on
  `TrialSession.Boundary`;
- seed every random source from the recipe: `UnityEngine.Random` and `new System.Random()` are seeded by the
  session; seed the game's own generators from `s.RunSeed` and the recipe's `Seed`.

```csharp
TrialSession.Boundary += () => { UnityEngine.Time.timeScale = 1f; DamageNumbers.Pool.Clear(); };
```

### 3. Run it twice

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --rounds 2
```

With two rounds, the `determinism` check fails any recipe whose `StateHash` differs between rounds.

## Reference

### Members

| Member | Default | Called |
|---|---|---|
| `public virtual IEnumerator Prepare(TrialSession s)` | nothing | Once per process, before the first recipe this adapter gets. With warm copies, at startup. |
| `protected abstract IEnumerator Run(TRecipe r, TrialSession s)` | | Per (recipe, round): set up, act, cut, probe. |
| `protected virtual IEnumerator Teardown(TRecipe r, TrialSession s)` | nothing | After `Run`, even when it failed. |
| `public virtual string StateHash { get; }` | `null` | Read after `Run`, before `Teardown`. A deterministic hash of the rules state, or null. |

`TrialAdapter<TRecipe>` is a `MonoBehaviour`: the session gives it its own GameObject that survives scene loads.
A plain `ITrialAdapter` (with `Accepts`) needs a public parameterless constructor.

### Which adapter plays a recipe

1. Only adapters whose recipe type is the recipe's class or a base of it, and whose `Accepts(recipe)` is true, count.
   A plain `ITrialAdapter` handles `TrialRecipe`, the least specific type.
2. The adapter with the most derived recipe type wins. `TrialAdapter<HudStates>` beats the package's
   `StaticTrialAdapter : TrialAdapter<StaticTrial>` for `HudStates`.
3. Two adapters for the same type are SCN203. Registration order decides nothing.

A selected recipe no adapter accepts fails alone, naming the registered adapters.

### Coroutine rules

- Everything is a coroutine: wait with `yield return s.WaitUntil(...)`, `s.WaitSeconds(...)` or `null`, never with
  sleeps.
- A throw, a timeout or `s.Fail` in `Run` fails the current recipe and stops `Run` at its next `yield`; `Teardown`
  still runs (limit 15 game seconds).
- In `Prepare`, any of them stops the queue with exit 3 (`prepare_failed`). `Prepare` has a limit of 60 seconds of
  real time.
- Split steps into methods and `yield return Step();` so the guards reach them. A coroutine started with
  `StartCoroutine` runs outside the guards.

### What makes a good StateHash

- Only rules state: unit positions, HP, turn, RNG state of the core. Never presentation (animations, particles).
- Stable across machines: integers, ordered collections, no `GetHashCode` of strings.
- The same value the multiverse and co-op telemetry use, so one function serves all three.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SCN202` | 3 | A registered type is not a valid adapter. | Derive from `TrialAdapter<TRecipe>` with a public parameterless constructor. |
| `SCN203` | 3 | Two adapters handle the same recipe type. | Keep one per type; make one more specific. |
| `no_adapter` | 3 | No `[assembly: TrialAdapter]` in the build. | Register the adapter; `dotnet scion diagnose` writes a skeleton. |
| `prepare_failed` | 3 | `Prepare` threw, timed out or called `Fail`. | Read `player.log` of the copy. |

## Examples

### A HUD adapter for static trials

```csharp
[assembly: TrialAdapter(typeof(Orchard.Trials.HudAdapter))]

public sealed class HudAdapter : TrialAdapter<HudStates>
{
    protected override IEnumerator Run(HudStates r, TrialSession s)
    {
        yield return SceneLoader.Load("HudPreview");
        yield return r.Play(s);
    }
}
```

### Map the run seed to the world

```csharp
var battle = Battle.Start(setup with { MapSeed = s.RunSeed * 7919 + r.Seed });
```

- [TrialSession](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/session/)
- [Adapters API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/adapters/)
- [SCN201-SCN203](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/trials/)

# TrialSession

`TrialSession` is the object adapters, grafts and checks talk to during a run. The player creates it when started
with `-scion-trials` (`TrialSession.Current`); adapters receive it in every call. Call its methods on the main thread:
a call from another thread does nothing and logs an error, which fails the recipe through the `log` check.

## Properties

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `static TrialSession Current` | The running session, or null without `-scion-trials`. |
| `static event Action Boundary` | Raised on the main thread after each recipe and once after the queue. Reset leaking state here. |
| `string OutputRoot` | The queue's output folder (`-scion-out`, or the folder of the last `RunQueue`). |
| `TrialRecipe Recipe` | The recipe running now, or null between recipes. |
| `string RecipeDir` | `<OutputRoot>/<IdDir>/r<Round>`. |
| `int Round` | The round being played, from 1. |
| `bool InRecipe` | True from the start of a recipe until its outputs are written. |
| `int RunSeed` | `-scion-seed` (`--seed`), 1 by default. |
| `IReadOnlyList<TrialRecipe> Recipes` | Every recipe found and expanded into ids, before filters. |
| `TrialRole Role` | `host` or `client:i` in co-op groups; `host` alone. |

## Capture

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `BeginCut()` | Starts capturing every rendered frame. Call it right before the action. |
| `EndCut()` | Stops capturing. The session also calls it when `Run` ends. |
| `Mark(string label)` | Labels the current frame (`frames.tsv`, `report.md`, `Marked` and `Order` checks, `context.png`). Ignored outside a cut. Labels may not contain a comma, `=`, tab or line break. |
| `MarkImpact()` | Marks the moment that matters: `window.png` centers on the first call; each call adds the label `IMPACT`. |
| `Still(string name)` | Saves the next rendered frame as `<name>.png`, inside or outside a cut. Names: up to 64 of `A-Za-z0-9_-.`; not `window`, `context`, `sheet`, `unstable`. Let a frame render after it. |
| `MaskRect(Rect screenPixels, string why)` | A region image comparison ignores in this recipe, in screen pixels, origin at the bottom left. |

## Verdict

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Fail(string reason)` | Fails the recipe and stops `Run` (or `Prepare`) at its next `yield`. `Teardown`, outputs and checks still run. The first reason is kept. Between recipes it fails the next one; after the last, the queue. |
| `Check(bool ok, string what)` | A soft check (id `assert`): when false, the recipe keeps running and fails at its end with `what`. |
| `Note(string line)` | A line in the recipe's `report.md`, stamped with game time, and in the log with `[Scion]`. |

## Data

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Probe(string key, double value)` | A number. The last value per key goes to `result.json` (`probes`) and is what `ProbeIs` tests; every call goes to `telemetry.jsonl`. |
| `Sensor(string name, Func<long> read)` | A `frames.tsv` column read once per captured frame. Lasts for the process: register in `Prepare`. Names `[a-z0-9_]+`. Keep `read` cheap and allocation-free. |
| `Event(string name, params (string Key, object Value)[] fields)` | A `"kind":"event"` line in `telemetry.jsonl`. Co-op uses `Event("turn", ("turn", n), ("hash", h))`. |

## Waiting

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `IEnumerator WaitUntil(Func<bool> cond, string what)` | Checks now, then every frame. On timeout: `timeout (30s): <what>`. |
| `IEnumerator WaitSeconds(float gameSeconds)` | Waits game time on the recipe's clock: `0.5f` is 15 frames at 30 fps on any machine. |

## Queues

```csharp
IEnumerator RunQueue(string only, int rounds, string outDir, Action<int> done = null)
```

Plays another queue in the same process without restarting the game; adapters already prepared skip `Prepare`.
`only` is a comma-separated pattern list (null = every non-`Explicit` recipe); `outDir` gets its own `run.json`,
`results.tsv` and recipe folders. `done` receives the exit code. Warm copies run every queue this way (op `run` of
the [control protocol](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/control-protocol/)). Throws `InvalidOperationException` when a queue is
already playing.

## Order of one recipe

| Moment | What happens |
|---|---|
| Start | `Recipe`, `Round`, `RecipeDir` set; `Random.InitState(Seed)`; `captureFramerate = Fps`; `Clock.Begin(1000)`; `SeededRandom.Reset(Seed)`; determinism controls on; checks `Begin`. |
| Run | `adapter.Run`, guarded; timeout = `TimeoutSeconds` of game time. |
| End | `EndCut`; `StateHash` read; PNG encoding starts; `Teardown`; PNGs awaited; checks `End`; then `frames.tsv`, `telemetry.jsonl`, `log.txt`, `result.json`, `report.md`; a line in `results.tsv`; `Boundary`. |

## See also

- [Write an adapter](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/adapters/)
- [Checks](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/checks/)
- [Session API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/session/)
- [Telemetry, probes and sensors](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/telemetry/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Checks

A check is a rule a recipe must pass. Built-in checks run on every recipe (no errors in the log, no blank or magenta
frames, the same hash every round); a recipe declares more in `Checks(TrialChecks c)`; the adapter adds soft checks
with `session.Check`; the game adds checks for every recipe with `ITrialCheck`. A failed check fails the recipe at
its end, without stopping it, and its id and reason go to `result.json` and `results.tsv`.

## When to use

- Use `Fail` when going on makes no sense (the battle never started); use `Check` or declared checks for everything
  else, so one run reports every problem.
- Use `ProbeIs` for numbers the rules produce (damage, HP, turns).
- Use an `ITrialCheck` for a rule about every frame of every recipe (no black frames, a HUD element always visible).

## Steps

### 1. Declare checks in the recipe

```csharp
protected override void Checks(TrialChecks c) =>
    c.Marked("IMPACT")
     .Order("IMPACT", "unit_down")
     .Frames(20, 90)
     .ProbeIs("damage", d => d >= 10, "a critical slash deals at least 10")
     .NoErrors("^Shader warning in 'Orchard/Water'")
     .Skip("px", "leaf particles drift between rounds");
```

### 2. Add soft checks in the adapter

```csharp
s.Check(battle.State.Unit(1).Hp < hp, "the slash lowers the defender's HP");
```

### 3. Allow known errors for the whole project

`scion.json`:

```json
{"schema_version":1,"log_allow":["^The referenced script \\(Unknown\\) on this Behaviour is missing"]}
```

The CLI passes them to every copy with `-scion-log-allow <file>`.

## Reference

### Built-in checks

| Id | Fails when |
|---|---|
| `log` | An Error, Exception or Assert is logged between the start of `Run` and the end of the recipe. `[Scion]` lines never count. |
| `assert` | `TrialSession.Check(false, ...)` was called. |
| `blank` | Every frame of the cut is one color (99 % or more). Some blank frames only warn. |
| `magenta` | A frame has 0.2 % or more of Unity's missing-shader magenta. |
| `determinism` | With 2 or more rounds in the process: the state hash differs (fails), or the frame count differs by one (warns) or more (fails). |
| `px` | With 2 or more rounds: the pixel hash differs (fails; set `Deterministic(pixels: false)` to warn only). |
| `gate:<id>` | An enabled gate fails ([Gates](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/gates/)). |

### TrialChecks

| Method | Check id | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `NoErrors(params string[] allowRegex)` | `log` | Each .NET regex allows matching errors. Calls add up. |
| `Deterministic(bool frames = false, bool pixels = true)` | `determinism`, `px` | Round comparison with any number of rounds; `frames: true` fails on one frame of difference. |
| `Marked(string label, int atLeast = 1)` | `marked:<label>` | The label was marked at least `atLeast` times in the cut. |
| `Order(params string[] labels)` | `order` | The labels were marked in this order (same frame or later). |
| `Frames(int min, int max)` | `frames` | The cut has `min` to `max` frames. |
| `ProbeIs(string key, Func<double, bool> ok, string why)` | `probe:<key>` | The last value of the probe passes `ok`. A key never probed fails. |
| `Gate(string id, params (string, object)[] options)` | `gate:<id>` | Enables a gate for this recipe. |
| `Skip(string checkId, string why)` | | Turns a check off for this recipe; shown as `skipped` with `why`. |

When a base recipe declares checks and a subclass adds more, call `base.Checks(c)`.

### ITrialCheck

```csharp
[assembly: TrialCheck(typeof(Orchard.Trials.HudAlwaysVisible))]

public sealed class HudAlwaysVisible : ITrialCheck
{
    int missing;
    public string Id => "hud-visible";
    public void Begin(TrialRecipe recipe, TrialSession session) => missing = -1;
    public void OnFrame(in FrameView frame)
    {
        if (missing < 0 && !Hud.Current.IsVisible) missing = frame.Index;
    }
    public void OnLog(string message, string stack, LogType type) { }
    public CheckResult End() => missing < 0 ? CheckResult.Pass() : CheckResult.Fail("HUD hidden", missing);
}
```

- One instance per process; `Begin` for each (recipe, round), then `OnFrame` per captured frame and `OnLog` per log
  line, then `End`. All on the main thread.
- `Id`: unique, no spaces, commas or `=`, not a built-in id.
- `FrameView`: `Index`, `Width`, `Height`, `Pixels` (bottom row first), `Layout`, `Px`, `GameMs`. Valid only during
  the call; keep `OnFrame` allocation-free.
- `CheckResult.Pass()`, `Warn(reason, frame, region)`, `Fail(reason, frame, region)`; `Region` in pixels, origin at
  the bottom left. `CheckStatus` is `Pass`, `Warn`, `Fail` or `Skipped`.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| check `fail` | 1 | A check failed. | Read `checks[]` in `result.json`: `id`, `reason`, `frame`, `region`. |
| invalid check | 3 | An `ITrialCheck` type or id is invalid. | Fix the id or the constructor. |

## Examples

### Every recipe ends with no unit stuck mid-animation

```csharp
public CheckResult End() => UnitView.AnyAnimating ? CheckResult.Warn("a unit is still animating") : CheckResult.Pass();
```

### A recipe that must fail, for testing the checks

```csharp
public sealed class SlashMisses : OrchardRecipe
{
    public SlashMisses() { Explicit = true; Distance = 5; }
    protected override void Checks(TrialChecks c) => c.ProbeIs("damage", d => d > 0, "expected to fail: out of range");
}
```

## See also

- [TrialSession](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/session/)
- [Gates](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/gates/)
- [Checks API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/checks/)

# Variants, modes and seeds

One recipe class can stand for many situations. `[Vary]` fields and `Variants()` expand it into **variants**
(`SlashHit[Attacker=mage,Distance=3]`); `[assembly: TrialModes]` adds **modes** such as resolutions (`@360p`); a seed
range repeats the selection per seed (`#7`). Each combination is an **id** with its own folder, baseline and verdict.
This guide covers the id grammar, `TrialArgs`, `Setup()`, modes, tags, patterns and `trial list --ids`.

## When to use

- Use `[Vary]` for a small grid of values (3 attackers x 3 distances).
- Use `Variants()` when combinations are not a full grid, or values are computed.
- Use modes for capture settings that apply to every recipe (resolutions, a color-blind filter).
- Use seed ranges to search for rare failures, not for baselines: each seed is its own id.

## Steps

### 1. Vary fields

```csharp
public sealed class SlashHit : OrchardRecipe
{
    [Vary("knight", "mage", "rogue")] public new string Attacker = "knight";
    [Vary(1, 3)] public new int Distance = 1;

    protected override void Setup()
    {
        Ability = Attacker == "mage" ? "fireball" : "slash";   // after the args are applied
    }
}
```

This gives 6 ids: `SlashHit[Attacker=knight,Distance=1]` through `SlashHit[Attacker=rogue,Distance=3]`.

### 2. Or yield the variants

```csharp
protected override IEnumerable<TrialArgs> Variants()
{
    yield return new TrialArgs { { "Attacker", "knight" }, { "Distance", 1 } };
    yield return new TrialArgs { { "Attacker", "mage" }, { "Distance", 4 }, { "tunable:CritShake.Strength", 0.8f } };
}
```

`Variants()` replaces the `[Vary]` grid when it returns non-null. Keys are field or property names of the recipe, or
`tunable:<Type>.<Field>` ([Tunables and presets](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/tunables/)).

### 3. Declare modes

```csharp
[assembly: TrialModes("360p=640x360", "720p=1280x720", "deuter")]
```

A mode `name=WxH` sets the capture size. Any other mode is passed to every adapter that implements
`ITrialModeAware`:

```csharp
public sealed class OrchardAdapter : TrialAdapter<OrchardRecipe>, ITrialModeAware
{
    public void ApplyMode(string mode) => ColorFilter.Set(mode == "deuter" ? Filter.Deuteranopia : Filter.None);
    // ...
}
```

### 4. Select

```sh
dotnet scion trial list --ids
dotnet scion trial run "SlashHit[Attacker=mage,*]" --mode 360p
dotnet scion trial run --tag combat --seeds 1-20
```

## Reference

### Id grammar

```text
<Name>[<key>=<value>,...]@<mode>#<seed>
```

| Part | Present when | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `Name` | always | `SlashHit` |
| `[k=v,...]` | the recipe has variants; keys in declaration order | `[Attacker=mage,Distance=3]` |
| `@mode` | a mode is selected | `@360p` |
| `#seed` | a seed range is selected | `#7` |

Values print with invariant culture (`0.8`, `true`). The folder name replaces any character outside
`[A-Za-z0-9_.,=@#[]-]` with `_`.

### Patterns

| Pattern | Matches |
|---|---|
| `SlashHit` | The `Name`: every variant of the recipe. |
| `SlashHit[Attacker=mage,Distance=3]` | One exact id. |
| `SlashHit[Attacker=mage,*]` | A glob over ids: `*` any text, `?` one character. |
| `--tag combat,ui` | Recipes with any of the tags. |
| `--players 4` | Recipes with `Players == 4`. |

Several patterns are separated by commas or given as separate arguments. A pattern that matches nothing exits 2
with `no_match` and `did_you_mean`. `Explicit` recipes run only when a pattern names their exact `Name` or `Id`.

### Player flags

| Flag | CLI | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `-scion-only <patterns>` | positional patterns | Select ids. |
| `-scion-tag <tags>` | `--tag` | Select by tag. |
| `-scion-mode <name>` | `--mode` | One mode for the whole run. |
| `-scion-seeds <a-b>` | `--seeds` | Repeat the selection per seed; ids get `#<seed>`. |
| `-scion-list` | `trial list --ids` | Write `recipes.json` with the expanded ids and exit 0. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_match` | 2 | No id matches. | Use `did_you_mean` or `trial list --ids`. |
| `bad_value` | 2 | A `[Vary]` value does not convert to the field's type, or an unknown mode. | Fix the value; list modes in `TrialModes`. |
| recipe error `unknown variant key <k>` | 1 | `TrialArgs` names a member the recipe does not have. | Use the field name. |

## Examples

### Every attacker at 360p and 720p

```sh
dotnet scion trial run "SlashHit[*]" --mode 360p
dotnet scion trial run "SlashHit[*]" --mode 720p
```

### Hunt a rare failure over 200 seeds

```sh
dotnet scion trial run KnightFalls --seeds 1-200 -j 8
```

## See also

- [Write a recipe](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/recipes/)
- [trial list](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/trial-list/)
- [recipes.json](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/recipes-json/)
- [Recipes API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/recipes/)

# Static trials

Some things have no action to play: a HUD in 20 states, every unit in its idle pose, every room template. A
`StaticTrial<TItem>` enumerates items, shows each one, lets it settle, captures it in one or more **views** and
writes a labeled `sheet.png` with all of them. The package registers the adapter that plays static trials, so a
static trial needs no adapter of its own.

## When to use

- Use a static trial to review many states at once, or to catch a regression in any of them.
- Use a normal recipe when something must happen over time (a hit, a turn).

## Steps

### 1. Enumerate, show, clear

```csharp
using System.Collections;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using Scion.Trials;

namespace Orchard.Trials
{
    public sealed class UnitGallery : StaticTrial<UnitKind>
    {
        public UnitGallery() { Description = "Every unit in its idle pose."; Tags = new[] { "art" }; }

        protected override IEnumerable<UnitKind> Enumerate() => UnitKinds.All;
        protected override string ItemName(UnitKind k) => k.Id;

        protected override IEnumerator Show(UnitKind k, TrialSession s)
        {
            Gallery.Place(k);
            yield return s.WaitUntil(() => Gallery.Ready, "unit placed");
        }

        protected override IEnumerator Clear(UnitKind k, TrialSession s)
        {
            Gallery.Clear();
            yield break;
        }

        protected override IEnumerable<TrialView> Views(UnitKind k)
        {
            yield return TrialView.Screen;
            yield return TrialView.Top(new Bounds(Vector3.zero, new Vector3(4, 2, 4)), pxPerUnit: 32, grid: true);
        }

        protected override void Measure(UnitKind k, TrialSession s) => s.Probe(k.Id + "_height_px", Gallery.HeightPx);
    }
}
```

### 2. Run it

```sh
dotnet scion trial run UnitGallery
dotnet scion trial show UnitGallery --image sheet
```

## Reference

### Members

| Member | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Enumerate()` | abstract | The items, in a stable order. |
| `ItemName(TItem)` | `ToString()` | The still's name and the sheet label. Names follow the still rules. |
| `Show(TItem, TrialSession)` | abstract | Put the item on screen and wait until it is ready. |
| `Clear(TItem, TrialSession)` | nothing | Remove it. |
| `Views(TItem)` | `TrialView.Screen` | The cameras to capture with. |
| `Measure(TItem, TrialSession)` | nothing | Probes for the item, after it settled. |
| `SettleFrames` | 3 | Frames to render after `Show` before capturing. |

### Views

| View | Captures |
|---|---|
| `TrialView.Screen` | The game camera, as the player sees it. |
| `TrialView.Ui` | Only the UI layer, on a transparent background. |
| `TrialView.Top(bounds, pxPerUnit, grid)` | An orthographic camera from above, framing `bounds` at `pxPerUnit`; `grid` draws a 1-unit grid. |

### Outputs

For each item and view: `<item>.<view>.png` (the view name is omitted for `Screen`). Then `sheet.png`: every
capture in a grid, labeled with the item name, with the longer side at most 2000 px. A static trial has no cut, so
`window.png` and `context.png` are not written; baselines compare the stills.

### Adapter choice

The package registers `StaticTrialAdapter : TrialAdapter<StaticTrial>`, which only calls `Play`. To load a scene
first, register an adapter for your type; the more specific type wins:

```csharp
public sealed class HudAdapter : TrialAdapter<HudStates>
{
    protected override IEnumerator Run(HudStates r, TrialSession s)
    {
        yield return SceneLoader.Load("HudPreview");
        yield return r.Play(s);
    }
}
```

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| recipe error `duplicate item name <name>` | 1 | Two items give the same `ItemName`. | Make names unique. |
| recipe error `timeout (30s): <what>` | 1 | `Show` never got ready. | Raise `TimeoutSeconds` for big galleries, or split the trial. |

## Examples

### Only the items that changed

```sh
dotnet scion trial run UnitGallery
dotnet scion trial show UnitGallery --changed --grid
```

### HUD states at two resolutions

See [Capture every HUD state](/scion/41664431a8f5/cookbook/hud-states/).

## See also

- [Capture every HUD state](/scion/41664431a8f5/cookbook/hud-states/)
- [Audit level rooms](/scion/41664431a8f5/cookbook/level-rooms/)
- [Adapters API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/adapters/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Co-op trials (1-4 players)

A recipe with `Players = 2` to `4` runs as a **group**: one host copy and `Players - 1` client copies of the same
test build, connected on a free port the CLI picks. Every process writes the state hash of each turn to its
telemetry; the recipe passes only if all of them agree and none fails. Pixels come from the host. This guide covers
`Players`, the `scion.json` keys `host_args`, `client_args` and `port_arg`, `-scion-role`, and how groups count
toward `-j`.

## When to use

- Write a co-op recipe for every mechanic that crosses the network: turns, shared abilities, joining and leaving.
- Keep solo recipes for presentation: they are cheaper and capture the same pixels.

## Before you begin

- The game takes its own command-line flags to host, join and pick a port. Orchard uses `-orchard-host`,
  `-orchard-join localhost` and `-orchard-port <n>`.
- The adapter writes a `turn` event with the state hash at the end of every turn.

## Steps

### 1. Tell the CLI how to start each role

```json
{"schema_version":1,"trials":{"host_args":["-orchard-host"],"client_args":["-orchard-join","localhost"],"port_arg":"-orchard-port"}}
```

### 2. Write the recipe

```csharp
public sealed class CoopTurn : OrchardRecipe
{
    public CoopTurn()
    {
        Players = 4;
        Description = "Four players each act once; every peer agrees on the state.";
        TimeoutSeconds = 60;
    }
}
```

### 3. Play it by role in the adapter

```csharp
protected override IEnumerator Run(OrchardRecipe r, TrialSession s)
{
    yield return s.WaitUntil(() => Lobby.Connected == r.Players, "all players connected");
    s.BeginCut();
    for (int turn = 1; turn <= r.Players; turn++)
    {
        if (Lobby.LocalPlayer == turn - 1) battle.Issue(Command.Ability("slash", attacker: turn - 1, target: 4));
        yield return s.WaitUntil(() => battle.State.Turn > turn, "turn " + turn);
        s.Event("turn", ("turn", turn), ("hash", battle.State.Hash64.ToString("X16")));
    }
    s.EndCut();
    hash = battle.State.Hash64.ToString("X16");
}
```

`s.Role` tells the adapter whether it is the host (`IsHost`, index 0) or `client:1` to `client:3`.

### 4. Run it

```sh
dotnet scion trial run CoopTurn -j 8
```

With `-j 8`, two groups of four run at once.

## Reference

![Diagram: a host and three clients connected on one port; every process writes per-turn hashes; pixels come from the host.](../../../assets/diagrams/coop-group.svg)

### What the CLI does per group

1. Picks a free port (bind to 0 and release).
2. Starts the host with `player_args`, `host_args`, `port_arg <port>` and `-scion-role host`.
3. Starts each client with `player_args`, `client_args`, `port_arg <port>` and `-scion-role client:<i>`.
4. Gives every process of the group the host's shard and `-scion-players <Players>`.
5. After the group ends, compares the `turn` events of every process.

### Rules

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Group size | `Players` copies, counted against `-j`. A `-j` smaller than `Players` is raised to `Players`. |
| Selection | A process plays only recipes whose `Players` equals its `-scion-players` (default 1), so solo copies never wait for clients. |
| Clock | The host runs on the virtual clock; clients run on the real clock and follow the host's ticks. |
| Pixels | Only the host captures. Clients write `result.json`, telemetry and logs. |
| Pass | Every process passes, and every `turn` event agrees on `hash` for the same `turn`. |
| Fail | Any process failing or exiting (a client that drops) fails the recipe, naming the process and the turn. |

### Output

Each process has its own `q<i>/` folder; `summary.json` lists them under `copies[]` with `role` and `group`.
A mismatch reads:

```text
CoopTurn r1: turn 3 hash differs: host 9F3A0C11D2E4B5A6, client:2 1B44E07AC9D20F13
```

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| recipe error `turn <n> hash differs` | 1 | Peers disagree on the rules state. | Run `dotnet scion diagnose`; look for rules reading local state. |
| recipe error `client:<i> exited <code>` | 1 | A client crashed or quit. | Read `q<i>/player.log`. |
| `copy_timeout` | 3 | A group made no progress. | Check `host_args`, `client_args` and `port_arg`. |

## Examples

### Only the co-op recipes

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --players 2
dotnet scion trial run --players 4
```

### A two-player recipe with a pass-through flag

```sh
dotnet scion trial run CoopTurn -- -orchard-latency 80
```

Arguments after `--` go to every process of the group and replace the same flag from `player_args`.

## See also

- [Parallel copies](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/parallel/)
- [Configuration](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/configuration/)
- [Player command line](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/player-flags/)
- [Netcode clock](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/netclock/)

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Parallel copies

`trial run -j N` starts N copies of the test build, each with a shard `i/N` of the (id, round) pairs, and merges
their folders into one run. This guide covers how shards split the work, how to choose N (`doctor` suggests it from
cores and free memory), timeouts, the watchdog, `keep_runs`, and measured costs on a laptop.

## When to use

- Always: even two copies halve the time of a long queue.
- Raise `-j` until the machine runs out of cores or memory; past that, use warm copies or the mosaic.

## Steps

### 1. Ask doctor

```sh
dotnet scion doctor
```

The output has `suggested_copies`: the smaller of (cores - 1) and (free memory / memory per copy measured on the
last run, or 600 MB before the first).

### 2. Run with that number

```sh
dotnet scion trial run -j 6 --rounds 4
```

### 3. Set it as the default

```json
{"schema_version":1,"trials":{"defaults":{"copies":6,"rounds":1,"timeout_s":300}}}
```

## Reference

### Shards

Every (round, id) pair, sorted by round and then by id (ordinal), is assigned round-robin: pair `k` goes to shard
`k mod N`. Each pair runs in exactly one copy. A copy with no pairs exits 0 at once. Co-op groups take the host's
shard ([Co-op trials](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/coop/)).

### Options that affect copies

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `-j N` | `trials.defaults.copies` | Copies (co-op groups count `Players` each). |
| `--rounds N` | 1 | Rounds of every id; shards split them. |
| `--timeout <s>` | `trials.defaults.timeout_s` (300) | Real seconds for one copy; past it, the copy is killed (`copy_timeout`, exit 3). |
| `--window` | off | Show the copies' windows instead of headless offscreen capture. |
| `--size WxH` | `trials.defaults.size` (1280x720) | Capture size. |

### Watchdog

Each copy rewrites `run.json` as it progresses. A copy that makes no progress for 120 seconds of real time ends with
exit 3 and `watchdog`. The CLI kills the whole process tree of a copy that times out.

### Keeping runs

Runs live in `trials.out` (default `.scion/runs/`), one folder per run named `yyyyMMdd-HHmmss`. At the start of each
run, the CLI deletes the oldest runs beyond `trials.keep_runs` (default 10). There is no separate clean-up command.

### Measured costs

On an Apple M5 (10 cores, 16 GB), Orchard's test build at 1280x720 offscreen:

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Startup to first recipe | 2.1 s |
| Memory per copy | about 550 MB |
| One combat recipe (2 s of game time at 30 fps) | 1.4 s of real time |
| 120 recipe-rounds with `-j 1` | 172 s |
| 120 recipe-rounds with `-j 6` | 31 s |

Startup dominates short runs; warm copies remove it ([Warm copies](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/warm-copies/)).

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `copy_timeout` | 3 | A copy passed `--timeout`, or was interrupted. | Read `q<i>/player.log`; raise `--timeout` for long queues. |
| `watchdog` | 3 | A copy stopped making progress for 120 s. | Look for a `WaitUntil` that never ends or a modal dialog. |
| `player_crashed` | 3 | A copy exited without writing its outputs. | Read `q<i>/player.log` and the crash report. |
| warning `low_memory` | 0 | Free memory is below what `-j` copies need. | Lower `-j`. |

## Examples

### Spread a long queue on a big machine

```sh
dotnet scion trial run -j 14 --rounds 2
```

### One copy for debugging, with a window

```sh
dotnet scion trial run SlashHit -j 1 --window
```

## See also

- [trial run](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/trial-run/)
- [Warm copies](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/warm-copies/)
- [Mosaic](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/mosaic/)
- [doctor](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/doctor/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Warm copies

A warm copy is a test build that started, prepared every adapter and waits, idle, for work on a local control
channel. `dotnet scion trial serve -j N` starts N of them; `dotnet scion trial run --warm` sends recipes to them
instead of starting new processes, so a run takes the time of the recipes alone. Warm copies also receive injected
grafts. This guide covers serving, running, stopping and the live files under `~/.scion/live/`.

## When to use

- Use warm copies while iterating on grafts or recipes: a run of a few recipes drops from seconds to under a second.
- Use cold runs (`trial run` without `--warm`) for baselines, CI and anything you approve: a warm run compares only
  hash and frames.

## Steps

### 1. Start them

```sh
dotnet scion trial serve -j 2
```

<!-- validate: cli/trial-serve -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"trial serve","ok":true,"copies":[{"q":0,"pid":4242,"port":51234,"state":"idle","out":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/serve/q0"},{"q":1,"pid":4243,"port":51240,"state":"idle","out":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/serve/q1"}],"next_step":"dotnet scion trial run --warm"}
```

The command returns when every copy is `idle`. Copies run in the background with
`-scion-serve -scion-control 0`, and without `-scion-quit`.

### 2. Run recipes on them

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --warm SlashHit FireballArea
```

The CLI splits the selection between idle copies and sends each an op `run`. The output is the same envelope as a
cold run.

### 3. Inject and run again

```sh
dotnet scion graft inject --to all
dotnet scion trial run --warm SlashHit
```

### 4. Stop them

```sh
dotnet scion trial serve --stop
```

## Reference

### What a warm run compares

| Compared | Cold run | Warm run |
|---|---|---|
| State hash | yes | yes |
| Frame count | yes | yes |
| Pixel hashes and images | yes | no (a warm process has rendered other recipes before, so caches and pools differ) |
| Can be approved | yes | no |

### Live files

Each copy writes `control.json` in its output folder and the same object in `~/.scion/live/<pid>.json`, mode 0600,
after the channel listens. The CLI finds copies through the live folder and deletes files of dead processes. The
token in the file authenticates every request ([control.json and live files](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/control-json/)).

### Lifecycle of a copy

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `preparing` | Startup: flags, discovery, every adapter's `Prepare`. |
| `idle` | Waiting for an op. |
| `running` | Playing a queue (`RunQueue`). An `inject` now answers `pending: true`. |

After 50 injections a copy reports `recycle: true` and `trial serve` replaces it at the next boundary (Mono never
unloads assemblies).

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_copies` | 3 | `--warm` found no live copy of this build. | `dotnet scion trial serve -j 2`. |
| `busy` | 3 | Every copy is running a queue. | Wait or start more copies. |
| `build_stale` | warning | The build changed after the copies started. | `trial serve --stop`, then serve again. |

## Examples

### Serve a different build

```sh
dotnet scion trial serve -j 2 --build /tmp/orchard-test/Orchard.app
```

### Watch status from a script

```sh
dotnet scion trial serve --format json | jq '.copies[] | {pid, state}'
```

`trial serve` without `-j` on a running set reports the copies and starts none.

## See also

- [trial serve](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/trial-serve/)
- [Live injection](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/injection/)
- [Control protocol](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/control-protocol/)
- [control.json and live files](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/control-json/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Capture and outputs

Every recipe writes a folder of outputs: a verdict (`result.json`), a human report (`report.md`), per-frame data
(`frames.tsv`), telemetry, the log, and images built from the frames of the cut. This guide covers headless and
offscreen capture, the contact sheets `window.png` and `context.png`, stills, `sheet.png`, the options `--frames`,
`--sound`, `--size` and `-scion-raw`, the 2000 px rule and the platform id that names baselines.

## When to use

- Read `window.png` first: it shows the moment that matters, frame by frame.
- Use `--frames` only to make a video or inspect one frame; it writes every frame as a PNG and is slow.
- Use `-scion-raw` when a tool needs the exact bytes that were hashed.

## Steps

### 1. Run headless (the default)

```sh
dotnet scion trial run SlashHit
```

Copies start with `-batchmode` and `-scion-offscreen`: the camera renders into textures at the capture size, with
no window. `Screen.width` and `Screen.height` read the capture size through `VirtualScreen`.

### 2. Find the images

```sh
dotnet scion trial show SlashHit
```

The output lists the paths of `window.png`, `context.png`, the stills and `report.md`.

### 3. Capture more when needed

```sh
dotnet scion trial run SlashHit --frames --size 1920x1080 --sound
```

## Reference

### Images per recipe

| File | Content | Size rule |
|---|---|---|
| `window.png` | Up to 12 consecutive frames centered on the first `MarkImpact` (or the cut's middle), 3 columns. | Longer side at most 2000 px |
| `context.png` | 6 frames spread over the whole cut (start, marks, end), 3x2. | Same |
| `<still>.png` | One frame per `Still(name)`, full size. | Capture size |
| `sheet.png` | Every item of a static trial, labeled. | Longer side at most 2000 px |
| `frames/NNNN.png` | Every frame of the cut (`--frames`). | Capture size |
| `frames/NNNN.raw` + `frames/raw.json` | The exact bytes hashed per frame (`-scion-raw`). | Capture size |
| motion pack | `motion-diff.png`, `tracks.png`, `idmask/`, `metrics.json`, `preview.gif` (`--motion`) | See [The motion pack](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/motion-pack/) |

Sheets downscale by the smallest integer that keeps the longer side at or under 2000 px: 12 frames of 1280x720 in
3 columns (3840x2880) downscale by 2. Labels name the frame number and its marks.

### Platform id

Images depend on the platform, so baselines keep one folder per platform:

```text
<os>-<gfx>-<W>x<H>-<capture>        osx-metal-1280x720-offscreen
```

`os` is `osx`, `win` or `linux`; `gfx` is the graphics API in lowercase (`metal`, `direct3d11`, `vulkan`); capture
is `offscreen` or `screen` (`--window`), because UI composition differs.

### Options

| CLI | Player flag | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--window` | (no `-batchmode`) | headless | Render to a window; the platform id ends in `screen`. |
| `--size WxH` | `-screen-width`, `-screen-height` | `trials.defaults.size` | Capture size. |
| `--frames` | `-scion-frames` | off | Every frame as PNG. |
| `--sound` | `-scion-sound` | muted | Keep audio on. |
| `--raw` | `-scion-raw` | off | Keep raw frames. |
| `--motion` | `-scion-motion` | off | Write the motion pack. |

### Coordinates

In the C# API (`MaskRect`, `CheckResult.Region`, `FrameView`) the origin is at the bottom left, like `Screen`. In
JSON, PNG and `Scion.Compare`, the origin is at the top left. The player converts when writing.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `capture_broken` | 3 | Captures are empty, usually `-batchmode` without offscreen capture. | Let the CLI start copies, or add `-scion-offscreen`. |
| recipe error `PNG encode failed` | 1 | Writing an image failed. | Check free disk space in `trials.out`. |
| `out_not_writable` | 3 | The output folder cannot be written. | Fix permissions or `trials.out`. |

## Examples

### A 4K still for a store page

```sh
dotnet scion trial run UnitGallery --size 3840x2160
```

### Frames for a GIF

```sh
dotnet scion trial run SlashHit --frames
ffmpeg -framerate 30 -i .scion/runs/20261011-143200/q0/SlashHit/r1/frames/%04d.png slash.gif
```

## See also

- [The run folder](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/run-folder/)
- [The motion pack](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/motion-pack/)
- [Raw frames](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/raw-frames/)
- [Baselines and approval](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/baselines/)

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Baselines and approval

A baseline is the approved result of one id: its state hash, frame count and, per platform, its frame hashes and
images. Every `trial run` compares each result with `scion/baselines/` and gives a verdict (`same`, `within`,
`px_changed`, `changed`, `new`, `stale`). `trial approve` turns a run into the new baseline. Agents may approve only
`new`; replacing a baseline someone approved needs a person at an interactive terminal.

## When to use

- Approve after an intended change, once the run shows exactly the change you meant.
- Never approve to make a failure go away: a failed recipe cannot be approved.

## Steps

### 1. Run and read the verdicts

```sh
dotnet scion trial run
dotnet scion trial show --changed
```

<!-- validate: cli/trial-show -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"trial show","ok":true,"run":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/runs/20261011-143200","count":1,"recipes":[{"id":"SlashHit","rounds":{"ok":2,"failed":0},"hashes":["9F3A0C11D2E4B5A6"],"frames":[46],"vs_approved":"changed","report":"q0/SlashHit/r1/report.md","images":["q0/SlashHit/r1/window.png"],"reasons":["image"],"stale":[],"px_diff":0.12}],"next_step":"look at q0/SlashHit/r1/window.png; if intended, a person approves: dotnet scion trial approve SlashHit --reason \"...\""}
```

### 2. Compare side by side

```sh
dotnet scion trial show SlashHit --grid
```

`--grid` writes one image per artifact with three columns: baseline, current, difference.

### 3. Approve

```sh
dotnet scion trial approve SlashHit --reason "crit shake is stronger"
```

<!-- validate: cli/trial-approve -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"trial approve","ok":true,"run":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/runs/20261011-143200","approved":1,"unchanged":0,"baselines":[{"id":"SlashHit","was":"changed","round":1,"copy":0,"dir":"scion/baselines/SlashHit"}],"staged":true,"refused":[],"next_step":"git commit -m \"Approve SlashHit: crit shake is stronger\""}
```

`approve` writes the files and runs `git add` on them; it never commits.

## Reference

### Verdicts

| Verdict | When |
|---|---|
| `same` | Hash, frames and images match. |
| `within` | Images differ inside the recipe's `Tolerance`. |
| `px_changed` | Hash and frames match, frame hashes differ, and the recipe compares no images (`Tolerance = null`). Informative. |
| `changed` | The hash differs, frames differ by more than one, an image is outside the tolerance, or the rule digest changed. |
| `new` | The id has no `baseline.json`. |
| `stale` | `baseline.json` exists but not for this platform, or fps, player args or Unity differ. Images and frame hashes are suspended; the hash is still compared, so a different hash is `changed`. |

`reasons` lists what triggered `changed`: `hash`, `frames`, `px`, `image`, `rule_hash`. `stale` lists why:
`platform`, `fps`, `player_args`, `unity`.

### Who approves what

| Verdict | Agent (no TTY) | Person at a terminal |
|---|---|---|
| `new` | yes | yes |
| `changed`, `stale`, `within`, `px_changed` | no: exit 2, `human_required` | yes, after a confirmation prompt |
| failed recipe | no | no |
| run with `--grafts` or `--warm` | no | no |

Approval is all or nothing: if one id is refused, nothing is written and `refused[]` says why. The `guard` hook
asks the person before an agent's `trial approve` and denies edits under `scion/baselines/`
([Hooks](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/hooks/)).

### Storage

```text
scion/baselines/SlashHit/
  baseline.json                         hash, frames, fps, player args, rule digest, approval
  osx-metal-1280x720-offscreen/
    platform.json                       size, Unity, tolerance, images
    frames.tsv                          per-frame hashes
    window.png  context.png  before.png
    unstable.png                        learned mask, optional
```

Store PNGs with Git LFS. Approving on one platform updates `baseline.json` and that platform's folder; other
platforms become `stale` until someone approves on each.

### Rule digest

`rule_digest` is a 12-hex digest of the files under `rule_paths` in `scion.json` (`Assets/Orchard/Core`,
`Assets/Orchard/Data`), uncommitted changes included. When it differs from the baseline's, the verdict is `changed`
with reason `rule_hash`, even if the hash happens to match: a rule change must be reviewed.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `human_required` | 2 | Approval of a non-`new` verdict without a TTY. | A person runs the command at a terminal. |
| `refused` | 1 | An id failed, or the run used `--grafts` or `--warm`. | Fix it, run cold, approve again. |
| `no_match` | 2 | The id is not in the run. | `trial show` lists the ids of the run. |
| warning `not_staged` | 0 | `git add` failed (no repository, LFS missing). | Stage the files yourself. |

## Examples

### Approve every new recipe (agents may)

```sh
dotnet scion trial approve --new --reason "first baseline for the gallery"
```

### Preview what would be approved

```sh
dotnet scion trial approve --changed --reason "new palette" --dry-run
```

## See also

- [trial approve](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/trial-approve/)
- [baseline.json and platform.json](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/baselines/)
- [Image comparison](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/image-comparison/)
- [Hooks](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/hooks/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Image comparison

Images are compared with `Scion.Compare`: a per-pixel perceptual distance (OKLab with the HyAB metric), a tolerance
per recipe (`ImageTolerance`), masks for regions that must be ignored, and an optional mask learned from runs that
shows which pixels are unstable. The result is a status per artifact (`Same`, `Within`, `Changed`), a changed ratio,
the bounds of the change and a heatmap `diff.png`.

## When to use

- Keep the default tolerance for most recipes: it ignores dithering and GPU rounding and catches visible changes.
- Use `ImageTolerance.Exact` for pixel art and UI that must not move a pixel.
- Set `Tolerance = null` for recipes where only the rules matter: images are captured but never compared.

## Steps

### 1. Choose the tolerance

```csharp
public HudStates()
{
    Tolerance = ImageTolerance.Exact;
}

public FireballArea()
{
    Tolerance = new ImageTolerance(pixel: 0.08f, maxRatio: 0.005f, maxPixels: -1);
}
```

### 2. Mask what changes on purpose

```csharp
public SlashHit()
{
    Mask("*", new Rect(0f, 0.94f, 1f, 0.06f), "turn timer");   // every artifact, top strip
    Mask("window.png", new Rect(0.8f, 0f, 0.2f, 0.1f), "fps counter");
}
```

Coordinates are normalized (0 to 1) with the origin at the bottom left, like `Screen`. At run time,
`session.MaskRect(screenPixels, why)` adds a mask in pixels.

### 3. Learn unstable pixels

```sh
dotnet scion trial run FireballArea --learn-unstable 3
```

The recipe runs 3 times; pixels that differ between those runs form `unstable.png`, saved with the baseline when
approved. A learned mask may cover at most 2 % of the image: above that, the recipe is not deterministic enough to
mask, and the run warns `mask_cap` instead of hiding the problem.

### 4. Read a change

```sh
dotnet scion trial show FireballArea --grid
dotnet scion trial diff 20261011-143200 20261011-150512 FireballArea
```

## Reference

### The metric

Each pixel pair is converted to OKLab and compared with HyAB (absolute lightness difference plus Euclidean distance
in a and b), scaled to 0 to 1. A pixel counts as changed when its distance is above `Pixel`. The image is:

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| `Same` | No changed pixel. |
| `Within` | Changed pixels are at most `MaxRatio` of the unmasked area and at most `MaxPixels` (when not -1). |
| `Changed` | Otherwise. |

The same metric gives the same result on every machine, so baselines from one Mac compare with captures from
another Mac of the same platform id.

### Tolerances

| Value | Pixel | MaxRatio | MaxPixels |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ImageTolerance.Default` | 0.1 | 0.001 | -1 |
| `ImageTolerance.Exact` | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `null` (recipe) | images not compared; frame hash changes give `px_changed` | | |

### Outputs

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `<run>/diff/<IdDir>/r<n>/<artifact>.diff.png` | Heatmap: changed pixels in red over a grey copy of the current image; masks hatched. |
| `compare.json` | Per id: verdict, reasons, image statuses, ratios, bounds (pixels, top-left origin) and diff paths. |
| `trial show --grid` output | Baseline, current and diff side by side. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| warning `mask_cap` | 0 | The learned mask would cover more than 2 %. | Make the recipe deterministic ([Particles, animators, UI and physics](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/control/)). |
| warning `px_unstable` | 0 | Frame hashes vary between rounds of this run. | Same as above; `px_changed` is noise until fixed. |
| warning `baseline_unreadable` | 0 | A baseline image or JSON cannot be read. | Check Git LFS (`git lfs pull`). |

## Examples

### Compare two images from code

```csharp
var a = Image.Load("scion/baselines/SlashHit/osx-metal-1280x720-offscreen/window.png");
var b = Image.Load(".scion/runs/20261011-143200/q0/SlashHit/r1/window.png");
var r = ImageDiff.Compare(a, b, Mask.Empty(a.Width, a.Height), ImageTolerance.Default);
Console.WriteLine($"{r.Status} {r.Ratio:P2} at {r.Bounds.X},{r.Bounds.Y}");
```

### Exact UI, tolerant world

```csharp
Tolerance = ImageTolerance.Default;
Mask("*", new Rect(0f, 0f, 1f, 0.15f), "HUD compared by HudStates with Exact");
```

## See also

- [Baselines and approval](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/baselines/)
- [Compare API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/compare/)
- [trial diff](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/trial-diff/)
- [A/B comparisons](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/ab-comparison/)

# Specs

A spec states, before the work starts, what a change must achieve: balance numbers from the simulator, visual
expectations and gates on recipes, and questions for the judge. It is a `TrialSpec` in the `Scion.Specs` project,
run with `dotnet scion trial run --spec <Name> --variants a,b,c`, and it returns one JSON verdict per variant. Specs
turn "make crits feel stronger" into something an agent can iterate on and a person can trust.

## When to use

- Write a spec before asking an agent for a feel or balance change, so success is defined up front.
- Use it to compare variants (presets, grafts, tunable sets) on the same criteria.
- Do not change a spec after running it to make a variant pass; write a new spec.

## Before you begin

- A specs project referencing `Scion.Specs` (`specs.project` in `scion.json`):

```sh
dotnet new classlib -o Trials/Specs/Orchard.Specs
dotnet add Trials/Specs/Orchard.Specs package Scion.Specs --version 1.0.0
```

## Steps

### 1. Write the spec

```csharp
using Scion.Specs;

namespace Orchard.Specs
{
    public sealed class StrongerCrits : TrialSpec
    {
        public override string Name => "StrongerCrits";
        public override string Target => "Critical hits read clearly as stronger without slowing the turn.";

        public override void Define(SpecBuilder s)
        {
            s.Balance("Duel", players: 1, matches: 500)
             .Expect("win_rate", min: 0.45, max: 0.55)
             .Expect("turns_mean", min: 6, max: 9);

            s.Visual("SlashHit")
             .Expect("hit_stop_ms", min: 50, max: 120)
             .Expect("shake_peak_px", min: 4, max: 12)
             .Gate(Gates.Photosensitivity)
             .Gate(Gates.TextContrast);

            s.Judge("SlashHit", head: "hit_weight").Expect("score", min: 0.6);
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. Run it on variants

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --spec StrongerCrits --variants base,heavy,snappy
```

<!-- validate: cli/trial-run -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"trial run","ok":true,"run":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/runs/20261012-091500","build_id":"4c49a1e0b2f3","copies":6,"wall_s":48.3,"runs":{"recipes":1,"rounds":1,"total":3,"ok":3,"failed":0,"changed":0,"px_changed":0,"new":0,"stale":0},"failed":[],"changed":[],"determinism":{"hash_stable":true,"frame_jitter":[]},"spec":{"name":"StrongerCrits","ok":true,"variants":[{"name":"base","ok":false,"failed":["hit_stop_ms 40 < 50"]},{"name":"heavy","ok":true,"failed":[]},{"name":"snappy","ok":true,"failed":[]}],"verdict":"heavy and snappy pass; base fails hit_stop_ms"},"next_step":"compare heavy and snappy: dotnet scion trial show SlashHit --grid"}
```

### 3. Let a person pick

The spec cuts the variants that fail; it does not choose between those that pass. Look at the grid or ask the judge
for a duel, then approve.

## Reference

### SpecBuilder

| Call | Runs | Measures |
|---|---|---|
| `Balance(name, players, matches)` | The rules simulator in .NET, with bots, `matches` times | `ISimulation.Metrics`: `win_rate`, `turns_mean` and the game's own |
| `Visual(recipe)` | The recipe in the test build, with `--motion` | The motion metrics (`hit_stop_ms`, `shake_peak_px`, `flash_ms`...) and probes |
| `Judge(recipe, head)` | The judge head on the recipe's images | `score`, `probabilities` |
| `Metamorphic(property)` | A property on the core ([Metamorphic tests](/scion/41664431a8f5/explore/metamorphic/)) | pass or fail |
| `Curve(name, levels)` | A balance curve over levels ([Balance with the simulator](/scion/41664431a8f5/explore/balance/)) | per-level metrics |

`Expect(metric, min, max)` adds a bound (either may be omitted). `Gate(id)` enables a gate on the recipe.

### Variants

`--variants a,b,c` names presets in `scion/presets/`, applied one per variant to every part of the spec. The
`base` preset is always the initial values.

### Guards

- A spec is frozen once it ran: the CLI records its source hash in the run, and a later run of a changed spec with
  the same name warns.
- Every spec run includes the `base` variant as a control.
- When a variant fails, `next_step` asks for a person to look at a sample of the failures, not just the numbers.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_match` | 2 | No spec with that name in `specs.project`. | Use `did_you_mean`. |
| `no_simulation` | 3 | `Balance` needs an `ISimulation` and the core declares none. | Implement `ISimulation` ([Core API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/core/)). |
| `model_missing` | 3 | `Judge` needs a head that is not trained. | `dotnet scion judge list`; train the head. |
| spec `ok: false` | 1 | No variant passes. | Read `spec.variants[].failed`. |

## Examples

### A balance-only spec

```csharp
public override void Define(SpecBuilder s) =>
    s.Balance("CoopFloor3", players: 4, matches: 1000).Expect("win_rate", min: 0.6, max: 0.75);
```

### Run a spec in CI

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --spec StrongerCrits --variants base
```

## See also

- [Specs API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/specs/)
- [Gates](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/gates/)
- [Balance with the simulator](/scion/41664431a8f5/explore/balance/)
- [trial run](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/trial-run/)

# Turn any match into a recipe

Anything that happens while someone plays a test build can become a recipe. Press **F9**: the game saves the
match's setup, seed and command log to `scion/recipes/captured/<name>.match.json`. Every saved match is a
`CapturedMatch` recipe that replays the commands and captures the result like any other recipe. The game implements
`IMatchCapture` once to save and restore its setup.

## When to use

- Capture a bug the moment you see it: the recipe reproduces it for an agent and guards the fix.
- Capture a moment that looks great, so later changes cannot break it unnoticed.
- Captured matches are also the starting points of the multiverse and the live loop.

## Before you begin

- The rules take commands and are deterministic from a seed (level 2 or more, see
  [Find non-determinism](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/diagnose/)).

## Steps

### 1. Implement IMatchCapture

```csharp
using Scion.Trials;

[assembly: MatchCapture(typeof(Orchard.Trials.OrchardMatchCapture))]

namespace Orchard.Trials
{
    public sealed class OrchardMatchCapture : IMatchCapture
    {
        public bool CanCapture => Battle.Current != null;
        public int Seed => Battle.Current.Setup.Seed;
        public int Players => Battle.Current.Setup.Players;
        public string SaveSetup() => JsonUtility.ToJson(Battle.Current.Setup);
        public IEnumerable<(int Turn, int Player, string Data)> Commands() =>
            Battle.Current.Log.Select(c => (c.Turn, c.Player, c.ToJson()));

        public IEnumerator Replay(MatchData match, TrialSession s)
        {
            var battle = Battle.Start(JsonUtility.FromJson<BattleSetup>(match.Setup));
            yield return s.WaitUntil(() => battle.Ready, "battle ready");
            s.BeginCut();
            foreach (var c in match.Commands)
            {
                battle.Issue(Command.FromJson(c.Data));
                yield return s.WaitUntil(() => battle.Idle, "turn " + c.Turn);
            }
            s.EndCut();
        }

        public string StateHash => Battle.Current?.State.Hash64.ToString("X16");
    }
}
```

### 2. Capture

Play the test build and press F9. The game shows `Saved match knight-dies-to-crit` and writes:

```text
scion/recipes/captured/knight-dies-to-crit.match.json
```

The name is typed in a small prompt (Enter keeps the suggested name).

### 3. Replay it

```sh
dotnet scion trial list
dotnet scion trial run "CapturedMatch[match=knight-dies-to-crit]"
```

## Reference

### The file

<!-- validate: match -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"name":"knight-dies-to-crit","captured_at":"2026-10-11T16:02:10Z","build_id":"4c49a1e0b2f3","source":"f9","seed":7,"players":1,"setup":{"map":"orchard-02","units":["knight","skeleton","skeleton"]},"commands":[{"turn":1,"player":0,"data":"{\"ability\":\"slash\",\"attacker\":0,\"target\":1}"},{"turn":2,"player":1,"data":"{\"ability\":\"bite\",\"attacker\":1,\"target\":0}"}],"turns":2,"feature":null}
```

`source` is `f9`, `hunt` (found by the [rare-moment hunter](/scion/41664431a8f5/explore/rare-moments/)) or `manual`. Matches the
hunter finds go to `scion/recipes/found/` until someone moves them to `captured/`.

### The recipe

`CapturedMatch` is a recipe of the package with one variant per file, `CapturedMatch[match=<name>]`. Its adapter
calls `IMatchCapture.Replay`. Baselines, checks and approval work as for any recipe.

### Options

| Where | Setting |
|---|---|
| Key | F9 by default; change it with `[assembly: MatchCapture(typeof(OrchardMatchCapture), Key = KeyCode.F8)]`. |
| Folder | `scion/recipes/captured/` (`trials.recipes_staging` + `captured/`). |
| Player flag | `-scion-match <file>` plays one match file directly. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| recipe error `replay diverged at turn <n>` | 1 | The rules changed since the capture, or are not deterministic. | Compare with `dotnet scion multiverse run`; recapture if the change is intended. |
| `no_match` | 2 | No match file with that name. | `trial list` shows captured matches. |

## Examples

### Guard a bug fix

```sh
dotnet scion trial run "CapturedMatch[match=knight-dies-to-crit]" --rounds 2
dotnet scion trial approve --new --reason "regression guard for the crit death bug"
```

### Play one match file in a window

```sh
.scion/builds/test/Orchard.app/Contents/MacOS/Orchard -scion-trials -scion-out /tmp/m -scion-match scion/recipes/captured/knight-dies-to-crit.match.json
```

## See also

- [The multiverse](/scion/41664431a8f5/explore/multiverse/)
- [Rare-moment hunter](/scion/41664431a8f5/explore/rare-moments/)
- [Recipes API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/recipes/)
