# Mosaic

The mosaic runs K **arenas** in one test-build process: K copies of the scene side by side, each with its own camera
rendering into its own texture, each playing one id. One process instead of K saves memory and startup, and the
output is a grid that shows the variants of one moment next to each other. This guide covers the requirements,
when to choose the mosaic over copies, `trial run --mosaic K` and the `IMosaicAdapter` interface.

## When to use

| Situation | Choose |
|---|---|
| Many different recipes, CPU-bound | Copies (`-j`) |
| A few variants of one moment, to look at side by side | Mosaic |
| Memory is the limit (big scenes, small machine) | Mosaic |
| The game has singletons or global state per scene | Copies, until `diagnose` shows no blockers |

## Before you begin

- The game can run several battles in one scene: no singletons for battle state, no global `Time.timeScale`, no
  static caches shared between battles.
- `dotnet scion diagnose` lists what blocks the mosaic under `singletons`.

## Steps

### 1. Check the blockers

```sh
dotnet scion diagnose
```

<!-- validate: cli/diagnose -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"diagnose","ok":true,"adoption_level":3,"assemblies":["Orchard.Core","Orchard.Runtime"],"counts":{"SCN301":12,"SCN302":3,"SCN303":0,"SCN304":0,"SCN305":1,"SCN306":0,"SCN307":0},"blockers":[],"singletons":["Orchard.Runtime.CameraRig.Current (Assets/Orchard/Runtime/CameraRig.cs:14)"],"plan":["Make CameraRig.Current per arena to enable the mosaic."],"adapter_skeleton":null,"report":"Library/Scion/diagnose.md","next_step":"fix the singletons listed, then: dotnet scion trial run --mosaic 4"}
```

### 2. Make the adapter arena-aware

```csharp
public sealed class OrchardAdapter : TrialAdapter<OrchardRecipe>, IMosaicAdapter
{
    public IEnumerator PrepareArena(int arena, TrialSession s)
    {
        yield return SceneLoader.LoadAdditive("Battle", offset: new Vector3(arena * 100, 0, 0));
    }

    protected override IEnumerator Run(OrchardRecipe r, TrialSession s)
    {
        var arena = s.Arena;                     // 0..K-1
        var battle = Battle.Start(setup, root: Arenas.Root(arena));
        // ... the same as a single run, through battle and arena-local objects ...
    }
}
```

`TrialSession.Arena` is the arena of the current recipe; `TrialSession.ForArena(i)` returns the session of
arena `i` from shared code.

### 3. Run

```sh
dotnet scion trial run SlashHit --variants base,heavy,snappy --mosaic 3
```

The run writes the usual per-id folders, plus `mosaic.png`: the `window.png` of every arena in one row each,
aligned on `IMPACT`.

## Reference

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Arenas | `K` from 2 to 16; each plays one id at a time from the process's shard. |
| Cameras | One per arena, rendering to a texture at the capture size; nothing renders to the screen. |
| Clock | Shared: all arenas advance the same virtual frame together. |
| Hash | Per arena, from the adapter's `StateHash` while `Arena` is set. |
| Result | `result.json` has `arena`; `run.json` has `mosaic: K`. |
| Player flag | `-scion-mosaic K`. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mosaic_unsupported` | 3 | The adapter does not implement `IMosaicAdapter`. | Implement it, or use copies. |
| recipe error `arena state leaked` | 1 | An arena's hash depends on another arena (a shared singleton). | Fix what `diagnose` lists under `singletons`. |

## Examples

### Four seeds of one moment

```sh
dotnet scion trial run KnightFalls --seeds 1-4 --mosaic 4
```

### The multiverse in a mosaic

```sh
dotnet scion multiverse run knight-dies-to-crit --at-turn 2 --variants base,heavy --mosaic
```

## See also

- [Parallel copies](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/parallel/)
- [Find non-determinism](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/diagnose/)
- [The multiverse](/scion/41664431a8f5/explore/multiverse/)

# Deterministic runs

A trial is only useful if the same recipe gives the same result every time. In test builds the weaver redirects
every source of variation the game reads (time, wall clock, screen size, unseeded randomness) to Scion's virtual
versions, and the session resets them at the start of every recipe. The game's rules then produce the same state
hash on every round and machine, and the same frames, so a difference always means a change.

## How it works

### What is redirected

With `SCION_TRIALS`, the weaver rewrites reads in every assembly that references `Scion.Runtime`, and the reads only
in the assemblies listed in `trials.redirect_assemblies` of `ScionSettings.json`:

| The game reads | In a test build it reads |
|---|---|
| `Time.time`, `timeAsDouble`, `timeSinceLevelLoad(AsDouble)` | `Clock.Time`, ... (virtual, from 1000 s at each recipe) |
| `Time.unscaledTime(AsDouble)`, `unscaledDeltaTime` | `Clock.UnscaledTime`, ... |
| `Time.realtimeSinceStartup(AsDouble)` | `Clock.RealtimeSinceStartup` (= virtual unscaled time) |
| `DateTime.Now`, `UtcNow`, `Today` | `Clock.Now`, ... (from `Clock.Epoch`, 2000-01-01 by default; no time zone) |
| `Screen.width`, `Screen.height` | `VirtualScreen.Width`, `Height` (the capture size, also in `-batchmode`) |
| `new WaitForSecondsRealtime(t)` | `new VirtualWaitForSecondsRealtime(t)` |
| `new System.Random()` (no seed) | `new SeededRandom()` (seed from the recipe and creation order) |

`Time.deltaTime` needs no redirect: `Time.captureFramerate = recipe.Fps` makes every frame advance exactly `1/Fps`
of game time, however long it took to render.

### What the session resets per recipe

1. `UnityEngine.Random.InitState(recipe.Seed)`;
2. `Time.captureFramerate = recipe.Fps`;
3. `Clock.Begin(Clock.RecipeStart)`: virtual time restarts at 1000 s, so the position in the queue does not matter;
4. `SeededRandom.Reset(recipe.Seed)`: the n-th `new System.Random()` gets the same seed every round;
5. the determinism controls of `recipe.Control`: particle seeds, animator and UI Toolkit updates, physics stepping
   ([Particles, animators, UI and physics](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/control/)).

### What the game must do

- Seed its own generators from the recipe (`Seed`) and the run (`RunSeed`).
- Keep rules on the main thread, with ordered collections and integer math in the core (rules R4 and R5 of the
  [Scion Standard](/scion/41664431a8f5/standard/rules/)).
- Mark real-time code (profilers, timeouts) with `[WallClock]` so it keeps the real clock.

`dotnet scion diagnose` finds the rest: wall-clock reads, threads, unordered collections, `GetHashCode` seeds and
`Guid`s, with file and line ([Find non-determinism](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/diagnose/)).

### The state hash

The adapter's `StateHash` is a hash of the rules state after the recipe. It is the main determinism signal: rounds
must agree on it, baselines store it, the multiverse compares it per turn and co-op peers compare it per turn.

## Key terms

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Virtual clock | `Clock`: time that advances one capture step per frame, from 1000 s at each recipe. |
| Epoch | The virtual wall-clock start, `Clock.Epoch` (`-scion-epoch`). |
| Recipe seed | `TrialRecipe.Seed`: seeds Unity's random and `SeededRandom` per recipe. |
| Run seed | `TrialSession.RunSeed` (`--seed`): the game maps it to its world seed. |
| State hash | The adapter's hash of rules state; equal across rounds when deterministic. |
| Adoption level | 1 (grafts), 2 (trials), 3 (multiverse): what the project can use today ([Find non-determinism](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/diagnose/)). |

## Guarantees and limits

- Redirects exist only in test builds; final builds read the real clock and screen.
- Only `new` expressions in woven code are replaced: a class derived from `System.Random`, or one created by
  reflection, keeps its behavior; pass it a seed.
- Inside `FixedUpdate`, the virtual `Time.time` keeps the frame's value; fixed-step code should add up
  `Time.fixedDeltaTime`.
- Netcode keeps its own tick unless `SCION_NETCLOCK` is on ([Netcode clock](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/netclock/)).
- Pixels can still vary with GPU drivers across machines; images compare per platform.

## See also

- [Clock, screen and random](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/clock-and-screen/)
- [Verify determinism](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/verify/)
- [Find non-determinism](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/diagnose/)
- [Determinism API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/determinism/)

# Clock, screen and random

These types are the targets of the weaver's redirects in test builds (`SCION_TRIALS`) and live in `Scion.Runtime`,
namespace `Scion`. Game code rarely calls them directly: it keeps reading `Time`, `Screen` and `DateTime`, and the
weaver points the reads here. This page lists what each one does, when it is active, and how to keep real time with
`[WallClock]`.

## Clock

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `const double RecipeStart = 1000.0` | `Time` and `UnscaledTime` at the start of every recipe. |
| `static readonly DateTime DefaultEpoch` | 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z. |
| `static bool Active` | True between `Begin` and `End`. Inactive, every property returns the real value. |
| `static DateTime Epoch` | The virtual wall-clock start (`-scion-epoch`). |
| `static void Begin(double start = RecipeStart)` | Called by the session at each recipe. |
| `static void End()` | Called at the end of the queue. |
| `static void Advance(float delta)` | Tests outside Unity: move every clock by `delta`. |
| `Time`, `TimeAsDouble` | Virtual `Time.time`. |
| `TimeSinceLevelLoad`, `TimeSinceLevelLoadAsDouble` | Virtual time since the recipe start. |
| `UnscaledTime`, `UnscaledTimeAsDouble`, `UnscaledDeltaTime` | Virtual unscaled time. |
| `RealtimeSinceStartup`, `RealtimeSinceStartupAsDouble` | Equal to virtual unscaled time. |
| `Now`, `UtcNow`, `Today` | `Epoch` plus elapsed virtual unscaled time. `Now` and `UtcNow` have the same value. |

## VirtualScreen

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `static void Set(int width, int height)` | The capture size; the session sets it from `--size`. |
| `static void Clear()` | Back to the real screen. |
| `static int Width`, `Height` | Targets of `Screen.width` and `Screen.height`. |

`-batchmode` players report 640x480 from `Screen`; with `VirtualScreen` the game lays out its UI at the capture size.

## VirtualWaitForSecondsRealtime

A `WaitForSecondsRealtime` whose wait reads `Clock.RealtimeSinceStartupAsDouble`, so a real-time wait lasts the
same number of frames in every run. The weaver replaces `new WaitForSecondsRealtime(t)` with it.

## SeededRandom

A `System.Random` whose seed is a hash of the recipe seed and the order of creation within the recipe.
`SeededRandom.Reset(seed)` restarts the count; the session calls it at each recipe. The weaver replaces
`new System.Random()` with `new SeededRandom()`. Create instances on the main thread so the order is stable.

## WallClock

```csharp
[WallClock]
static double ElapsedRealSeconds() => Time.realtimeSinceStartupAsDouble - startedAt;
```

`[WallClock]` on a method, class or struct stops every redirect inside it, including compiler-generated code
(iterators, async bodies, lambdas, local functions) and nested types. Use it for profilers, timeouts and log
timestamps. It changes nothing in final builds.

## Redirect assemblies

Assemblies that do not reference `Scion.Runtime` (Unity UI, URP) can have their reads redirected too:

```json
{"schema_version":1,"trials":{"redirect_assemblies":["UnityEngine.UI","Unity.RenderPipelines.Universal.Runtime"]}}
```

in `ProjectSettings/ScionSettings.json`. Only reads are redirected there; `new` expressions are not replaced. Scion's
own assemblies are never redirected. Recompile after editing the file.

## See also

- [Deterministic runs](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/overview/)
- [Determinism API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/determinism/)
- [Configuration](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/configuration/)
- [SCN301-SCN307](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/determinism/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Particles, animators, UI and physics

Time and randomness are not the only sources of variation: particle systems pick their own seeds, animators and UI
Toolkit update on their own schedules, and physics steps depend on frame timing. `DeterminismControl` turns Scion's
control of each on or off per recipe (`Particles`, `Animators`, `UiToolkit`, `Physics`; all on by default), and
`Determinism.SeedFor` gives your own systems stable seeds by path and creation order.

## When to use

- Leave `Control = DeterminismControl.All` unless a recipe tests the uncontrolled behavior.
- Turn one control off when it conflicts with how the game drives that system, and mask or skip the affected pixels.
- Use `SeedFor` for procedural systems of your own (foliage sway, ambient creatures).

## Steps

### 1. Keep the default, or narrow it

```csharp
public sealed class FireballArea : OrchardRecipe
{
    public FireballArea()
    {
        Control = DeterminismControl.All & ~DeterminismControl.Physics;   // the game steps physics itself
    }
}
```

### 2. Seed your own systems

```csharp
void Awake()
{
#if SCION_TRIALS
    seed = Determinism.SeedFor(transform.GetHierarchyPath(), creationOrder: Sway.Count++);
#else
    seed = Environment.TickCount;
#endif
}
```

### 3. Verify

```sh
dotnet scion trial run FireballArea --rounds 3 --check
```

## Reference

### Controls

| Flag | What Scion does while a recipe runs |
|---|---|
| `Particles` | Every `ParticleSystem` gets `useAutoRandomSeed = false` and `randomSeed = SeedFor(path, order)` when it starts; clones of one prefab differ by creation order. |
| `Animators` | Animators update in the session's frame step (`AnimatorUpdateMode.Normal` driven by virtual time), never with `UnscaledTime` from the real clock. |
| `UiToolkit` | UI Toolkit panels tick on the virtual clock, so transitions and caret blinks land on the same frames. |
| `Physics` | `Physics.simulationMode = Script` and one `Physics.Simulate(1/Fps)` per frame; `Physics2D` likewise. |

`DeterminismControl.None` turns all off; `All` turns all on.

### Determinism members

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Determinism.SeedFor(string path, int creationOrder)` | FNV hash of the recipe seed, the path and the order. |
| `Determinism.Census()` | What this frame still depends on: real-time reads, auto-seeded systems, dynamic bodies. Logged in `report.md` when a round differs. |
| `Determinism.Begin`, `End` | Called by the session. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| check `px` fails | 1 | Pixels differ between rounds. | Read `determinism.tsv` with `--check`; look at `Census` in `report.md`. |
| warning `px_unstable` | 0 | Pixels differ between rounds of the run. | Find the uncontrolled system; mask it as a last resort. |

## Examples

### A recipe that tests physics as the game runs it

```csharp
Control = DeterminismControl.Particles | DeterminismControl.Animators | DeterminismControl.UiToolkit;
```

### Print the census from the adapter

```csharp
foreach (var line in Determinism.Census()) s.Note(line);
```

## See also

- [Deterministic runs](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/overview/)
- [Verify determinism](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/verify/)
- [Determinism API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/determinism/)

# Netcode clock

Netcode for GameObjects keeps its own time from the real clock, so a networked recipe can tick one frame earlier or
later between rounds: the state hash still agrees, but the frame count jitters by one. With the define
`SCION_NETCLOCK` and `netclock_assemblies` in `ScionSettings.json`, the weaver redirects the time reads of Netcode
to the virtual clock on the host, and frame counts become exact.

## When to use

- Turn it on when co-op or networked solo recipes report `frame_jitter` and you want frames to fail on difference
  (`Deterministic(frames: true)`).
- Leave it off for games without Netcode.

## Before you begin

- Netcode for GameObjects in the project.
- A test build workflow (`dotnet scion build test`).

## Steps

### 1. List Netcode's assembly

`ProjectSettings/ScionSettings.json`:

```json
{"schema_version":1,"trials":{"netclock_assemblies":["Unity.Netcode.Runtime"]}}
```

### 2. Add the define to test builds

Add `SCION_NETCLOCK` to the scripting defines of the test build profile, or pass it in your build script:

```csharp
ScionBuild.BuildTestPlayer(options with { extraScriptingDefines = new[] { "SCION_NETCLOCK" } });
```

### 3. Verify

```sh
dotnet scion build test
dotnet scion trial run CoopTurn --rounds 3 --check
```

`frame_jitter` in the output should be empty.

## Reference

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| What is redirected | Netcode's reads of `Time.realtimeSinceStartup`, `Time.unscaledTime`, `Time.unscaledDeltaTime` in the listed assemblies. |
| Where | Only on the host of a group, and in solo copies. Clients stay on the real clock and follow the host's ticks. |
| Continuity | The netclock never jumps back at `Clock.Begin`: it advances continuously across recipes, so connections survive the queue. |
| `NetClock` type | `Scion.Trials.NetClock.Time` and `DeltaTime`: the same continuous time, for libraries you cannot weave (a custom time provider). |
| Without the define | `netclock_assemblies` is ignored. |

### A time provider for libraries you cannot weave

```csharp
sealed class TrialsTimeProvider : IRealTimeProvider   // Netcode for GameObjects, host of a trials run
{
    public float RealTimeSinceStartup => (float)NetClock.Time;
    public float UnscaledTime => (float)NetClock.Time;
    public float UnscaledDeltaTime => NetClock.DeltaTime;
    public float DeltaTime => UnityEngine.Time.deltaTime;
    public float FixedDeltaTime => UnityEngine.Time.fixedDeltaTime;
}
```

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SCN114` | compile error | A redirect target is missing in `Scion.Runtime` (a mismatched package). | Reinstall the package; CLI and package versions must match. |
| warning `frame_jitter` | 0 | Frame counts differ by one between rounds. | Turn on `SCION_NETCLOCK`. |

## Examples

### Fail co-op recipes on any frame difference

```csharp
protected override void Checks(TrialChecks c) => c.Deterministic(frames: true);
```

### Check the tick column

```sh
dotnet scion trial run CoopTurn --rounds 2 --check
grep tick .scion/runs/20261011-143200/q0/determinism.tsv
```

## See also

- [Co-op trials (1-4 players)](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/coop/)
- [Clock, screen and random](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/clock-and-screen/)
- [Configuration](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/configuration/)

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Verify determinism

Determinism is verified, not assumed. Two or more rounds of a recipe in one process must give the same state hash
(the `determinism` check) and the same pixels (`px`). `--check` compares every later round frame by frame with the
first and writes `determinism.tsv` with the first frame that differs and the first cause; `--jitter` adds random
real-time delays to expose code that follows the wall clock.

## When to use

- Run 2 rounds on every change (`--rounds 2`): it costs little and catches most problems.
- Run `--check --jitter 20` nightly, on many rounds, to catch the rare ones.
- Run `--check` when a round differs and you need to know where.

## Steps

### 1. Two rounds

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --rounds 2
```

The output's `determinism` block says whether every hash was stable and which recipes jittered by a frame:

```json
{"hash_stable":true,"frame_jitter":["CoopTurn 212/213"]}
```

### 2. Find where rounds diverge

```sh
dotnet scion trial run FireballArea --rounds 3 --check
```

`q0/determinism.tsv`:

```tsv
id	round	vs_round	status	frame	cause	detail
FireballArea	2	1	same	-1	none	
FireballArea	3	1	diff	17	rng	Random.state differs from frame 17
```

### 3. Shake the timing

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --rounds 4 --check --jitter 20
```

From the second round of each id, every frame sleeps a random 0 to 20 ms of real time. Deterministic code does not
notice; code that reads the real clock does.

## Reference

### Causes, in order

`cause` is the first column of `frames.tsv` that differs, in this order:

| Cause | Column | Usually means |
|---|---|---|
| `state` | the adapter's `state` sensor | A rule diverged. Look at the frame's events. |
| `tick` | the adapter's `tick` sensor | Network or fixed-step timing ([Netcode clock](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/netclock/)). |
| `rng` | `UnityEngine.Random` state | Something consumed random numbers in a different amount. |
| `unscaled` | virtual unscaled time | A real-time read leaked. |
| `time` | virtual time | `Time.timeScale` changed differently. |
| `px` | pixel hash | Only presentation differs ([Particles, animators, UI and physics](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/control/)). |
| `frames` | frame count | The cut ended on a different frame. |

Register the `state` and `tick` sensors in the adapter's `Prepare` so the first two causes can be found.

### Options

| CLI | Player flag | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--rounds N` | `-scion-rounds N` | Rounds per id. |
| `--check` | `-scion-check` | Frame-by-frame comparison; writes `determinism.tsv`. Never changes a verdict. |
| `--jitter <ms>` | `-scion-jitter <ms>` | Random real-time sleep per frame from the second round; 0 to 1000. |

### In the CLI output

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `determinism.hash_stable` | Every id had the same hash in every round. |
| `determinism.frame_jitter` | Ids whose frame counts differed by one, as `Id a/b`. |
| warning `px_unstable` | Pixel hashes varied between rounds. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| check `determinism` fails | 1 | Hashes differ between rounds. | `--check`; fix the cause at the frame. |
| check `px` fails | 1 | Pixels differ between rounds. | See `cause` `px`. |
| warning `frame_jitter` | 0 | Frame counts off by one. | Usually Netcode; turn on `SCION_NETCLOCK`. |

## Examples

### A nightly batch

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --rounds 10 --check --jitter 20 -j 8
```

### One recipe, many seeds

```sh
dotnet scion trial run KnightFalls --seeds 1-50 --rounds 2
```

## See also

- [Find non-determinism](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/diagnose/)
- [results.tsv, frames.tsv, determinism.tsv](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/tables/)
- [Run Scion in CI](/scion/41664431a8f5/cookbook/ci/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Find non-determinism

`dotnet scion diagnose` reads the determinism scan the weaver writes for each game assembly
(`Library/Scion/determinism-<assembly>.json`) and turns it into a report: the project's **adoption level** (1 to 3),
the blockers with file and line (SCN303 to SCN307), what test builds already redirect (SCN301, SCN302), the
singletons that block the mosaic, a plan, and an adapter skeleton when there is no adapter yet.

## When to use

- First thing in an existing project: it says what works today and what to fix first.
- When `--check` points at `unscaled`, `rng` or `state` and the cause is not obvious.
- Before turning on the mosaic or the multiverse.

## Steps

### 1. Compile the project once

Open the project in Unity (or build). The weaver writes the scan for every assembly that references
`Scion.Runtime`.

### 2. Run diagnose

```sh
dotnet scion diagnose
```

<!-- validate: cli/diagnose -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"diagnose","ok":true,"adoption_level":2,"assemblies":["Orchard.Core","Orchard.Runtime"],"counts":{"SCN301":14,"SCN302":2,"SCN303":1,"SCN304":1,"SCN305":2,"SCN306":0,"SCN307":0},"blockers":[{"file":"Assets/Orchard/Runtime/TurnTimer.cs","line":31,"code":"SCN303","message":"TurnTimer.Tick reads the wall clock (Stopwatch.GetTimestamp), which is not redirected."},{"file":"Assets/Orchard/Core/AiPlanner.cs","line":88,"code":"SCN305","message":"AiPlanner.Pick depends on an unordered collection or query (HashSet<Unit>)."}],"singletons":[],"plan":["Use Time in TurnTimer.Tick or mark it [WallClock].","Sort candidates in AiPlanner.Pick before choosing."],"adapter_skeleton":null,"report":"Library/Scion/diagnose.md","next_step":"fix the 2 blockers, then: dotnet scion trial run --rounds 2 --check"}
```

### 3. Fix, rebuild, verify

Fix the blockers in the order of `plan`, then:

```sh
dotnet scion build test
dotnet scion trial run --rounds 2 --check
```

## Reference

### Adoption levels

| Level | Needs | Unlocks |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Grafts | The package. | Grafts, automatic anchors, `graft check`, the project index. |
| 2. Trials | An adapter; recipes give the same hash every round (`hash_stable`). | Parallel recipes, captures, checks, baselines, bisect, co-op comparison, the judge. |
| 3. Multiverse | The rules in an assembly without engine references, registered as an `ISimulation`, and no blockers. | Balance specs, the multiverse, metamorphic tests, the hunter, guided search; the mosaic once `singletons` is empty. |

`doctor` reports the same level with `adoption_next`, the next step.

### Findings

| Id | Severity | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| SCN301 | info | A read redirected in test builds (time, screen). |
| SCN302 | info | A creation replaced in test builds (`Random`, `WaitForSecondsRealtime`). |
| SCN303 | warning | A wall-clock read that is not redirected (`Stopwatch`, `Environment.TickCount`). |
| SCN304 | warning | Threads or tasks in game logic. |
| SCN305 | warning | An unordered collection or query decides an outcome. |
| SCN306 | warning | Randomness seeded from `GetHashCode`. |
| SCN307 | warning | A `Guid` created at run time. |

SCN3xx never appear in the Unity console: the scan can list hundreds of lines, which would bury real errors. They
appear only in the scan file and in `diagnose`. Details: [SCN301-SCN307](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/determinism/).

### Options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--assembly <name>` | Only one assembly. |
| `--adapter` | Write an adapter skeleton to `Assets/Orchard/Trials/GameAdapter.cs` (`--dry-run` prints it). |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `config_not_found` | 2 | No `scion.json` above the current folder. | `dotnet scion init`. |
| warning `recipes_unchecked` | 0 | No scan file yet. | Open the project in Unity once. |

## Examples

### Only the core

```sh
dotnet scion diagnose --assembly Orchard.Core
```

### Suppress a reviewed finding

```csharp
#pragma warning disable SCN305 // order does not matter: we sum the set
int total = units.Sum(u => u.Hp);
#pragma warning restore SCN305
```

## See also

- [diagnose](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/diagnose/)
- [SCN301-SCN307](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/determinism/)
- [Add Scion to an existing game](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/existing-project/)

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# The evaluation funnel

An agent can produce ten versions of a hit effect in minutes; nobody can review ten versions of everything. Scion
evaluates in a funnel: cheap, certain stages first, each cutting what reaches the next. The **state oracle** and the
**objective gates** may block a change; **taste triage** (the judge, evaluators) only orders what is left; a
**person** picks. No model ever approves a change.

## How it works

![Diagram: four stages from wide to narrow: state oracle, objective gates, taste triage, a person picks.](../../../assets/diagrams/funnel.svg)

### 1. State oracle (blocks)

What the rules say happened: the state hash, checks, probes, the turn log. A graft that changes the hash is wrong
whatever it looks like. Cost: free, already in every run. See [Checks](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/checks/).

### 2. Objective gates (block)

Measurable visual rules that do not need taste: text that overflows its box, contrast under WCAG, flashes that risk
seizures, a regression against the baseline, telemetry that says something happened while the pixels show nothing.
A gate is a check with the id `gate:<name>`; a failing gate fails the recipe. See [Gates](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/gates/).

### 3. Taste triage (orders)

What remains is a matter of feel: is the hit heavy enough, is the HUD clean? Judge heads score images and sequences
in milliseconds; evaluators (scripts or agents) add scores from files. Scores never fail a run (`gate: false`): they
sort variants and pick which pairs a person should see. See [The Judge](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/overview/) and
[Evaluators](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/evaluators/).

### 4. A person picks

The person sees few, well-chosen comparisons: blind A/B pairs aligned on the impact frame
([A/B comparisons](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/ab-comparison/)). Their vote approves the baseline and trains the judge.

### Where the inputs come from

| Stage | Reads |
|---|---|
| State oracle | `result.json` (`hash`, `checks`, `probes`), `telemetry.jsonl` |
| Gates | frames, `frames.tsv`, the UI tree in test builds, telemetry |
| Taste | `window.png`, `context.png`, the motion pack, `metrics.json` |
| Person | `trial show --grid`, `preview.gif`, the judge's ranking |

## Key terms

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| State oracle | The rules' own record: hash, checks, probes. |
| Gate | An objective visual check that can fail a recipe. |
| Triage | Ordering variants by predicted taste; never blocks. |
| Head | A small judge model that answers one question. |
| Evaluator | An external scorer (process or agent) wired through files. |
| Duel | A blind A/B comparison shown to a person. |

## Guarantees and limits

- Only stages 1 and 2 change exit codes. A low judge score is never a failure.
- Gates measure what they can measure: a gate that passes does not mean the screen looks good.
- The judge is trained on the team's own votes; it predicts their taste, not general quality.
- A person approves every replaced baseline ([Baselines and approval](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/baselines/)).

## See also

- [Gates](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/gates/)
- [The motion pack](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/motion-pack/)
- [The Judge](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/overview/)
- [Evaluators](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/evaluators/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Gates

A gate is an objective visual check: it measures something a person would otherwise have to notice, and fails the
recipe when the measure is out of bounds. Gates are checks with the id `gate:<name>`, enabled per recipe with
`TrialChecks.Gate` or per spec with `.Gate(Gates.X)`. Their results appear in `result.json` like any check, with the
frame and the region of the problem.

## Enabling a gate

```csharp
protected override void Checks(TrialChecks c) =>
    c.Gate(Gates.TextOverflow)
     .Gate(Gates.TextContrast, ("min_ratio", 4.5))
     .Gate(Gates.Photosensitivity);
```

`Gates` holds the ids as string constants (`Gates.TextOverflow == "text_overflow"`). Options are name and value
pairs; unknown options fail the recipe with a message listing the valid ones.

## Built-in gates

### TextOverflow

Id `text_overflow`. Fails when a TextMeshPro or UI Toolkit text in the visible UI is truncated, wraps beyond its
rect or overflows its parent, on any captured frame. Reads the UI tree in test builds. Options: `ignore` (a list of
element names).

### UiGrid

Id `ui_grid`. Fails when a UI element's edges are off the layout grid by more than `tolerance_px` (default 1).
Options: `grid_px` (default 8), `tolerance_px`, `root` (a UI element name). Use it on static HUD states.

### TextContrast

Id `text_contrast`. Fails when text contrast with the pixels behind it is under WCAG 2.2: 4.5:1 for normal text,
3:1 for large text (18 pt, or 14 pt bold). Measures the rendered frame under each text element. Options:
`min_ratio`, `min_ratio_large`.

### Photosensitivity

Id `photosensitivity`. Fails on general or red flashes above the limits of the IRIS method (more than 3 flashes in
any second over 25 % of the screen). Reads every frame of the cut; works on `window.png` sequences too. Options:
`area` (default 0.25), `max_per_second` (default 3).

### ImageRegression

Id `image_regression`. Fails when an image is `changed` against the baseline, instead of only reporting the verdict.
Use it for screens that must never change without a new approval in the same commit. No options.

### TelemetryVsPixel

Id `telemetry_vs_pixel`. Fails when telemetry says a visual effect happened (an `fx` line: `Flash`, `Shake`, `Vfx`,
`Text`) but the frames within `window_frames` (default 6) after it show no change in the region, or the frame hash
did not change. Catches effects that fire but draw nothing (a missing material, a culled layer).

### NothingChanged

Id `nothing_changed`. Fails when the cut shows less than `min_ratio` (default 0.001) of changed pixels between its
first and last frame. Catches actions that silently do nothing on screen.

### Palette

Id `palette`. Fails when an isolated 2D asset (a sprite or a UI icon captured with `TrialView.Ui` on a transparent
background) uses colors outside the palette file. Options: `palette` (a `.hex` or `.gpl` file), `max_delta` (OKLab
distance, default 0.02). Only for isolated assets: lighting and post-processing change colors in scenes.

## Custom gates

Write an `ITrialCheck` whose `Id` starts with `gate:` and register it with `[assembly: TrialCheck]`. Two examples from
Orchard:

```csharp
public sealed class FloatingPropGate : ITrialCheck   // props must touch the ground
{
    string problem;
    public string Id => "gate:floating_prop";
    public void Begin(TrialRecipe r, TrialSession s) => problem = null;
    public void OnFrame(in FrameView f) { }
    public void OnLog(string m, string st, LogType t) { }
    public CheckResult End()
    {
        foreach (var prop in Props.All)
            if (prop.GroundGap > 0.02f) return CheckResult.Fail($"{prop.name} floats {prop.GroundGap:0.00} above ground");
        return CheckResult.Pass();
    }
}
```

A blocked door gate works the same way: for each door in the room, ask the navigation mesh for a path through it
and fail with the door's name when there is none.

## Results

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `checks[].id` | `gate:text_contrast` |
| `checks[].status` | `pass`, `warn`, `fail`, `skipped` |
| `checks[].reason` | `"Score" 3.1:1 on #5a5a5a (needs 4.5:1)` |
| `checks[].frame`, `region` | where; region in pixels, origin at the top left |

## See also

- [The evaluation funnel](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/overview/)
- [Checks](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/checks/)
- [Specs](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/specs/)
- [Specs API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/specs/)

# The motion pack

A sheet of frames shows what a hit looks like, not how it moves. With `--motion`, each recipe also writes a
**motion pack**: `motion-diff.png` (what changed between frames), `tracks.png` (where things moved), `idmask/`
(which object is which), `metrics.json` (hit-stop, shake, flash, number easing as numbers) and `preview.gif` for
people. Agents read the metrics and the two PNGs; they never need to watch a video.

## When to use

- Turn on `--motion` when the task is about feel: hit-stop, shake, flash, timing.
- Use the metrics as spec targets (`Expect("hit_stop_ms", 50, 120)`).

## Steps

### 1. Run with the pack

```sh
dotnet scion trial run SlashHit --motion
```

### 2. Read the metrics

`q0/SlashHit/r1/metrics.json`:

<!-- validate: metrics -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"id":"SlashHit","round":1,"impact_frame":14,"hit_stop":{"frames":2,"ms":66.7},"shake":{"peak_px":7.5,"rms_px":3.1,"decay_ms":200},"flash":{"delta_l":0.42,"ms":100,"area":0.03,"per_second":1},"anticipation_ms":133.3,"numbers":[{"text":"12","rise_px":38,"ms":900,"easing":"ease-out"}],"targets":{"hit_stop_ms":{"min":50,"max":120,"status":"pass"}}}
```

### 3. Look at the images when needed

```sh
dotnet scion trial show SlashHit --image motion-diff
```

## Reference

### Files

| File | Content | For |
|---|---|---|
| `window.png` | 12 frames around the impact | agents, people |
| `context.png` | 6 frames across the cut | agents, people |
| `motion-diff.png` | The same frames as `window.png`, each showing only what changed since the previous frame (brighter = more) | agents |
| `tracks.png` | The first frame with the path of each tracked object drawn over it, one color per object, dots every frame | agents |
| `idmask/NNNN.png` | Per frame, every renderer drawn in a flat color by object id; `idmask/ids.json` maps colors to object paths | tools |
| `metrics.json` | Motion metrics (below) | agents, specs, the judge |
| `preview.gif` | The cut at real speed, at most 640 px wide | people |
| `report.md` | Links and a metrics table | both |

### Metrics

| Metric | How it is measured |
|---|---|
| `hit_stop.frames`, `ms` | Consecutive frames after the impact where tracked objects do not move. |
| `shake.peak_px`, `rms_px`, `decay_ms` | Camera offset per frame (from the camera transform), in screen pixels. |
| `flash.delta_l`, `ms`, `area`, `per_second` | Mean OKLab lightness change in the flashed region, its duration and screen fraction. |
| `anticipation_ms` | Time between the command and the impact. |
| `numbers[]` | Floating text: rise in pixels, lifetime, the easing that fits best (`linear`, `ease-out`, `ease-in-out`, `back`). |
| `targets` | The bounds from the active spec and whether each passes. |

### Image rules

- Every PNG keeps the longer side at or under 2000 px.
- Frames carry their number and marks in a label strip, so an agent can cite "frame 14".
- `motion-diff.png` and `tracks.png` share the frame order and size of `window.png`.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| warning in `report.md` `no impact mark` | 0 | No `MarkImpact` in the cut; metrics measured from the cut's middle. | Mark the impact from an observer graft. |
| `bad_value` | 2 | `--motion` with `--warm` (warm runs capture no images). | Run cold. |

## Examples

### Ask for motion only on combat recipes

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --tag combat --motion
```

### Use a metric in a spec

```csharp
s.Visual("SlashHit").Expect("shake_peak_px", min: 4, max: 12);
```

## See also

- [Capture and outputs](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/capture/)
- [Judge motion](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/motion/)
- [The run folder](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/run-folder/)

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Telemetry, probes and sensors

Pixels show what happened; telemetry says it. Every recipe writes `telemetry.jsonl` (one JSON line per event: log
lines, notes, marks, probes, checks, faults, game events, `Fx` calls, injections) and `frames.tsv` (one row per
captured frame, with fixed columns, the game's sensors and the marks). Probes are the numbers checks and specs test.

## Probes

```csharp
session.Probe("damage", hpBefore - hpAfter);
```

- The last value per key goes to `result.json` under `probes`; `ProbeIs` tests it.
- Every call writes a `probe` line to telemetry, with frame and game time.
- Keys: lowercase letters, digits and `_`.

Core code can declare probes without referencing Trials: `[Probe("damage")]` on a field or property of a rule type
makes the adapter's generated code record it at the end of each recipe ([Core API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/core/)).

## Sensors

```csharp
session.Sensor("enemy_hp", () => battle.State.Unit(1).Hp);
```

- A column in `frames.tsv`, read once per captured frame.
- Registered once per process, in `Prepare`; columns freeze at the first `BeginCut` of a recipe.
- `state` and `tick` are the conventional names that `--check` reads first ([Verify determinism](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/verify/)).

## Marks

`Mark(label)`, `MarkImpact()` and `Fx.Mark(label)` label the current frame. Labels appear in the `marks` column, as
`mark` lines in telemetry and in `report.md`'s timeline. `IMPACT` is reserved for `MarkImpact`.

## Telemetry kinds

Every line has `f` (frame of the cut, -1 outside it), `t` (game seconds since the recipe start) and `kind`:

| kind | Fields | Written by |
|---|---|---|
| `log` | `type` (`Error`, `Assert`, `Exception`, `Warning`), `msg`, `stack` (up to 2 KB), `thread` (`main`, `worker`) | Unity's log |
| `note` | `msg` | `TrialSession.Note` |
| `mark` | `label` | `Mark`, `MarkImpact`, `Fx.Mark` |
| `probe` | `key`, `value` | `Probe` |
| `check` | `id`, `status`, `reason`, `frame` | the checks at the end |
| `fault` | `source`, `type`, `msg` | a graft that threw |
| `event` | `name` and the caller's fields | `TrialSession.Event` |
| `fx` | `verb`, `args`, `by` | every `Fx` call |
| `inject` | `version`, `bound` | an injection applied |

```json
{"f":14,"t":1.467,"kind":"event","name":"turn","turn":3,"hash":"9F3A0C11D2E4B5A6"}
```

## frames.tsv columns

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `frame` | Frame index in the cut, from 0. |
| `ms` | Game milliseconds since the cut started (integer). |
| `real_ms` | Wall milliseconds (informative, never compared). |
| `px` | xxHash64 of the frame's raw bytes, 16 hex digits. |
| `rng` | xxHash64 of `UnityEngine.Random.state`. |
| `unscaled`, `time` | Virtual unscaled and scaled time since the recipe start, seconds with 6 decimals. |
| sensors | One column per sensor, in registration order. |
| `marks` | Labels of the frame, comma-separated. |

## See also

- [TrialSession](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/session/)
- [telemetry.jsonl](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/telemetry-jsonl/)
- [results.tsv, frames.tsv, determinism.tsv](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/tables/)
- [Effects with Fx](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/fx/)

# A/B comparisons

Comparing two versions of an effect by eye is easy to get wrong: the frames are not aligned, the labels give the
answer away, and the first one shown wins more often. Scion's comparisons align variants on the impact event, show
one row per variant plus a difference row, hide which is which behind shuffled labels (X, Y, Z) and ask each pair in
both orders. The same rules apply when an agent, the judge or a person compares.

## When to use

- Use `trial show --grid` to compare a run with its baseline.
- Use `trial diff` to compare two runs (before and after a graft, two presets).
- Use `judge vote` to collect blind duels from people ([Train a head](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/training/)).

## Steps

### 1. Produce the variants

```sh
dotnet scion trial run SlashHit --variants base,heavy,snappy
```

### 2. Compare two runs

```sh
dotnet scion trial diff 20261011-143200 20261011-150512 SlashHit
```

<!-- validate: cli/trial-diff -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"trial diff","ok":true,"a":"20261011-143200","b":"20261011-150512","recipes":[{"id":"SlashHit","hash":"same","frames":[46,48],"first_frame":14,"cause":"px","images":[{"file":"window.png","status":"changed","ratio":0.021,"diff":"diff/SlashHit/r1/window.diff.png"}]}],"next_step":"look at diff/SlashHit/r1/window.diff.png"}
```

### 3. Ask blind

```sh
dotnet scion judge vote --run 20261011-150512 --head hit_weight
```

The page shows two sequences labeled X and Y, aligned on the impact, and asks which is better (or a tie, and how
strongly). Each pair comes back later in the other order.

## Reference

### Alignment

Variants are aligned on the first `IMPACT` mark. When a variant has none, on the first mark with the same label in
both; otherwise on the cut's first frame, and the grid says so. Frames before and after are padded so every row has
the same length.

### Grid layout

| Row | Content |
|---|---|
| One per variant | The `window.png` frames, aligned. |
| Difference | Per column, the heatmap between the first two rows. |

Labels in the grid are the variant names for `--grid` and `trial diff` (not blind), and X, Y, Z for duels.

### Blind rules

- Labels are shuffled per pair and stored in the vote, never shown with names.
- Each pair is asked in both orders; votes that disagree with themselves count as a tie.
- The control variant (`base`) is included in every comparison set.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_match` | 2 | A run or id is not found. | Use the run folder name from `trial run`. |
| warning in output `not aligned` | 0 | No common mark. | Mark the impact in both variants. |

## Examples

### Compare two copies of one run

```sh
dotnet scion trial diff 20261011-143200/q0 20261011-143200/q3 KnightFalls
```

### Grid against the baseline

```sh
dotnet scion trial show SlashHit --grid
```

## See also

- [Image comparison](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/image-comparison/)
- [trial diff](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/trial-diff/)
- [Train a head](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/training/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Evaluators

An evaluator scores the images of a run from outside Scion: a script, a model you run, or an agent. `dotnet scion
trial eval <run>` writes `eval-in.json` (questions and blind items), runs the evaluators configured in `scion.json`
or waits for an answer file, reads `eval-out.json` and writes `evals.tsv`. The CLI never calls a model itself, and
scores only order variants: an evaluator can never fail a run.

## When to use

- Use an evaluator for a question the trained judge does not cover yet, or to get a second opinion.
- Use an agent evaluator when you are an agent: export, answer the file yourself, import.

## Steps

### 1. Configure evaluators

```json
{"schema_version":1,"evaluators":[{"name":"contrast-script","command":["python3","tools/eval_contrast.py"],"kind":"process","gate":false},{"name":"agent","command":[],"kind":"agent","gate":false}]}
```

A `process` evaluator is called with the paths of `eval-in.json` and `eval-out.json` as its two arguments. An
`agent` evaluator is answered by hand or by an agent through `--import`.

### 2. Run them

```sh
dotnet scion trial eval 20261011-150512 --with contrast-script
```

### 3. Or answer as an agent

```sh
dotnet scion trial eval 20261011-150512 --with agent
# read .scion/runs/20261011-150512/eval-in.json, look at the images, write eval-out.json
dotnet scion trial eval 20261011-150512 --import eval-out.json
```

<!-- validate: cli/trial-eval -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"trial eval","ok":true,"run":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/runs/20261011-150512","evaluators":["agent"],"items":3,"exported":null,"imported":"eval-out.json","evals":"evals.tsv","scores":[{"id":"SlashHit[preset=heavy]","evaluator":"agent","question":"hit_weight","score":0.8}],"next_step":"dotnet scion trial show --grid"}
```

## Reference

### Files

| File | Written by | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `eval-in.json` | the CLI | Questions and items with blind labels (X, Y, Z), image paths, frames and metrics. |
| `eval-out.json` | the evaluator | Answers per item and question, with probabilities, confidence and evidence. |
| `evals.tsv` | the CLI | `id evaluator question score label`, one line per answer. |

The shapes are the judge's question and answer formats ([eval-in.json, eval-out.json, evals.tsv](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/evals/)).

### Rules

- Items are blind: the evaluator sees labels, never variant names. The CLI maps labels back on import.
- `gate` must be `false`: scores never change exit codes. An evaluator that should block is a gate, written as an
  `ITrialCheck`.
- Scores also go to the `eval` column of `summary.tsv`.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_match` | 2 | `--with` names an evaluator not in `scion.json`. | Use `did_you_mean`. |
| `bad_value` | 2 | `eval-out.json` does not match the schema. | Validate it against `judge-answer.schema.json`. |
| none | 1 | A process evaluator exited non-zero; its scores are missing and `ok` is false. | Read its stderr in the run's `evals.log`. |

## Examples

### Two evaluators at once

```sh
dotnet scion trial eval 20261011-150512 --with contrast-script,agent
```

### Export only

```sh
dotnet scion trial eval 20261011-150512 --with agent --dry-run
```

## See also

- [trial eval](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/trial-eval/)
- [eval-in.json, eval-out.json, evals.tsv](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/evals/)
- [Questions and answers](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/questions/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# The Judge

The Scion Judge answers taste questions about captures in milliseconds: is this HUD readable, is there a visual
glitch, does this hit feel heavy, does this screen look like our game. It has two parts: frozen **eyes** (a
pre-trained vision encoder) that turn each image into an embedding once, and small **heads** trained on your own
votes in seconds, one per question. The judge filters and orders; it never approves anything.

## How it works

```text
capture -> eyes (frozen, e.g. SigLIP 2) -> embedding, computed once and cached
                                              |-> head "has_glitch"   (noul)
                                              |-> head "readability"  (score)
                                              |-> head "main_issue"   (choice)
                                              '-> head "hit_weight"   (score)
```

### Eyes once, heads many

Computing an embedding is the expensive part, and it does not depend on the question. Scion computes it once per
image (and per view: full frame, HUD crop, corners, actor crop) and caches it under `judge.cache`. A new question is
a new head: a small classifier over the cached embeddings, trained in seconds. The cost of a question is in its
labels, not in its training.

### Why not ask a large model every time

A general vision-language model can review a screen, but it re-reads the whole context for every image, takes
seconds per item and does not know your taste. The judge answers in 10 to 50 ms per image, 100 captures in seconds,
a 30-frame sequence in under a second, on a laptop, and its answers are calibrated against your own gold set.
Large models are still useful: as agent evaluators on the few items the judge escalates.

### Where it sits

The judge is stage 3 of the [evaluation funnel](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/overview/): after the state oracle and the gates,
before a person. It sorts variants, picks which pairs a person should see, and escalates items it is unsure about.

### Pixel art

Downscaling erases one-pixel detail. For pixel art, views crop instead of scaling, or upscale 2x with nearest
neighbor, before the eyes see the image.

## Key terms

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Eyes | The frozen vision encoder (`judge.eyes` in `scion.json`). |
| Embedding | The vector the eyes produce for one image and view; cached. |
| Head | A small model trained on embeddings and votes; answers one question. |
| View | Which part of the image the eyes see: `full`, `hud`, `corners`, `actor`. |
| Vote | One person's (or agent's) answer: a duel winner, a score or a choice. |
| Gold set | Votes by the project's people, never used for training, used to measure a head. |
| Escalate | A question whose answer had low confidence; sent to a person or an agent evaluator. |

## Guarantees and limits

- The judge never changes an exit code or approves a baseline.
- A head predicts the taste of the people who voted; with few votes it is noisy, and `judge show` says so.
- Confidence is not accuracy: accuracy is measured on the gold set and reported as `calibration.agreement`.
- Studio data (captures, votes, heads) stays on your machines; nothing is sent anywhere.
- Model licenses vary by model card; check them before shipping heads ([Models and licenses](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/models/)).

## See also

- [Questions and answers](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/questions/)
- [Train a head](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/training/)
- [Review a UI with the judge](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/ui-review/)
- [judge (CLI)](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/judge/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Questions and answers

Every head answers one question, and every evaluator receives and returns the same shapes. A question has a type
(`noul`, `score` or `choice`), instructions and criteria; an answer has the value, the probabilities, a confidence
and a short legend, plus Scion's fields: evidence (frame and region), whether to escalate, the head version and its
calibration against the gold set.

## Question types

| Type | Asks | Answer value |
|---|---|---|
| `noul` | Yes or no (`has_glitch`). | `noul`: probability of yes, 0 to 1. |
| `score` | A level from 2 to 10 levels, each with what it means and examples. | `score`: the probability-weighted mean of the levels. |
| `choice` | One of up to 255 options, each with a description (`main_issue`). | `choice`: the option id. |

## Question file

`scion/judge/questions/readability.json`, the input of `judge new`:

<!-- validate: judge-question -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"run":null,"blind":true,"orders":2,"questions":{"readability":{"type":"score","instructions":"How easy is the HUD to read at 1x on a laptop screen?","criteria":["text size","contrast","hierarchy"],"levels":[{"what":"Hard to read","examples":["scion/judge/examples/read-0.png"]},{"what":"Readable with effort","examples":[]},{"what":"Effortless","examples":["scion/judge/examples/read-2.png"]}]}},"items":[]}
```

The same shape, with `items` filled, is `eval-in.json` for evaluators.

## Answer

<!-- validate: judge-answer -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"model":"siglip2-so400m","head_version":"readability@3","items":{"X":{"answers":{"readability":{"type":"score","score":1.2,"confidence":0.41,"probabilities":{"0":0.12,"1":0.56,"2":0.32},"legend":"small turn counter","evidence":{"frame":3,"region":[1100,20,160,40]}},"has_glitch":{"type":"noul","noul":0.04,"confidence":0.92}},"escalate":["readability"]}},"preferences":[],"calibration":{"gold_set":"ui_v1","agreement":0.78}}
```

## Answer fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `model` | The eyes (or the evaluator's model). |
| `head_version` | `<head>@<version>`. |
| `items.<label>.answers.<question>` | One answer per question. |
| `type` | The question type. |
| `noul`, `score`, `choice` | The value, by type. |
| `probabilities` | Per level or option. |
| `confidence` | 0 to 1: how concentrated the probabilities are. Not accuracy. |
| `legend` | A few words on why (from the nearest labeled examples). |
| `evidence` | `frame` and `region` (pixels, top-left origin) the answer is about. |
| `escalate` | Questions whose confidence fell under the head's threshold. |
| `preferences` | For duels: `pair`, `winner`, `strength` (1 slight, 2 clear). |
| `calibration` | `gold_set` and `agreement` with the people's gold votes. |

## Writing good questions

- Ask something concrete. "Is it beautiful?" is too vague to learn; "Does the palette stay cohesive?", "Does it look
  like these five approved screens?", "Is the selected state obvious?" work.
- Give every score level a description and examples.
- Prefer duels for feel ("which hit is heavier?"): people agree more on comparisons than on absolute scores.

## See also

- [The Judge](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/overview/)
- [eval-in.json, eval-out.json, evals.tsv](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/evals/)
- [Judge data files](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/judge-data/)
- [Evaluators](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/evaluators/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Train a head

A head learns one question from votes. This guide creates a head, collects votes with `judge vote` (blind duels in
the browser), adds synthetic examples (degraded versions and fabricated bugs), keeps a gold set that never enters
training, trains with `judge train` (cross-validated, seconds) and promotes the new version only when it agrees
more with the people's gold votes than the previous one.

## When to use

- Train a head when the same taste question comes up on every change (HUD readability, hit weight, glitches).
- Start with three heads: UI readability, visual glitch, and "looks like our game".

## Before you begin

- The judge configured in `scion.json` (`judge.dir`, `judge.eyes`, `judge.cache`); `dotnet scion doctor` checks that
  the eye model is present.
- A few runs with captures of the thing to judge.

## Steps

### 1. Create the head

```sh
dotnet scion judge new readability --question scion/judge/questions/readability.json --view hud
```

### 2. Vote

```sh
dotnet scion judge vote --run 20261011-150512 --head readability
```

A local page opens with blind pairs (X and Y), each asked in both orders. Ten minutes gives about 60 duels. Votes go
to `scion/judge/votes/readability.jsonl`.

### 3. Add synthetic examples

```sh
dotnet scion judge vote --head readability --synthetic 200
```

Scion degrades approved captures (lower contrast, 1 px misalignment, clutter, off-palette color, overflowing text)
and fabricates bugs (missing-shader magenta, floating props, z-fighting). Each pair "original beats degraded" is a
vote with `source: agent` and the degradation as its tag.

### 4. Set the gold set apart

```sh
dotnet scion judge vote --head readability --gold ui_v1 --count 150
```

Gold votes come only from people, never from agents, and never enter training. A week later, re-vote 30 to 50 of
them (`--regold`) to measure how much people agree with themselves: that is the ceiling a head can reach.

### 5. Train

```sh
dotnet scion judge train readability
```

<!-- validate: cli/judge -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"judge train","ok":true,"head":{"schema_version":1,"name":"readability","version":4,"eyes":"siglip2-so400m","view":"hud","question":{"type":"score","instructions":"How easy is the HUD to read at 1x on a laptop screen?"},"trained_at":"2026-10-12T08:10:00Z","votes":412,"calibration":{"gold_set":"ui_v1","agreement":0.81,"ceiling":0.86}},"training":{"folds":5,"accuracy":0.83,"gold_agreement":0.81,"previous":0.78,"promoted":true},"next_step":"dotnet scion judge run <run> --heads readability"}
```

### 6. Use it

```sh
dotnet scion judge run 20261011-150512 --heads readability,has_glitch
```

## Reference

### Promotion rule

A new version replaces the current head only when its agreement with the gold set is higher than the previous
version's. Otherwise it is kept as `readability@4-rejected` for inspection, and `promoted` is false.

### What makes votes useful

| Do | Because |
|---|---|
| Include near-misses: pairs almost equal where one is worse | They teach the boundary. |
| Mix sources: old versions of the game (git), degradations, fabricated bugs, real variants | One source teaches its own artifacts. |
| Vote in both orders | Position bias cancels out. |
| Let the judge pick the next duels (`judge vote` does by default) | It asks where it is least sure. |

### Agents in the loop

Agents may generate synthetic pairs, label pairs in batch as `source: agent`, pick the most informative screens for a
person, and explain disagreements ("it learned that dark means bad"). They never vote in the gold set, and a head is
promoted only by agreement with people.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_missing` | 3 | The eye model is not downloaded. | `dotnet scion doctor` prints the download command. |
| `no_match` | 2 | No head with that name. | `dotnet scion judge list`. |
| training `promoted: false` | 0 | The new version does not beat the old one on gold. | Add near-miss votes; check `judge show` for where it errs. |

## Examples

### Inspect a head

```sh
dotnet scion judge show readability
```

### A duel head for feel

```sh
dotnet scion judge new hit_weight --question scion/judge/questions/hit_weight.json --view actor --sequence
```

## See also

- [Questions and answers](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/questions/)
- [judge (CLI)](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/judge/)
- [Judge data files](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/judge-data/)
- [Judge motion](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/motion/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Judge motion

Feel lives in motion: how long the hit-stop lasts, how the shake decays, when the flash peaks. A **sequence head**
combines two inputs: the numbers of the motion pack (`metrics.json`) and the embeddings of each frame of the cut. A
small tree model learns the taste over the numbers from few examples and explains its answer; the frame embeddings
add style. This guide creates and uses a sequence head.

## When to use

- Use a sequence head for feel questions: "which hit is heavier?", "is the anticipation visible?", "too much juice?".
- Use an image head for anything that one frame shows.

## Before you begin

- Runs made with `--motion`, so `metrics.json` exists for each recipe.
- The gates still run first: a sequence that fails photosensitivity is never ranked.

## Steps

### 1. Create a sequence head

```sh
dotnet scion judge new hit_weight --question scion/judge/questions/hit_weight.json --view actor --sequence
```

### 2. Collect duels on sequences

```sh
dotnet scion trial run SlashHit --variants base,heavy,snappy --motion
dotnet scion judge vote --run 20261012-091500 --head hit_weight
```

Duels show the two `preview.gif` side by side, aligned on the impact.

### 3. Train and run

```sh
dotnet scion judge train hit_weight
dotnet scion judge run 20261012-091500 --heads hit_weight
```

## Reference

### Inputs

| Input | From | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Motion metrics | `metrics.json`: hit-stop, shake, flash, anticipation, numbers | The tree model: explainable, works with 50 votes |
| Frame embeddings | The eyes on each frame of `window.png`, `actor` view | Style: does the motion look like our approved hits |

### Output

A sequence head answers like any head, and its `legend` names the metrics that weighed most:

```text
hit_weight 0.74 (heavier): hit_stop.ms 100 (+), shake.peak_px 9 (+), flash.ms 80 (-)
```

### Speed

A 30-frame sequence takes under a second: metrics are already computed, and frame embeddings are cached like any
image.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bad_value` | 2 | The run has no `metrics.json`. | Run with `--motion`. |
| `model_missing` | 3 | The eyes are not installed. | `dotnet scion doctor`. |

## Examples

### Too much or too little juice

```json
{"schema_version":1,"run":null,"blind":true,"orders":2,"questions":{"juice":{"type":"choice","instructions":"How much juice does the hit have?","options":[{"id":"too_little","description":"Flat"},{"id":"right","description":"Right"},{"id":"too_much","description":"Noisy"}]}},"items":[]}
```

### Rank presets

```sh
dotnet scion judge run 20261012-091500 --heads hit_weight,juice
```

## See also

- [The motion pack](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/motion-pack/)
- [Train a head](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/training/)
- [Tune a hit effect](/scion/41664431a8f5/cookbook/tune-hit-feel/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Taste heads and feel presets

Taste is not one thing. A head trained on the studio's votes predicts the studio; a head trained on playtesters
predicts casual players; an accessibility head favors contrast and calm motion. Heads are swappable per audience.
Feel works the same way: named **presets** of tunable values (`heavy`, `snappy`) that blend with weights, so an agent
turns two or three knobs instead of fifteen numbers.

## When to use

- Use audience heads when the team and the players disagree, or for accessibility reviews.
- Use presets to name a feel once and reuse it across effects and recipes.

## Steps

### 1. Train a head per audience

```sh
dotnet scion judge new hit_weight.casual --question scion/judge/questions/hit_weight.json --view actor --sequence
dotnet scion judge vote --head hit_weight.casual --run 20261012-091500
```

Head names may have a suffix after a dot; `judge run --heads hit_weight.casual` picks that one.

### 2. Save presets

`scion/presets/snappy.json`:

<!-- validate: preset -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"name":"snappy","description":"Short, crisp hits.","tunables":{"CritShake.Strength":0.2,"CritShake.Stop":0.03,"HitFlash.Seconds":0.05}}
```

### 3. Blend and compare

```sh
dotnet scion trial run SlashHit --variants base,heavy,snappy,"base + 0.7 heavy + 0.3 snappy" --motion
dotnet scion judge run <run> --heads hit_weight,hit_weight.casual
```

## Reference

### The cycle

1. Generate many variants (presets, blends, guided search).
2. The judge orders them per audience.
3. A person picks between the top two.
4. The vote trains the head; a winning blend can become a preset.

### Where art-style variations come from

Scion varies what code and numbers control: grafts, tunables, presets. New art in the game's style (sprites, icons)
comes from your art pipeline or image tools, outside Scion; once in the project, trials capture it and the judge
ranks it like anything else.

### Blend syntax

`base + 0.7 heavy + 0.3 snappy`: weights are decimals, presets are names in `scion/presets/`, `base` is the initial
values. See [Tunables and presets](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/tunables/).

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_match` | 2 | A preset or head name does not exist. | List `scion/presets/` or `judge list`. |
| `bad_value` | 2 | A blend does not parse. | Use `name`, `+` and decimal weights. |

## Examples

### An accessibility head

```sh
dotnet scion judge new calm_motion.access --question scion/judge/questions/calm_motion.json --sequence
```

### Use a blend in a spec run

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --spec StrongerCrits --variants base,"base + 0.7 heavy + 0.3 snappy"
```

## See also

- [Tunables and presets](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/tunables/)
- [Train a head](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/training/)
- [Guided search](/scion/41664431a8f5/explore/guided-search/)
