> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Review a UI with the judge

This tutorial reviews Orchard's battle HUD in about 30 to 45 minutes instead of hours. Scion captures 20 HUD states
at two resolutions, the gates catch objective problems, the judge scores and ranks every capture, an agent reviews
only the worst and the uncertain ones next to reference screens, makes variations, the judge compares them in
pairs, and a person picks between the final two. The vote trains the judge for next time.

## Before you begin

- The `HudStates` static trial ([Capture every HUD state](/scion/41664431a8f5/cookbook/hud-states/)).
- Trained heads `readability`, `has_glitch` and `looks_like_orchard` ([Train a head](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/training/)).
- Optional: a reference library of screens from other games, indexed by the judge (`scion/judge/references/`).

## Steps

### 1. Capture (about 1 minute)

```sh
dotnet scion trial run HudStates --mode 360p
dotnet scion trial run HudStates --mode 720p
```

40 stills, two sheets.

### 2. Gates (seconds)

`HudStates` enables `TextOverflow`, `TextContrast` and `UiGrid`. Failures come first in `trial show --failed`.

### 3. Judge (seconds)

```sh
dotnet scion judge run <run> --heads readability,has_glitch,looks_like_orchard
```

Every capture gets a score per head; low-confidence answers are listed under `escalate`.

### 4. References (milliseconds)

```sh
dotnet scion judge run <run> --references 5
```

For each capture, the five most similar reference screens and their notes.

### 5. Agent review of the worst (5 to 10 minutes)

The agent reads only the 10 to 15 lowest-scored and escalated captures, each next to its references, and writes a
short list of problems with evidence (state, region).

### 6. Variations (5 to 15 minutes)

The agent writes graft or theme changes for the problems (spacing, contrast, icon size) as drafts and runs the
states again with `--grafts`.

### 7. Re-judge in pairs (3 to 5 minutes)

```sh
dotnet scion trial diff <before> <after> HudStates
dotnet scion judge run <after> --heads readability --pairs <before>
```

### 8. A person picks (about 5 minutes)

```sh
dotnet scion judge vote --run <after> --head readability --top 2
```

The person sees the top two variants per state, blind, and picks.

### 9. The vote trains

```sh
dotnet scion judge train readability
```

## Check the result

- `trial show HudStates --failed` lists no gate failures.
- `judge run` scores the winning variant above the original on `readability` for most states.
- `judge show readability` reports a new version, promoted, with agreement on the gold set equal or higher.

## Next steps

- Promote the winning grafts and approve the new stills ([From draft to final build](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/lifecycle/)).
- Add the HUD review to CI with only steps 1 and 2 ([Run Scion in CI](/scion/41664431a8f5/cookbook/ci/)).
- Train an audience head for accessibility ([Taste heads and feel presets](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/presets/)).

## See also

- [Capture every HUD state](/scion/41664431a8f5/cookbook/hud-states/)
- [Gates](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/gates/)
- [Train a head](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/training/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Models and licenses

The judge's eyes are pre-trained vision encoders that run locally. Scion does not ship model weights: `dotnet scion
doctor` checks the configured model and prints the command that downloads it into the local model cache. This page
lists the supported models, their cost, where the judge keeps its data and what to check in each license.

## Supported eyes

| `judge.eyes` | Model | Good at | Embedding | Time per image (Apple M5) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `siglip2-so400m` (default) | SigLIP 2 So400m, patch 14, 384 px | General images, UI with text | 1152 | about 25 ms |
| `siglip2-base` | SigLIP 2 Base, patch 16, 256 px | Fast first passes | 768 | about 8 ms |
| `dinov2-base` | DINOv2 Base, patch 14 | Shapes, layout, art style without text | 768 | about 15 ms |
| `uiclip` | UIClip | Web and app UI conventions | 512 | about 10 ms |

Switching eyes recomputes embeddings (10,000 images take about 5 to 10 minutes) and retrains heads (seconds each).

## Hardware

The judge runs the eyes with ONNX Runtime, on the GPU when one is available:

| Machine | Runs on |
|---|---|
| macOS on Apple silicon | GPU and Neural Engine through CoreML. |
| Windows with a DirectX 12 GPU | GPU through DirectML. |
| Linux with an NVIDIA GPU | GPU through CUDA. |
| Any machine without a supported GPU | CPU, about 5 to 10 times slower. |

## Where the data lives

| Data | Path | In git |
|---|---|---|
| Questions, heads, votes, gold sets | `judge.dir` (`scion/judge/`) | Yes (small JSON and JSONL) |
| Embeddings cache | `judge.cache` (`.scion/judge/`) | No |
| Model weights | the local model cache (`~/.cache/scion/models/`) | No |

Nothing leaves the machine: the judge makes no network calls after the model is downloaded.

## Licenses

- Check the model card of the eyes you use; SigLIP 2 and DINOv2 are published under Apache-2.0 at the time of
  writing, UIClip under its own terms.
- Heads trained on your votes are yours. Heads trained on third-party images (store screenshots, glitch datasets)
  are for internal use: do not ship their weights.
- If you use an agent to label pairs, follow the model provider's terms on using outputs for training.

## See also

- [The Judge](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/overview/)
- [Judge data files](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/judge-data/)
- [License](/scion/41664431a8f5/help/license/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# The multiverse

The multiverse replays a captured match up to turn N, forks it, and plays K variants from there: other grafts,
other tunables, other presets, other bots. Because the rules are deterministic, any difference is caused by the
variant. Scion reports, per variant, whether the rules diverged, the first turn and the first field that changed,
and shows the visuals side by side in a mosaic. It is how you prove a graft is only visual, and how you see what a
balance change does to a real match.

## When to use

- Before promoting a graft: run the match with and without it; nothing may diverge.
- When tuning rules: see the first turn where a new damage value changes the outcome.
- When a bug appears late in a match: fork just before it and try fixes.

## Before you begin

- Adoption level 3: the rules registered as an `ISimulation`, deterministic in plain .NET
  ([Find non-determinism](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/diagnose/)).
- A captured match ([Turn any match into a recipe](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/captured-matches/)).

## Steps

### 1. Fork and run

```sh
dotnet scion multiverse run knight-dies-to-crit --at-turn 2 --variants base,heavy,crit-1200
```

`crit-1200` is a preset that sets the rule tunable `Balance.CritPermille` to 1200.

<!-- validate: cli/multiverse -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"multiverse run","ok":true,"run":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/multiverse/20261012-101500","match":"knight-dies-to-crit","at_turn":2,"variants":[{"name":"base","diverged":false,"first_turn":null,"field":null},{"name":"heavy","diverged":false,"first_turn":null,"field":null},{"name":"crit-1200","diverged":true,"first_turn":3,"field":"units[0].hp"}],"report":"multiverse.json","mosaic":null,"next_step":"heavy is visual only; crit-1200 changes units[0].hp at turn 3: dotnet scion multiverse show 20261012-101500"}
```

### 2. Read the report

```sh
dotnet scion multiverse show 20261012-101500
```

`multiverse.json` has the hash of every turn for the base and each variant, and for diverged variants the field's
value before and after.

### 3. See it

```sh
dotnet scion multiverse run knight-dies-to-crit --at-turn 2 --variants base,heavy --mosaic
```

With `--mosaic`, the test build replays the variants side by side from the fork turn and writes `mosaic.png`.

## Reference

### Variants

| Kind | Given as | Changes |
|---|---|---|
| `preset` | a preset name or blend | tunables |
| `tunables` | `tunable:Balance.CritPermille=1200` | one or more tunables |
| `grafts` | `grafts:<dll>` | presentation code (the rules must not diverge) |
| `bot` | `bot:<name>` | who plays the remaining turns |

`--variants` takes a comma-separated list, or a JSON file with one object per variant.

### How it runs

1. The `ISimulation` replays the match's commands up to `--at-turn` and saves the state (`ISaveable`).
2. For each variant, it loads the state, applies the variant and plays the remaining commands (or the bot).
3. After every turn it records `Hash()`; the first turn whose hash differs from the base is `first_turn`.
4. At that turn, `IInspectable.Diff` names the first field that differs (`units[0].hp`).

Steps 1 to 4 run in plain .NET, in parallel, in milliseconds per turn. Only `--mosaic` starts the test build.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_simulation` | 3 | No `[assembly: Simulation]`. | Register an `ISimulation`. |
| `not_forkable` | 3 | The simulation does not implement `ISaveable`. | Implement `Save` and `Load` on the state. |
| `no_match` | 2 | The match file or a variant does not exist. | `trial list` shows captured matches. |
| variant `diverged` with `grafts` | 1 | A graft changed rules. | Move the change to the core ([Grafts are visual only](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/visual-only/)). |

## Examples

### Prove a draft graft is visual

```sh
dotnet scion multiverse run knight-dies-to-crit --at-turn 0 --variants base,grafts:.scion/grafts/ScionGrafts_51c2.dll
```

### Let bots finish the match

```sh
dotnet scion multiverse run knight-dies-to-crit --at-turn 2 --variants bot:aggressive,bot:cautious
```

## See also

- [multiverse (CLI)](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/multiverse/)
- [Turn any match into a recipe](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/captured-matches/)
- [Mosaic](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/mosaic/)
- [Core API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/core/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# The live loop

The live loop replays a short window of real play over and over in a test build: say turns 3 to 4 of a captured
match. Each graft injection applies at the start of the next pass, so you tune an effect while watching the exact
moment it belongs to. `dotnet scion trial loop` drives it; `graft watch` injects on every save.

## When to use

- Tuning feel on one moment: a crit, a unit falling, a turn banner.
- Reproducing a visual bug that needs a specific game state.

## Before you begin

- A captured match or a recipe's `telemetry.jsonl` with turn events.
- A test build (`dotnet scion build test`).

## Steps

### 1. Start the loop

```sh
dotnet scion trial loop "CapturedMatch[match=knight-dies-to-crit]" --span 3..4 --window
```

The test build opens in a window, replays the match to the start of turn 3 once, saves that state and then plays
turns 3 to 4 in a loop.

### 2. Edit and inject

In another terminal:

```sh
dotnet scion graft watch
```

Every save rebuilds the drafts and injects them; the next pass shows the change.

### 3. Stop

Press Ctrl-C in the loop's terminal, or pass `--passes N` to stop after N passes.

<!-- validate: cli/trial-loop -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"trial loop","ok":true,"run":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/loops/20261012-103000","id":"CapturedMatch[match=knight-dies-to-crit]","span":"3..4","passes":14,"injects":5,"last":{"ok":true,"hash":"9F3A0C11D2E4B5A6","frames":96,"window":"pass14/window.png"},"stopped_by":"interrupt","next_step":"dotnet scion graft promote CritShake"}
```

## Reference

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<Id>` | | A recipe id, usually a captured match. |
| `--from <file>` | the recipe's match | A `.match.json` or a `telemetry.jsonl` to take the window from. |
| `--span a..b` | the whole recipe | Turns to loop (inclusive). |
| `--passes N` | until stopped | Stop after N passes. |
| `--window` | headless | Show the window (usual for the loop). |

Every pass writes `pass<N>/` with `result.json`, `window.png` and telemetry, so you can compare passes with
`trial diff`. The hash of the loop must stay the same across passes; when an injected graft changes it, the loop
stops with `stopped_by: error`.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_simulation` | 3 | Restoring the state needs `ISaveable` on the rules. | Implement it, or loop a whole recipe (no `--span`). |
| `bad_value` | 2 | `--span` outside the match's turns. | Check `turns` in the match file. |
| stopped by `error` | 1 | A pass changed the hash. | The injected graft touches rules. |

## Examples

### Loop a whole short recipe

```sh
dotnet scion trial loop SlashHit --window
```

### Loop from a recipe's telemetry

```sh
dotnet scion trial loop KnightFalls --from .scion/runs/20261011-143200/q1/KnightFalls/r1/telemetry.jsonl --span 1..1
```

## See also

- [trial loop](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/trial-loop/)
- [Live injection](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/injection/)
- [Tune a hit effect](/scion/41664431a8f5/cookbook/tune-hit-feel/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Bisect a regression

When a recipe was right at an old commit and is wrong now, `dotnet scion bisect` finds the commit that changed it.
It drives `git bisect`: at each step it builds the test player cold, runs the recipe, and compares on what you
choose (`hash`, `pixels` or one check). A step that cannot decide (the build fails, the recipe is flaky) exits 125
and is skipped. It takes about log2(commits) steps.

## When to use

- A `changed` verdict nobody expected, or a check that started failing.
- Not for flaky recipes: fix determinism first, or bisect will skip most steps.

## Before you begin

- A clean working tree (bisect checks out commits).
- The recipe exists at both ends of the range (or comes from `--recipes`).

## Steps

### 1. Run it

```sh
dotnet scion bisect SlashHit --good v1.4.0 --on pixels
```

<!-- validate: cli/bisect -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"bisect","ok":true,"id":"SlashHit","good":"v1.4.0","bad":"HEAD","on":"pixels","steps":6,"skipped":["8c1f2d0"],"first_bad":{"commit":"5e7a913","subject":"Brighter hit flash material","date":"2026-10-09T17:20:00Z"},"log":".scion/bisect/20261012-110000/log.txt","next_step":"git show 5e7a913"}
```

### 2. Read the result

`first_bad` is the first commit where the recipe differs from `--good`. The log has each step's commit, build time,
verdict and decision.

## Reference

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<Id>` | | The recipe id. |
| `--good <rev>` | required | A revision where the recipe was right. |
| `--bad <rev>` | `HEAD` | A revision where it is wrong. |
| `--on hash` | `hash` | Compare the state hash with the good revision's. |
| `--on pixels` | | Compare images with the good revision's (same platform). |
| `--on check:<id>` | | Good when that check passes (`check:probe:damage`). |
| `--rounds N` | 2 | Rounds per step; all rounds must agree or the step is skipped. |

### Exit 125

Each step exits 0 (good), 1 (bad) or 125 (skip) to `git bisect run`. 125 means: the build failed, the recipe does
not exist at that commit, or rounds disagree. Too many skips leave a range instead of one commit; `first_bad` is then
null and the log lists the candidates.

### Cost

Every step is a cold build (Orchard: about 35 s on an Apple M5) plus the recipe. Ten commits take about 4 steps.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `usage` | 2 | The working tree has changes. | Commit or stash them. |
| `no_match` | 2 | The id does not exist at `--good`. | Use `--recipes` with a DLL that has it. |
| `first_bad: null` | 1 | Too many skipped steps. | Fix determinism or the build at the skipped commits. |

## Examples

### A check that started failing

```sh
dotnet scion bisect KnightFalls --good 3f2a0b1 --on check:order
```

### A rule change between two releases

```sh
dotnet scion bisect FireballArea --good v1.3.0 --bad v1.4.0 --on hash
```

## See also

- [bisect](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/bisect/)
- [Exit codes](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/exit-codes/)
- [Verify determinism](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/verify/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Metamorphic tests

A metamorphic test checks a relation between two runs instead of one expected value: mirroring the map must
mirror the result, swapping players must swap the result, turning visual effects off must not change the hash,
saving and loading mid-match must not change the hash. Scion runs them on the core simulator in plain .NET, over
many seeds, so they find rule bugs no single recipe would.

## When to use

- On every rule change, in CI: they are fast and need no Unity.
- When adding a mechanic with symmetry (positions, teams, turn order).

## Before you begin

- Adoption level 3 (`ISimulation` registered).
- The state implements the interface each property needs: `IMirrorable`, `IPermutable`, `ISaveable`.

## Steps

### 1. Declare the properties in a spec

```csharp
public sealed class RulesHold : TrialSpec
{
    public override string Name => "RulesHold";
    public override string Target => "Orchard's rules are symmetric and save-safe.";

    public override void Define(SpecBuilder s)
    {
        s.Metamorphic(Metamorphic.Mirror, matches: 200);
        s.Metamorphic(Metamorphic.Permute, matches: 200, players: 4);
        s.Metamorphic(Metamorphic.VisualToggle, matches: 50);
        s.Metamorphic(Metamorphic.SaveLoad, matches: 200);
    }
}
```

### 2. Run

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --spec RulesHold
```

A failure names the property, the seed, the turn and the field:

```text
Mirror: seed 117, turn 5: units[2].x is 3, mirrored run has 5 (expected 4)
```

### 3. Turn a failure into a recipe

```sh
dotnet scion hunt run RulesHold --seed 117 --save
```

saves the failing match to `scion/recipes/found/`.

## Reference

| Property | Relation | State needs |
|---|---|---|
| `Metamorphic.Mirror` | Run on the mirrored map; the final state equals the mirror of the original's. | `IMirrorable.Mirror()` |
| `Metamorphic.Permute` | Swap player seats; the result is permuted the same way. | `IPermutable.Permute(int[] order)` |
| `Metamorphic.VisualToggle` | Run in the test build with every promoted graft disabled; the hash is the same. | a test build |
| `Metamorphic.SaveLoad` | Save at a random turn, load, continue; the hash is the same. | `ISaveable.Save()`, `Load(byte[])` |

Matches are generated by bots from seeds 1 to `matches`. `VisualToggle` runs the recipes in the test build instead of
the simulator.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_simulation` | 3 | No `ISimulation`. | Register one ([Core API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/core/)). |
| spec `ok: false` | 1 | A property failed. | Read the seed, turn and field; save the match. |

## Examples

### Only save-load, many seeds

```csharp
s.Metamorphic(Metamorphic.SaveLoad, matches: 5000);
```

### A custom property

```csharp
s.Metamorphic("heal_then_hit_equals_hit_then_heal", (sim, seed) => HealOrder.Check(sim, seed), matches: 300);
```

## See also

- [Specs API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/specs/)
- [Core API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/core/)
- [Balance with the simulator](/scion/41664431a8f5/explore/balance/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Rare-moment hunter

Some situations happen once in a thousand matches: four units dying on one turn, a heal landing on a unit already
at zero, a crit on the last enemy while a banner is showing. The hunter plays matches on the core simulator with
bots and mutated commands, keeps the ones that reach new **features** (combinations of state the simulation
reports), and saves each new feature as a match file. Every find becomes a recipe you can capture, check and
approve.

## When to use

- Before a release, to find edge cases no one wrote a recipe for.
- After a new mechanic, to see what it combines with.

## Before you begin

- Adoption level 3 (`ISimulation` with `Features`).

## Steps

### 1. Report features from the simulation

```csharp
public IEnumerable<string> Features(OrchardState s)
{
    if (s.DiedThisTurn >= 3) yield return "multi_kill";
    if (s.LastHeal?.Target.Hp == 0) yield return "heal_on_zero";
    if (s.Turn > 30) yield return "long_match";
    yield return "units_alive:" + s.Alive;
}
```

### 2. Hunt

```sh
dotnet scion hunt run CoopTurn --budget 10
```

<!-- validate: cli/hunt-run -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"hunt run","ok":true,"target":"CoopTurn","budget_s":600,"states":184220,"features":41,"finds":[{"name":"multi_kill-0007","file":"scion/recipes/found/multi_kill-0007.match.json","feature":"multi_kill"},{"name":"heal_on_zero-0002","file":"scion/recipes/found/heal_on_zero-0002.match.json","feature":"heal_on_zero"}],"next_step":"dotnet scion trial run \"CapturedMatch[match=heal_on_zero-0002]\""}
```

### 3. Look at the finds

```sh
dotnet scion trial run "CapturedMatch[match=heal_on_zero-0002]"
```

Move the ones worth keeping to `scion/recipes/captured/` and approve them.

## Reference

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<Id\|Spec>` | | The recipe (its setup and players) or a spec whose `Balance` setup to start from. |
| `--budget <minutes>` | 5 | Time to search. |
| `--seed <n>` | random | Start seed, for repeatable hunts. |
| `--save` | on | Write finds to `scion/recipes/found/`. |

### How it searches

1. Start from bot matches with random seeds.
2. Keep a corpus of matches that produced a feature never seen before.
3. Mutate corpus matches: change one command, swap two, change a seed, cut and continue with a bot.
4. Prefer mutations of matches whose features are rare.

One find is saved per new feature, minimized to the fewest turns that still produce it.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_simulation` | 3 | No `ISimulation`. | Register one. |
| `finds: []` | 0 | Nothing new in the budget. | Report more specific features, or raise `--budget`. |

## Examples

### A long hunt overnight

```sh
dotnet scion hunt run CoopTurn --budget 480
```

### Repeat a hunt exactly

```sh
dotnet scion hunt run CoopTurn --budget 10 --seed 42
```

## See also

- [hunt, search](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/hunt-and-search/)
- [Turn any match into a recipe](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/captured-matches/)
- [Core API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/core/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Guided search

Tuning by hand stops at a few knobs. Guided search explores many: it proposes tunable values with paired Bayesian
optimization, keeps a **MAP-Elites gallery** of the best option in each niche (fast and light, slow and heavy...),
lets the judge drop the clearly worse ones, and asks a person only the duels that decide. The result is a small set
of good, different options, ready to save as presets.

## When to use

- Feel with 4 to 15 tunables (a hit effect, a camera, a UI transition).
- Balance values when a spec defines success.

## Before you begin

- The tunables, with ranges ([Tunables and presets](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/tunables/)).
- A spec that says what is acceptable (`Visual(...).Expect(...)`), and a judge head for the taste part.

## Steps

### 1. Search

```sh
dotnet scion search run StrongerCrits --tunables CritShake.Strength,CritShake.Stop,HitFlash.Seconds --budget 60 --duels 20
```

<!-- validate: cli/search-run -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"search run","ok":true,"spec":"StrongerCrits","tunables":["CritShake.Strength","CritShake.Stop","HitFlash.Seconds"],"evaluated":60,"duels":20,"gallery":".scion/search/20261012-120000/search.json","best":[{"name":"g07","values":{"CritShake.Strength":0.62,"CritShake.Stop":0.08,"HitFlash.Seconds":0.09},"score":0.81},{"name":"g12","values":{"CritShake.Strength":0.35,"CritShake.Stop":0.04,"HitFlash.Seconds":0.05},"score":0.77}],"next_step":"save a winner: copy its values to scion/presets/<name>.json"}
```

### 2. Vote the duels

`search run` opens the duel page when it needs a person (`--duels` caps how many). Without a person, it stops after
the judge's ranking and lists the pending duels.

### 3. Keep the winners

Copy the values of the options you like into presets (`scion/presets/punchy.json`), and use them in recipes and specs.

## Reference

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<Spec>` | | The spec that defines acceptable results. |
| `--tunables a,b` | every tunable the spec's recipes use | What to search. |
| `--budget <n>` | 40 | Variants to evaluate. |
| `--duels <n>` | 10 | Maximum duels to ask a person. |
| `--niches a,b` | `hit_stop_ms,shake_peak_px` | Metrics that define the gallery's niches. |

### Loop

1. Propose a batch of variants (Bayesian optimization over pairs: it models which of two variants wins).
2. Run them as recipe variants in the test build (`--motion`).
3. Drop variants that fail the spec's gates or bounds.
4. Rank the rest with the judge; place each in its niche of the gallery if it beats the current one.
5. Ask a person the duels where the judge is least sure; their votes update the model and train the head.

`search.json` holds the gallery: every niche with its best variant, values, score and image.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bad_value` | 2 | A tunable has no range. | Add `[Tunable(min, max)]` (SCN005). |
| `model_missing` | 3 | The spec's judge head is not trained. | Train it, or remove `Judge` from the spec. |

## Examples

### A balance search on the simulator

```sh
dotnet scion search run CoopFloor3 --tunables Balance.CritPermille,Balance.EnemyHpPermille --budget 200 --duels 0
```

With `--duels 0` and a balance-only spec, the search runs entirely in plain .NET.

### Gallery niches by color and speed

```sh
dotnet scion search run StrongerCrits --niches flash_delta_l,hit_stop_ms
```

## See also

- [hunt, search](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/hunt-and-search/)
- [Tunables and presets](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/tunables/)
- [Taste heads and feel presets](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/presets/)

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Balance with the simulator

Balance questions ("is floor 1 easy enough?", "does four-player co-op get too easy?") need thousands of matches,
not one recipe. Balance specs run the rules as an `ISimulation` in plain .NET with bots, for 1 to 4 players, in
seconds, and check bounds on metrics such as win rate and match length. A difficulty curve spec checks a whole
progression at once. Bots shape the curve; telemetry from real players sets its level.

## When to use

- After every change to rules data (damage tables, enemy stats, floor depth).
- To compare balance presets before playtesting.

## Before you begin

- Adoption level 3: the rules in an assembly without engine references, with `ISimulation` and at least one `IBot`.

## Steps

### 1. Write a curve spec

```csharp
public sealed class DifficultyCurve : TrialSpec
{
    public override string Name => "DifficultyCurve";
    public override string Target => "Starts easy, ends hard, for 1 to 4 players.";

    public override void Define(SpecBuilder s)
    {
        for (int players = 1; players <= 4; players++)
            s.Curve("floors", levels: 6, players: players, matches: 500)
             .ExpectAt(1, "win_rate", min: 0.95)
             .ExpectAt(6, "win_rate", min: 0.35, max: 0.55)
             .Monotonic("win_rate", decreasing: true)
             .MaxStep("win_rate", 0.15);
    }
}
```

### 2. Run it

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --spec DifficultyCurve
```

Each player count runs 6 x 500 matches with the registered bots. On an Apple M5, Orchard's 12,000 matches take
about 40 seconds.

### 3. Read the curve

The spec's report lists win rate per floor and player count, and the bounds that failed:

```text
players=4  floor 1 0.99  floor 2 0.93  floor 3 0.90  floor 4 0.71  floor 5 0.52  floor 6 0.41
           failed: MaxStep win_rate 0.19 between floors 3 and 4
```

## Reference

### What a balance run needs from the core

| Member | Use |
|---|---|
| `ISimulation.Reset(seed, setup)` | A new match. |
| `ISimulation.LegalCommands`, `Apply`, `Done` | The bots play through them. |
| `ISimulation.Metrics` | `win_rate`, `turns`, and the game's own metrics (`damage_taken`, `heals_used`). |
| `IBot` with `[Bot("name")]` | Players with a style (`aggressive`, `cautious`, `random`). |

### Bots are not people

Bots of different styles shape the curve: if every style finds floor 6 equally hard, the curve's shape holds. The
level of the curve (how hard is hard) comes from telemetry of real matches: compare the spec's win rate with the win
rate players had, and set the bounds from that.

### Searching balance

With bounds in a spec, guided search can tune the rules data automatically
([Guided search](/scion/41664431a8f5/explore/guided-search/)).

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_simulation` | 3 | No `ISimulation`. | Register one. |
| spec `ok: false` | 1 | A bound failed. | Read the report; change data or the bounds (in a new spec). |

## Examples

### One floor, four players

```csharp
s.Balance("Floor3", players: 4, matches: 1000).Expect("win_rate", min: 0.6, max: 0.75);
```

### Compare two balance presets

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --spec DifficultyCurve --variants base,enemy-hp-90
```

## See also

- [Specs](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/specs/)
- [Specs API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/specs/)
- [Core API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/core/)

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# The Scion Standard

The Scion Standard is a small set of rules for how a Unity game is organized so that Scion, people and agents can
extend it safely. Its five principles say where rules live and how they change; its six layers (Core, Presentation,
Grafts, Adapters, Trials, Tests) say what may depend on what. Analyzers SCN001 to SCN005, `doctor` and the scaffolds
of `scion new` enforce it; nothing in it is required to use grafts or trials, but every rule you follow makes the
adapter thinner and unlocks more of Scion.

## How it works

### Five principles

1. **Rules are explicit in the core.** Plain C#, deterministic, integer math, extended by registration
   (`RuleModifier<T>`), never by IL weaving.
2. **Weaving happens only in presentation.** Grafts are visual; deleting the grafts folder still compiles and plays
   the same.
3. **Shallow inheritance, content as data.** A new enemy or ability is a data row plus a registered strategy, not a
   subclass tree.
4. **Commands go down, events come up.** Presentation sends commands to the core and reacts to its events; the
   methods that react are the anchors.
5. **Types, analyzers and `doctor` enforce the standard**, not long text files. Context files alone help little and
   cost tokens on every request.

### Six layers

| Layer | Contains | May depend on |
|---|---|---|
| Core | Rules, state, commands, events, rule tunables, the `ISimulation` | nothing of Unity |
| Presentation | Views, HUD, camera, audio, the `Fx` sink | Core |
| Grafts | `[Before]`/`[After]` methods, presentation tunables | Presentation, Core (read only) |
| Adapters | `TrialAdapter<T>`, network and input ports | Core, Presentation |
| Trials | Recipes, checks, specs | Adapters, Core |
| Tests | `dotnet test` projects, completeness tests | anything |

The dependency rule: arrows point down the table and never back up. Nothing depends on Grafts (SCN110); the Core
depends on nothing of Unity (an assembly with `noEngineReferences: true`).

### In Orchard

| Layer | Orchard |
|---|---|
| Core | `Orchard.Core`: `BattleState`, `Command`, `DamageCalc`, `BackstabBonus : RuleModifier<DamageCalc>` |
| Presentation | `Orchard.Runtime`: `HitPresenter`, `Hud`, `CameraRig`, `DamageNumbers`, `OrchardFxSink` |
| Grafts | `Assets/Orchard/Grafts`: `HitFlash`, `CritShake`, `DamageNumberPop`, `TurnBanner` |
| Adapters | `OrchardAdapter`, `OrchardMatchCapture` |
| Trials | `Orchard.Trials`: `SlashHit`, `CoopTurn`, `HudStates`; `Trials/Specs` |
| Tests | `Tests/Orchard.Core.Tests`, `Tests/Orchard.Grafts.Tests` |

## Key terms

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Core | The rules assembly, listed in `analyzers.rule_assemblies`. |
| Rule code | Code in the core; follows SCN001, SCN002 and SCN004. |
| Primitive | One of the standard's building blocks ([Primitives](/scion/41664431a8f5/standard/primitives/)). |
| Exemplar | A small, compiled, tested example in the project that agents copy. |
| Completeness test | A test that every enum value has a handler, every enemy a presentation. |

## Guarantees and limits

- Following the standard is gradual: each rule stands alone, and `doctor` reports the adoption level.
- The analyzers only report on assemblies you list; third-party code is never checked.
- Deviations are allowed with a justification, through the normal Roslyn suppression.

## See also

- [Rules R1-R8](/scion/41664431a8f5/standard/rules/)
- [Primitives](/scion/41664431a8f5/standard/primitives/)
- [Enforcement](/scion/41664431a8f5/standard/enforcement/)
- [Grafts are visual only](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/visual-only/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Rules R1-R8

Each rule below has a statement, the reason, an example from Orchard and how Scion checks it. Rules are numbered for
reference in reviews and in agent instructions ("this breaks R3"). Analyzer ids are in
[SCN001-SCN005](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/standard/).

## R1 Inherit one level from a Scion base, sealed

**Why.** The base controls the flow (Template Method), so subclasses cannot get it wrong, and `sealed` lets IL2CPP
devirtualize calls.

```csharp
public sealed class OrchardAdapter : TrialAdapter<OrchardRecipe> { /* ... */ }
public sealed class BackstabBonus : RuleModifier<DamageCalc> { /* ... */ }
public sealed class HudStates : StaticTrial<HudState> { /* ... */ }
```

**Enforced by** SCN001 (not sealed) and SCN002 (more than one level) in rule code.

## R2 Anchors take values, not services

**Why.** An anchor method whose parameters are plain values (`HitEvent`, `int turn`) gives grafts everything they
need without reaching into services, and keeps grafts testable with `new Call<T>(...)`.

```csharp
public float Play(HitEvent e)   // HitEvent is a readonly struct: attacker, target, amount, crit
```

**Enforced by** review and the exemplars; `anchor show` prints the signature grafts bind to.

## R3 Rules that change numbers are RuleModifier

**Why.** A rule change registered explicitly with a stage, a priority and integers is visible, ordered and the same
on every peer. A graft that changed it would vanish outside Unity.

```csharp
public sealed class BackstabBonus : RuleModifier<DamageCalc>
{
    public override Stage Stage => Stage.Mul;
    public override int Priority => 10;
    public override void Apply(ref DamageCalc c) { if (c.FromBehind) c.MulPermille += 500; }
}
```

**Enforced by** SCN003 (a graft writes rule state), SCN004 (`float` in rule code: use `int` or permille so every
machine computes the same result) and the hash A/B run.

## R4 New content is a Type Object plus a strategy by enum

**Why.** A new ability is a data row and one case in a strategy, so completeness can be tested: every enum value has
a handler.

```csharp
public enum AbilityEffect { Damage, Heal, Push }
public static int Resolve(AbilityEffect e, ref DamageCalc c) => e switch
{
    AbilityEffect.Damage => Damage.Apply(ref c),
    AbilityEffect.Heal => Heal.Apply(ref c),
    AbilityEffect.Push => Push.Apply(ref c),
    _ => throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(e)),
};
```

**Enforced by** completeness tests generated by `scion new effect`.

## R5 Interfaces only for context and optional capabilities

**Why.** Interfaces such as `ISaveable` or `IMirrorable` say what the state can do; using them for everything adds
indirection without value. Serialized types avoid `record` and `init`, which Unity's serializer does not support.

**Enforced by** review and `doctor`'s capability report.

## R6 Every mutation is a Command

**Why.** Commands can be logged, replayed, captured with F9, forked in the multiverse and sent over the network.
Event dispatch is a `switch` calling named methods, and those methods become anchors.

```csharp
battle.Issue(Command.Ability("slash", attacker: 0, target: 1));
```

**Enforced by** level 3 requirements: `ISimulation.Apply(command)` is the only way to change state.

## R7 The adapter is a Template Method

**Why.** One public, non-virtual entry point per job (build state, apply a command, hash) keeps adapters small and
the same across games.

**Enforced by** `TrialAdapter<TRecipe>` and the skeleton `diagnose --adapter` writes.

## R8 Helpers by composition

**Why.** A thin facade object (`Fx`) gives every graft the same verbs without a fat base class. Extension methods
only on struct contexts.

**Enforced by** the `Fx` facade and the exemplars.

## See also

- [The Scion Standard](/scion/41664431a8f5/standard/overview/)
- [Enforcement](/scion/41664431a8f5/standard/enforcement/)
- [SCN001-SCN005](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/standard/)
- [Core API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/core/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Primitives

A primitive is a building block with one job. Choosing the right one is most of following the standard: a number
that changes a rule is a `RuleModifier<T>`, a sound on a hit is a graft, a number someone will tune is a
`[Tunable]`. This page lists each primitive, when to use it and where it is documented.

## Table

| Primitive | Use it for | Never for | Docs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[Anchor(Id, Doc)]` | Stable, documented presentation moments agents should find first. | Rule methods. | [Anchors](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/anchors/) |
| Graft (`[Before]`/`[After]`) | Juice, sound, camera, HUD, telemetry, tutorial hints. | Changing a rule. | [Write a graft](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/write/) |
| `RuleModifier<T>` + `Stage` | Any rule that changes a number (damage, range, cost). | Presentation. | [Core API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/core/) |
| Strategy by enum | Effects, AI choices, presentation per effect. | Open-ended plugins. | [Rules R1-R8](/scion/41664431a8f5/standard/rules/) |
| Type Object | Immutable definitions: abilities, units, rooms (data rows, or a ScriptableObject compiled to a table). | State that changes during a match. | [Rules R1-R8](/scion/41664431a8f5/standard/rules/) |
| `[Tunable(min, max)]` | A number someone tunes; on rule fields, it enters the lobby hash. | Constants nobody tunes. | [Tunables and presets](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/tunables/) |
| `[Probe("key")]` | A rule value recorded in trials. | Per-frame values (use a sensor). | [Telemetry, probes and sensors](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/telemetry/) |
| Cue | A visual triggered by an event, one-shot or added and removed (a burning aura). | Logic. | below |
| Adapter | The game's port: trials, network, input. | Game rules. | [Write an adapter](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/adapters/) |
| Exemplar | A small compiled, tested example per primitive for agents to copy. | Documentation prose. | below |

## Stages of a rule modifier

| Stage | Order | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| `Stage.Base` | 1 | Set the base value from data. |
| `Stage.Add` | 2 | Flat bonuses. |
| `Stage.Mul` | 3 | Multipliers in permille (`MulPermille += 500` is +50 %). |
| `Stage.Clamp` | 4 | Minimums, maximums, immunities. |
| `Stage.Final` | 5 | Last-word effects (shields that absorb). |

Within a stage, `Priority` orders modifiers (lower first), then the type's full name.

## Cues

A cue is a pattern, not a type: a presentation method that reacts to one core event, named after it, and therefore
an anchor.

```csharp
public sealed class StatusCues : MonoBehaviour
{
    public void OnBurnAdded(int unit) => Auras.Add(unit, "burn");
    public void OnBurnRemoved(int unit) => Auras.Remove(unit, "burn");
}
```

Grafts on `OnBurnAdded` add sound or shake without touching the status system.

## Exemplars

`Assets/Orchard/Exemplars/` holds one file per primitive (`ExemplarGraft.cs`, `ExemplarModifier.cs`,
`ExemplarRecipe.cs`...), compiled with the project and covered by a test. `scion new` copies from them, and the
project index points agents to them.

## See also

- [Rules R1-R8](/scion/41664431a8f5/standard/rules/)
- [Core API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/core/)
- [Grafts API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/grafts/)
- [Enforcement](/scion/41664431a8f5/standard/enforcement/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Enforcement

The standard is enforced by tools, not by long text: Roslyn analyzers (SCN001 to SCN005, plus SCN003 and SCN110 for
grafts) report in the IDE and in Unity, scoped to the assemblies you list in `ScionSettings.json`; `doctor` reports
the adoption level and what is missing; `scion new` scaffolds code that already passes; completeness tests catch
missing handlers. This guide sets them up.

## When to use

- When adopting the standard in a project: set the scope first, then fix warnings gradually.
- When reviewing agent changes: the analyzers and tests catch most deviations before review.

## Steps

### 1. Scope the analyzers

`ProjectSettings/ScionSettings.json`:

```json
{"schema_version":1,"analyzers":{"rule_assemblies":["Orchard.Core"],"rule_types":["Unity.Netcode.*"],"graft_paths":["Assets/Orchard/Grafts/","../scion/grafts/"]}}
```

Only the assemblies in `rule_assemblies` get SCN001, SCN002, SCN004 and SCN005. Recompile after editing.

### 2. Scaffold new code

```sh
dotnet scion new feature Burn
dotnet scion new effect Push
dotnet scion new graft BurnAuraSound --after Orchard.Presentation.StatusCues.OnBurnAdded
dotnet scion new trial BurnTicks
```

Each command writes code that compiles and passes `doctor`, copied from the project's exemplars: a feature gets its
modifier, its data row and a recipe; an effect gets its enum case, its strategy and a completeness test entry.

### 3. Check the project

```sh
dotnet scion doctor --level 3
```

## Reference

### Analyzers

| Id | Severity | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| SCN001 | warning | A class in rule code is not sealed (R1). |
| SCN002 | warning | A class in rule code inherits more than one level (R1). |
| SCN003 | error | A graft writes rule state (R3). |
| SCN004 | warning | `float` in rule code (R3). |
| SCN005 | warning | A numeric `[Tunable]` without a range. |
| SCN110 | error | Game code calls a graft. |

The analyzers ship in the package (`Scion.Analyzers`, labeled `RoslynAnalyzer`), so Unity and IDEs that read Unity's
generated projects run them. For `dotnet build` outside Unity, add the `Scion.Testing` package, which carries them.

### Suppressing a deviation

```csharp
[SuppressMessage("Scion", "SCN002", Justification = "Netcode requires NetworkBehaviour as the base")]
public sealed class TurnSync : TurnSyncBase { }
```

or `#pragma warning disable SCN004` around the lines. `doctor` lists every suppression with its justification.

### Completeness tests

`scion new effect` adds the effect to `Tests/Orchard.Core.Tests/Completeness.cs`:

```csharp
[Fact]
public void Every_effect_has_a_handler()
{
    foreach (AbilityEffect e in Enum.GetValues(typeof(AbilityEffect)))
        Assert.True(Effects.Handles(e), $"{e} has no handler");
}
```

Other completeness tests in the template: every unit kind has a presentation, every status has cues, every rule
tunable has a range.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SCN001`-`SCN005` | compile warning or error | See the table above. | Follow the hint, or suppress with a justification. |
| `bad_value` | 2 | `scion new` with an unknown kind. | Use `feature`, `effect`, `graft` or `trial`. |

## Examples

### Fail CI on standard warnings in the core

```sh
dotnet build Trials/Specs/Orchard.Specs.csproj -warnaserror:SCN001,SCN002,SCN004,SCN005
```

### Preview a scaffold

```sh
dotnet scion new feature Burn --dry-run
```

## See also

- [SCN001-SCN005](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/diagnostics/standard/)
- [init, new, uninstall](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/init/)
- [doctor](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/doctor/)
- [Rules R1-R8](/scion/41664431a8f5/standard/rules/)

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# CLI overview

`dotnet scion` is Scion's command line, a local .NET tool (`Scion.Cli`). Every command has the form
`dotnet scion <noun> <verb>`, prints one JSON envelope outside a terminal (text inside one), always says the
`next_step`, and exits 0, 1, 2 or 3. This page covers installation, the global options (`--format`, `--dry-run`,
`--help`, `--version`), how the CLI finds the project root (`scion.json`), the test build (`--build`, `SCION_BUILD`),
Unity and the editor, the envelope and the exit-code precedence.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion <command> [<verb>] [arguments] [options] [-- player-args]
dotnet scion --help | --version
```

| Command | Verbs | Page |
|---|---|---|
| `doctor` | | [doctor](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/doctor/) |
| `init`, `new`, `uninstall` | | [init, new, uninstall](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/init/) |
| `build` | `test`, `final` | [build test, build final](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/build/) |
| `trial` (alias `trials`) | `list`, `run`, `show`, `approve`, `serve`, `diff`, `eval`, `loop` | [trial run](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/trial-run/) and siblings |
| `anchor` | `list`, `show` | [anchor list, anchor show](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/anchor/) |
| `graft` | `new`, `check`, `build`, `inject`, `restore`, `disable`, `promote`, `watch` | [graft](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/graft/) |
| `bisect` | | [bisect](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/bisect/) |
| `diagnose` | | [diagnose](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/diagnose/) |
| `index`, `guard` | | [index, guard](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/index-and-guard/) |
| `gen` | | [gen](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/gen/) |
| `judge` | `list`, `show`, `new`, `vote`, `train`, `run` | [judge](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/judge/) |
| `multiverse` | `run`, `show` | [multiverse](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/multiverse/) |
| `hunt`, `search` | `run` | [hunt, search](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/hunt-and-search/) |
| `mcp` | | [mcp](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/mcp/) |

## Description

### Install

```sh
dotnet new tool-manifest            # once per repository, if there is no .config/dotnet-tools.json
dotnet tool install --local Scion.Cli --version 1.0.0
dotnet tool restore                  # on another machine
```

The CLI and the package must have the same version: a DLL injected into a build of another weaver ABI is refused
(SCN131), and `doctor` warns `version_mismatch`.

### How it finds things

| What | Order |
|---|---|
| Project root | The nearest folder upward with `scion.json`. |
| Configuration | `scion.json`, deep-merged with `scion.local.json` (local wins). |
| Test build | `--build <app\|exe\|folder>`, then `SCION_BUILD`, then `scion.local.json`, then `build.test.output.<os>` in `scion.json`. `scion-build.json` must sit next to it. |
| Unity | The version in `ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt`, at the Hub's default path for the OS; `unity.editor` in `scion.local.json` overrides. |
| Editor open | `Temp/UnityLockfile` locked. Builds then go through the open editor (needs `com.unity.pipeline`) or stop with `editor_open`. |
| Ports | A free port per co-op group and per control channel (bind to 0, release). |

### Behavior every command shares

- Commands that write accept `--dry-run` and are idempotent: running one twice changes nothing the second time.
- Output is compact JSON (about 1.5 KB at most): long lists are cut with `"more": N`, and the full data goes to a
  file (`summary.json`) whose path is in the envelope.
- Arguments after `--` go to every player process; a flag also present in `player_args` replaces it.

## Options

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--format json\|text` | `json` outside a TTY, `text` in one | Output format. |
| `--dry-run` | off | Print what would change; change nothing. |
| `--build <path>` | discovery | The test build to use (commands that run players). |
| `--help`, `-h` | | Help for the command. |
| `--version` | | `1.0.0`. |

## Output

Every command prints one envelope:

<!-- validate: envelope -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"trial run","ok":false,"next_step":"run: dotnet scion build test","error":{"code":"build_not_found","message":"no test build at /Users/alex/orchard/.scion/builds/test/Orchard.app","hint":"run: dotnet scion build test","did_you_mean":[]}}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `schema_version` | 1. |
| `command` | The command as typed, without options (`trial run`). |
| `ok` | True when the exit code is 0. |
| `next_step` | One line: what to do next. Always present. |
| `warnings[]` | `{code, message}`; never change the exit code. |
| `error` | Only on exit 2 and 3: `code`, `message`, `hint`, `did_you_mean`. |
| command fields | Documented on each command's page and in its JSON Schema. |

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Everything ok (warnings do not count). |
| 1 | A recipe, check, graft check or spec failed. |
| 2 | Usage: unknown command, option or value; nothing matched. |
| 3 | Environment: no build, no Unity, a player crashed, a copy timed out. |

When several copies or steps end differently, the command exits with the highest-priority code: 2, then 3, then 1,
then 0. See [Exit codes](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/exit-codes/).

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `config_not_found` | 2 | No `scion.json` above the current folder. | `dotnet scion init`, or `cd` into the project. |
| `config_invalid` | 3 | `scion.json` does not match its schema. | Fix the key in the message. |
| `unknown_command`, `unknown_option` | 2 | A typo. | Use `did_you_mean`. |
| `build_not_found` | 3 | No test build found. | `dotnet scion build test`. |
| `unity_not_found` | 3 | No Unity of the project's version. | Set `unity.editor` in `scion.local.json`. |

Every code: [Error and warning codes](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/).

## Examples

### Text output in a script

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --format text
```

### Pick a build for one command

```sh
SCION_BUILD=/tmp/orchard-test/Orchard.app dotnet scion trial list
```

## See also

- [Install](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/install/)
- [Reading results](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/reading-results/)
- [Exit codes](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/exit-codes/)
- [Error and warning codes](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/)
- [Configuration](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/configuration/)

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# doctor

`dotnet scion doctor` checks that everything Scion needs is in place and says what to do about anything that is not.
It reports one check per line with a `hint`, the suggested number of parallel copies for this machine, the
project's adoption level (`adoption_level`, 1 to 3) and the next step to the next level (`adoption_next`).
`--level` sets how deep the checks go.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion doctor [--level 1|2|3] [--format json|text]
```

## Description

| Level | Checks |
|---|---|
| 1 (default) | `scion.json` and `ScionSettings.json` parse; CLI and package versions match; .NET SDK; Unity of the project's version; the editor lock. |
| 2 | Level 1, plus: the test build exists, has `SCION_TRIALS`, is not stale; `scion-build.json` reads; the output folder is writable; free memory and cores. |
| 3 | Level 2, plus: starts the test build with `-scion-list` (recipes, adapters, SCN201 to SCN203); the judge's eye model; Git LFS for baselines; suppressions with justifications. |

Each check has an `id`, a `status` (`ok`, `warn`, `fail`), a `detail` and, unless ok, a `hint`.

`suggested_copies` is the smaller of (cores - 1) and (free memory / memory per copy), using the last run's
measurement or 600 MB.

## Options

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--level 1\|2\|3` | 1 | Check depth (not the adoption level). |
| `--format json\|text` | auto | Output format. |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/doctor -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"doctor","ok":true,"level":2,"version":"1.0.0","adoption_level":2,"adoption_next":"level 3: register an ISimulation over Orchard.Core (see Core API)","checks":[{"id":"config","status":"ok","detail":"/Users/alex/orchard/scion.json"},{"id":"versions","status":"ok","detail":"CLI 1.0.0, package 1.0.0"},{"id":"unity","status":"ok","detail":"6000.3.25f1"},{"id":"build","status":"ok","detail":".scion/builds/test/Orchard.app (4c49a1e0b2f3)"},{"id":"machine","status":"ok","detail":"10 cores, 9.1 GB free of 16.0 GB"}],"suggested_copies":6,"next_step":"dotnet scion trial run -j 6"}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `level` | The check depth that ran. |
| `version` | The CLI version. |
| `adoption_level` | 1 grafts, 2 trials, 3 multiverse. |
| `adoption_next` | What is missing for the next level, or null at 3. |
| `checks[]` | `id`, `status`, `detail`, `hint`. |
| `suggested_copies` | For `trial run -j`. |

Schema: `https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/schemas/v1/cli/doctor.schema.json`.

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | No check failed (warnings allowed). |
| 2 | Bad option. |
| 3 | A check failed. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `config_not_found` | 2 | No `scion.json`. | `dotnet scion init`. |
| warning `version_mismatch` | 0 | The CLI and the package differ. | Install the same version of both. |
| warning `build_stale` | 0 | The test build is older than the sources. | `dotnet scion build test`. |
| warning `low_memory` | 0 | Not enough free memory for 2 copies. | Close apps or run `-j 1`. |
| `model_missing` | 3 | Level 3: the judge's eye model is not downloaded. | Run the command in `hint`. |

## Examples

### The deepest check

```sh
dotnet scion doctor --level 3
```

### Only the failing checks, in a script

```sh
dotnet scion doctor --format json | jq '.checks[] | select(.status != "ok")'
```

## See also

- [Install](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/install/)
- [Parallel copies](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/parallel/)
- [Find non-determinism](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/diagnose/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# init, new, uninstall

Three commands manage Scion in a project. `dotnet scion init` adds Scion to an existing Unity project (`scion.json`,
`ScionSettings.json`, the grafts folder and `.asmref`, `.gitignore` entries, the agent integration). `dotnet scion
new` creates a whole project from a genre template, or scaffolds a feature, effect, graft or trial inside one.
`dotnet scion uninstall` removes what `init` added. All three accept `--dry-run` and report `created`, `changed`,
`removed` and `skipped` files.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion init [--existing] [--agent claude|codex|cursor|none] [--game-assembly <name>] [--grafts-folder <path>] [--dry-run]
dotnet scion new --genre tactics|action|platformer|blank --name <Name> [--players 1-4] [--dry-run]
dotnet scion new feature|effect|graft|trial <Name> [--after|--before <Type.Method>] [--dry-run]
dotnet scion uninstall [--purge] [--dry-run]
```

## Description

`init` never overwrites: an existing file is listed in `skipped`. `uninstall` reverses `init` and keeps your grafts,
recipes and baselines unless `--purge`.

## init

| Creates or changes | Content |
|---|---|
| `scion.json` | Paths, defaults and builds for this project. |
| `ProjectSettings/ScionSettings.json` | `build.main_assembly`, analyzer scope. |
| `Assets/<Game>/Grafts/<Game>.Grafts.asmref` | Points the grafts folder at the game assembly. |
| `Packages/manifest.json` | Adds `me.jandson.scion` if missing. |
| `.config/dotnet-tools.json` | Adds `Scion.Cli`. |
| `.gitignore` | `.scion/`, `scion.local.json`, `Library/Scion/`. |
| `.gitattributes` | LFS for `scion/baselines/**/*.png`. |
| agent files | With `--agent claude`: the plugin's hooks in `.claude/settings.json` and `CLAUDE.md` pointing to the index. |

`--existing` is required when the project already has scripts: `init` then asks (or takes `--game-assembly`) which
assembly is the game.

## new

| Form | Creates |
|---|---|
| `new --genre tactics --name Orchard --players 4` | A Unity project at level 3: core with `ISimulation`, presentation, grafts, adapter, recipes, specs, tests, exemplars. |
| `new feature <Name>` | A `RuleModifier<T>`, its data row, a recipe and a completeness entry. |
| `new effect <Name>` | An enum case, its strategy, a cue, a completeness entry. |
| `new graft <Name> --after <Type.Method>` | A promoted graft with the right signature (drafts use `graft new`). |
| `new trial <Name>` | A recipe for the project's adapter, with checks. |

Genres: `tactics` (turn-based, grid), `action` (real time), `platformer`, `blank` (only the layers).

## uninstall

Removes `scion.json`, `ScionSettings.json`, the `.asmref`, the package and tool entries and the agent files. With
`--purge`, also `scion/` (drafts, recipes, presets, baselines, judge data) and `.scion/`.

## Options

| Option | Commands | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--existing` | init | Adopt a project with scripts. |
| `--agent <name>` | init | Agent integration: `claude` (default), `codex`, `cursor`, `none`. |
| `--game-assembly <name>` | init | The game assembly, without asking. |
| `--grafts-folder <path>` | init | Default `Assets/<Game>/Grafts`. |
| `--genre`, `--name`, `--players` | new | Project template. |
| `--after`, `--before` | new graft | The target. |
| `--purge` | uninstall | Also delete Scion data. |
| `--dry-run` | all | Change nothing. |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/init -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"init","ok":true,"dry_run":false,"created":["scion.json","ProjectSettings/ScionSettings.json","Assets/Orchard/Grafts/Orchard.Grafts.asmref"],"changed":["Packages/manifest.json",".gitignore",".gitattributes",".config/dotnet-tools.json"],"skipped":[],"adoption_level":1,"next_step":"dotnet scion doctor"}
```

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Done (or nothing to do). |
| 2 | Bad option, or `init` without `--existing` in a project with scripts. |
| 3 | A file could not be written. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `usage` | 2 | `init` in a project with scripts and no `--existing`. | Add `--existing`. |
| `config_invalid` | 3 | An existing `scion.json` is invalid. | Fix it; `init` never overwrites. |
| `bad_value` | 2 | Unknown genre or kind. | Use one of the listed values. |

## Examples

### Preview init in an existing project

```sh
dotnet scion init --existing --game-assembly Orchard.Runtime --dry-run
```

### A four-player tactics project

```sh
dotnet scion new --genre tactics --name Orchard --players 4
```

## See also

- [Start a new project](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/new-project/)
- [Add Scion to an existing game](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/existing-project/)
- [Enforcement](/scion/41664431a8f5/standard/enforcement/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# build test, build final

`dotnet scion build test` builds the test player (Mono, `SCION_SLOTS` and `SCION_TRIALS`) and writes
`scion-build.json` next to it; `dotnet scion build final` builds the shipping player without test defines. The CLI
runs Unity in batchmode with `build.test.method` or `build.final.method` from `scion.json`, or, when the editor is
open and `com.unity.pipeline` is installed, builds through the open editor. Compile errors come back with file,
line and code.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion build test  [--out <dir>] [--dry-run]
dotnet scion build final [--out <dir>] [--dry-run]
```

## Description

1. Finds Unity and checks the editor lock.
2. Closed editor: runs `Unity -batchmode -quit -projectPath <unity_project> -executeMethod <method> -scion-build-out <dir>`.
   Open editor with the pipeline package: writes `Temp/Scion/ScionBuildEntry.cs` and runs it in the editor.
3. Reads the `BUILD_RESULT` line and the log, and collects compile errors and SCN diagnostics.
4. On success, reads `scion-build.json` and prints the build id.

The output folder defaults to `build.test.output.<os>` (or `build.final.output.<os>`) in `scion.json`.

## build test

Builds with `ScionBuild.TestFromCommandLine` (or the method in `build.test.method`): Mono backend, `SCION_SLOTS` and
`SCION_TRIALS` added for the build only, `scion-build.json` written with the slots and recipe names. Trials, warm
copies, injection and the multiverse mosaic all need this build.

## build final

Builds with `ScionBuild.FinalFromCommandLine` (or `build.final.method`): the project's backend (IL2CPP by default),
no test defines, grafts called directly. It fails with SCN121 if a test define is set anywhere in the build.

## Options

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--out <dir>` | from `scion.json` | Output folder. |
| `--dry-run` | off | Print the program and arguments; build nothing. |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/build -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"build test","ok":false,"channel":"batchmode","seconds":21.4,"log":".scion/logs/build-20261012-130000.log","build_id":null,"output":".scion/builds/test/Orchard.app","errors":[{"file":"Assets/Orchard/Grafts/CritShake.cs","line":18,"code":"SCN104","message":"The signature of CritShake.After does not match HitPresenter.Play.","hint":"Expected: public static void After(HitPresenter presenter, HitEvent e, ref Call<float> c)","did_you_mean":[]}],"errors_total":1,"next_step":"fix Assets/Orchard/Grafts/CritShake.cs:18, then: dotnet scion build test"}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `channel` | `batchmode` or `editor`. |
| `seconds` | Build time. |
| `build_id` | 12 hex, or null on failure. |
| `output` | The player path. |
| `errors[]` | `file`, `line`, `code` (`CS0103`, `SCN104`...), `message`, `hint`. |
| `errors_total` | All errors, when the list is cut. |
| `program`, `args` | With `--dry-run`. |

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Built. |
| 1 | Compile errors or a build guard (SCN120, SCN121). |
| 2 | Bad option. |
| 3 | No Unity, editor open without the pipeline, Unity crashed. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `editor_open` | 3 | The editor is open and `com.unity.pipeline` is missing. | Close the editor, or install the pipeline package. |
| `unity_not_found` | 3 | No Unity of the project's version. | Set `unity.editor` in `scion.local.json`. |
| `unity_failed` | 3 | Unity exited without a `BUILD_RESULT` line. | Read the log in `log`. |
| warning `unity_exit` | 0 | Unity exited non-zero after a successful build. | Usually harmless; read the log. |
| `SCN120`, `SCN121` | 1 | Build guards. | See [Build modes](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/build-modes/). |

## Examples

### Show the Unity command

```sh
dotnet scion build test --dry-run
```

### A final build for a store

```sh
dotnet scion build final --out /tmp/orchard-release
```

## See also

- [Build modes](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/build-modes/)
- [scion-build.json](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/scion-build-json/)
- [Editor API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/editor/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# trial list

`dotnet scion trial list` lists the recipes a run can play. By default it reads recipe names from the test build's
assemblies (without starting it) and adds the sources in `scion/recipes/` and the captured and found matches. With
`--ids` it starts the build with `-scion-list` and prints every expanded id (variants, modes, seeds) with players,
tags and flags.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion trial list [patterns] [--ids] [--tag <tags>] [--players <n>] [--build <path>]
```

## Description

| Source | `source` | Read how |
|---|---|---|
| The test build | `build` | Recipe classes found in `Managed/*.dll` without running the player. |
| `scion/recipes/*.cs` | `staging` | Recipe sources compiled with `--recipes`. |
| `scion/recipes/captured/*.match.json` | `captured` | One `CapturedMatch` id per file. |
| `scion/recipes/found/*.match.json` | `found` | Finds of the hunter. |

A recipe that cannot be built (no public parameterless constructor) is listed with `problem`.

## Options

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `patterns` | all | Names, ids or globs. |
| `--ids` | off | Expand ids by starting the player with `-scion-list`. |
| `--tag <tags>` | | Only recipes with one of the tags (needs `--ids`). |
| `--players <n>` | | Only recipes with that `Players` (needs `--ids`). |
| `--build <path>` | discovery | The test build. |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/trial-list -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"trial list","ok":true,"build":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/builds/test/Orchard.app","build_id":"4c49a1e0b2f3","count":7,"recipes":[{"name":"SlashHit","source":"build","players":1},{"name":"FireballArea","source":"build","players":1},{"name":"KnightFalls","source":"build","players":1},{"name":"CoopTurn","source":"build","players":4},{"name":"HudStates","source":"build","players":1},{"name":"UnitGallery","source":"build","players":1},{"name":"CapturedMatch","id":"CapturedMatch[match=knight-dies-to-crit]","source":"captured","players":1}],"next_step":"dotnet scion trial run"}
```

With `--ids`, each entry has `id`, `type`, `tags` and `explicit`, and the full list is in `recipes.json` of a
temporary folder.

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Listed. |
| 2 | A pattern matched nothing. |
| 3 | No build, or the player failed with `--ids`. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_match` | 2 | No recipe matches. | Use `did_you_mean`. |
| `build_not_found` | 3 | No test build. | `dotnet scion build test`. |
| warning `recipe_unbuildable` | 0 | A recipe has no public parameterless constructor (SCN201). | Add one. |
| warning `unreadable_dll` | 0 | A DLL of the build could not be read. | Rebuild. |

## Examples

### Every id of one recipe

```sh
dotnet scion trial list SlashHit --ids
```

### Only co-op recipes

```sh
dotnet scion trial list --ids --players 4
```

## See also

- [Write a recipe](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/recipes/)
- [Variants, modes and seeds](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/variants/)
- [recipes.json](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/recipes-json/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# trial run

`dotnet scion trial run` is the command you use most. It selects recipes, starts copies of the test build (or uses
warm copies), splits the work into shards and co-op groups, waits, compares every result with `scion/baselines/`,
writes `summary.json`, `summary.tsv` and `compare.json` in a new run folder, and prints a short envelope with counts,
failures, changes, determinism and the `next_step`. It also runs specs, variants, the mosaic and the motion pack.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion trial run [patterns] [-j N] [--rounds N] [selection options] [capture options]
                       [--grafts <dll>] [--recipes <dll>] [--warm] [--spec <Name>] [--variants a,b]
                       [--build <path>] [-- player-args]
```

## Description

1. Selects ids: patterns, `--tag`, `--players`, `--mode`, `--seeds`, `--changed`, `--failed`; `Explicit` recipes only
   when named.
2. Creates `<trials.out>/<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>/` and deletes runs beyond `keep_runs`.
3. Starts copies (cold) or sends `run` to warm copies (`--warm`). Co-op recipes run in groups of `Players` copies.
4. Waits, with `--timeout` per copy and the 120 s watchdog.
5. Compares each (id, round) with its baseline: hash, frames, images (cold runs only), rule digest.
6. Writes `summary.json` (the full envelope plus `copies[]`), `summary.tsv`, `compare.json`, `diff/` heatmaps.
7. Prints the envelope, with lists cut to stay short.

## Options

### Selection

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `patterns` | every non-`Explicit` recipe | Names, ids or globs, comma- or space-separated. |
| `--tag <tags>` | | Recipes with any of the tags. |
| `--players <n>` | all | Recipes with that `Players`. |
| `--mode <name>` | none | One mode of `[assembly: TrialModes]`. |
| `--seeds <a-b>` | none | Repeat each id per seed; ids get `#<seed>`. |
| `--changed` | | The ids that were `changed` or `stale` in the last run. |
| `--failed` | | The ids that failed in the last run. |

### Execution

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `-j N` | `trials.defaults.copies` | Parallel copies. |
| `--rounds N` | 1 | Rounds per id. |
| `--seed N` | 1 | Run seed (`RunSeed`). |
| `--timeout <s>` | 300 | Real seconds per copy. |
| `--check` | off | Frame-by-frame determinism report (`determinism.tsv`). |
| `--jitter <ms>` | 0 | Random real-time sleep per frame from the second round. |
| `--warm` | off | Use warm copies (`trial serve`); compares hash and frames only. |
| `--mosaic <K>` | off | K arenas per process. |
| `--build <path>` | discovery | The test build. |

### Capture

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--window` | headless | Render to a window. |
| `--size WxH` | `trials.defaults.size` | Capture size. |
| `--frames` | off | Every frame as PNG. |
| `--raw` | off | Keep raw frames. |
| `--sound` | muted | Audio on. |
| `--motion` | off | The motion pack. |
| `--learn-unstable <n>` | off | Run n extra times and learn the unstable mask (cap 2 %). |

### Code and values

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--grafts <dll>` | none | Inject a draft graft DLL at startup (`-scion-inject`); the run cannot be approved. |
| `--recipes <dll>` | none | Load recipes from a DLL; same `Name` replaces. Repeatable. |
| `--set <key>=<value>` | none | Override a tunable (`tunable:CritShake.Strength=0.8`). Repeatable. |
| `--preset <name\|blend>` | none | Apply a preset or blend to every id. |
| `--variants a,b,c` | none | One variant per preset or blend; ids get `[preset=<name>]`. |
| `--spec <Name>` | none | Run a spec; the envelope gets `spec`. |
| `-- args` | | Passed to every player; replaces the same flag in `player_args`. |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/trial-run -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"trial run","ok":false,"run":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/runs/20261011-143200","build_id":"4c49a1e0b2f3","copies":6,"wall_s":27.1,"runs":{"recipes":6,"rounds":2,"total":12,"ok":11,"failed":1,"changed":1,"within":0,"px_changed":0,"new":0,"stale":0},"failed":[{"id":"KnightFalls","round":1,"copy":3,"error":"timeout (30s): unit down animation","report":"q3/KnightFalls/r1/report.md"}],"changed":[{"id":"SlashHit","vs_approved":"changed","hash":"same","image":"q0/SlashHit/r1/window.png","diff":"diff/SlashHit/r1/window.diff.png"}],"determinism":{"hash_stable":true,"frame_jitter":[]},"next_step":"read q3/KnightFalls/r1/report.md; SlashHit changed only in images: see diff/SlashHit/r1/window.diff.png"}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `run` | The run folder; paths in the envelope are relative to it. |
| `copies` | Processes started (or warm copies used). |
| `runs` | Counts: ids, rounds, (id, round) pairs, ok, failed, and per verdict. |
| `failed[]` | `id`, `round`, `copy`, `error`, `report`. |
| `changed[]` | `id`, `vs_approved`, `hash` (`same`/`changed`), `image`, `diff`. |
| `determinism` | `hash_stable`, `frame_jitter`. |
| `mosaic` | K, when used. |
| `spec` | With `--spec`: `name`, `ok`, `variants[]`, `verdict`. |

Files: [summary.json, summary.tsv, compare.json](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/summary/).

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Every recipe passed. Verdicts such as `changed` do not fail a run. |
| 1 | A recipe or check failed, or a spec failed. |
| 2 | Bad option or a pattern matched nothing. |
| 3 | No build, a copy crashed or timed out, environment errors. |

Copies are combined with precedence 2 > 3 > 1 > 0.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_match` | 2 | No id matches. | `did_you_mean`; `trial list --ids`. |
| `build_not_found` | 3 | No test build. | `dotnet scion build test`. |
| `build_wrong_mode` | 3 | The build lacks `SCION_TRIALS`. | `dotnet scion build test`. |
| `player_crashed` | 3 | A copy exited without outputs. | Read `q<i>/player.log`. |
| `copy_timeout` | 3 | A copy passed `--timeout` or was interrupted. | Raise `--timeout`, or find the stuck `WaitUntil`. |
| `no_free_port` | 3 | No free port for a group. | Close other servers. |
| `no_copies` | 3 | `--warm` with no warm copies. | `dotnet scion trial serve -j 2`. |
| `mosaic_unsupported` | 3 | `--mosaic` and no `IMosaicAdapter`. | Implement it or drop `--mosaic`. |
| warning `build_stale` | 0 | Sources changed after the build. | Rebuild before trusting the result. |
| warning `px_unstable` | 0 | Pixels vary between rounds. | See [Verify determinism](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/verify/). |
| warning `shard_ignored` | 0 | `-scion-shard` passed after `--`. | Let the CLI shard. |

## Examples

### The everyday run

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --rounds 2
```

### Combat only, with the motion pack, at 720p

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --tag combat --motion --size 1280x720
```

### A draft graft against every recipe

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --grafts .scion/grafts/ScionGrafts_51c2.dll
```

## See also

- [How trials work](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/overview/)
- [Parallel copies](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/parallel/)
- [summary.json, summary.tsv, compare.json](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/summary/)
- [Reading results](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/reading-results/)
- [Player command line](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/player-flags/)
