# Injection API

`Injection` swaps the slots of a running test build (`SCION_SLOTS`). The CLI and the control server call it; use it
directly only in your own tools. Swaps requested during a recipe wait for the next boundary.

## Injection

**Namespace:** `Scion` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Injection` · **Define:** `SCION_SLOTS`

```csharp
public static class Injection
{
    public static int Version { get; }
    public static event Action<InjectReport> Applied;
    public static InjectReport Inject(string dllPath, bool isolate = false);
    public static void Restore();
    public static bool Disable(string slotId);
}
```

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Version` | Loads applied so far; the `grafts` column of `results.tsv`. |
| `Applied` | Raised on the main thread after each applied load. |
| `Inject` | Loads the DLL and binds its grafts; merges by graft identity, or replaces with `isolate`. Refuses another `build_id` (SCN130) or ABI (SCN131). |
| `Restore` | Every slot back to the promoted grafts. |
| `Disable` | Empties one slot; returns false when the slot does not exist. |

Main thread only. Mono never unloads assemblies: each load stays in memory.

```csharp
#if SCION_SLOTS
var r = Injection.Inject(path);
Debug.Log(r.ToJson());
#endif
```

## InjectReport

**Namespace:** `Scion` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Injection` · **Define:** `SCION_SLOTS`

```csharp
public readonly struct InjectReport
{
    public int Version { get; }
    public bool Ok { get; }
    public bool Pending { get; }
    public string[] Bound { get; }
    public string[] Errors { get; }
    public bool Recycle { get; }
    public string ToJson();
}
```

`Errors` lines are `"SCNxxx: message"`. `Recycle` is true after 50 loads. JSON shape:
[InjectReport JSON](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/inject-report/).

## See also

- [Live injection](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/injection/)
- [InjectReport JSON](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/inject-report/)
- [Control protocol](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/control-protocol/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Determinism API

These types are the targets of the weaver's redirects and the session's per-recipe resets in test builds. They live
in `Scion.Runtime` under `SCION_TRIALS` (`NetClock` in `Scion.Trials`). Inactive, they return real values.

## Clock

**Namespace:** `Scion` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Runtime` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
public static class Clock
{
    public const double RecipeStart = 1000.0;
    public static readonly DateTime DefaultEpoch;      // 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z
    public static bool Active { get; }
    public static DateTime Epoch { get; set; }
    public static void Begin(double start = RecipeStart);
    public static void End();
    public static void Advance(float delta);
    public static float Time { get; }
    public static double TimeAsDouble { get; }
    public static float TimeSinceLevelLoad { get; }
    public static double TimeSinceLevelLoadAsDouble { get; }
    public static float UnscaledTime { get; }
    public static double UnscaledTimeAsDouble { get; }
    public static float UnscaledDeltaTime { get; }
    public static float RealtimeSinceStartup { get; }
    public static double RealtimeSinceStartupAsDouble { get; }
    public static DateTime Now { get; }
    public static DateTime UtcNow { get; }
    public static DateTime Today { get; }
}
```

`Begin` and `End` are called by the session. `Advance` is for tests outside Unity.

## VirtualScreen

**Namespace:** `Scion` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Runtime` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
public static class VirtualScreen
{
    public static void Set(int width, int height);
    public static void Clear();
    public static int Width { get; }
    public static int Height { get; }
}
```

## VirtualWaitForSecondsRealtime

**Namespace:** `Scion` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Runtime` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
public sealed class VirtualWaitForSecondsRealtime : UnityEngine.WaitForSecondsRealtime
{
    public VirtualWaitForSecondsRealtime(float time);
}
```

Waits on `Clock.RealtimeSinceStartupAsDouble`.

## SeededRandom

**Namespace:** `Scion` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Runtime` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
public sealed class SeededRandom : System.Random
{
    public SeededRandom();
    public static void Reset(int seed);
}
```

The seed is a hash of the recipe seed and the order of creation since the last `Reset`.

## DeterminismControl

**Namespace:** `Scion` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Runtime` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
[Flags]
public enum DeterminismControl { None = 0, Particles = 1, Animators = 2, UiToolkit = 4, Physics = 8, All = ~0 }
```

## Determinism

**Namespace:** `Scion` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Runtime` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
public static class Determinism
{
    public static void Begin(int seed, DeterminismControl control);
    public static void End();
    public static int SeedFor(string path, int creationOrder);
    public static IReadOnlyList<string> Census();
}
```

`Begin` and `End` are called by the session. `SeedFor` is FNV of the seed, the path and the order. `Census` lists
what still depends on real time or automatic seeds.

## NetClock

**Namespace:** `Scion.Trials` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Trials` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
public static class NetClock
{
    public static double Time { get; }
    public static float DeltaTime { get; }
}
```

Continuous virtual time for libraries that keep their own clock; it never jumps back at `Clock.Begin`.

## See also

- [Deterministic runs](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/overview/)
- [Clock, screen and random](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/clock-and-screen/)
- [Particles, animators, UI and physics](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/control/)
- [Netcode clock](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/netclock/)

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Recipes API

A recipe is a `TrialRecipe` subclass created through its public parameterless constructor. Variants come from
`[Vary]` fields or `Variants()`; modes from `[assembly: TrialModes]`. All types are in `Scion.Trials` under
`SCION_TRIALS`.

## TrialRecipe

**Namespace:** `Scion.Trials` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Trials` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
public abstract class TrialRecipe
{
    public virtual string Name { get; }                       // class name
    public string Id { get; }
    public string Variant { get; }
    public string Mode { get; }
    public IReadOnlyList<string> Tags { get; protected set; }
    public string Description { get; protected set; }
    public int Seed { get; protected set; } = 1;
    public int Fps { get; protected set; } = 30;
    public float TailSeconds { get; protected set; } = 0.5f;
    public float TimeoutSeconds { get; protected set; } = 30f;
    public int Players { get; protected set; } = 1;
    public bool Explicit { get; protected set; }
    public DeterminismControl Control { get; protected set; } = DeterminismControl.All;
    public ImageTolerance Tolerance { get; protected set; } = ImageTolerance.Default;
    protected virtual void Checks(TrialChecks c) { }
    protected virtual void Setup() { }
    protected virtual IEnumerable<TrialArgs> Variants() => null;
    protected void Mask(string artifact, Rect normalized, string why);
}
```

| Member | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `Id`, `Variant`, `Mode` | Set by the session when it expands the recipe. | |
| `Players` | 1 to 4. | 1 |
| `Explicit` | Runs only when named. | false |
| `Tolerance` | `null` compares no images. | `ImageTolerance.Default` |
| `Mask` | `artifact` is a file name or `*`; `normalized` has the origin at the bottom left. | |

## VaryAttribute

**Namespace:** `Scion.Trials` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Trials` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Field | AttributeTargets.Property)]
public sealed class VaryAttribute : Attribute
{
    public VaryAttribute(params object[] values);
}
```

Every combination of `[Vary]` values is a variant, in declaration order.

## TrialArgs

**Namespace:** `Scion.Trials` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Trials` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
public sealed class TrialArgs : IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<string, object>>
{
    public void Add(string name, object value);
}
```

Keys are recipe members or `tunable:<Type>.<Field>`.

## TrialModesAttribute

**Namespace:** `Scion.Trials` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Trials` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Assembly)]
public sealed class TrialModesAttribute : Attribute
{
    public TrialModesAttribute(params string[] modes);   // "360p=640x360", "deuter"
}
```

## ITrialModeAware

**Namespace:** `Scion.Trials` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Trials` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
public interface ITrialModeAware
{
    void ApplyMode(string mode);
}
```

Adapters implement it for modes that are not resolutions.

## CapturedMatch

**Namespace:** `Scion.Trials` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Trials` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
public sealed class CapturedMatch : TrialRecipe
{
    public string Match { get; }          // the variant key "match"
    public MatchData Data { get; }        // the parsed .match.json
}
```

One variant per file in `scion/recipes/captured/` and `found/`. Played by `IMatchCapture.Replay`.

# Adapters API

Adapters are the game's port into Trials. `TrialAdapter<TRecipe>` handles recipes of a type; `StaticTrial<TItem>`
needs no game adapter; `IMatchCapture` turns matches into recipes; `IMosaicAdapter` runs several arenas. All in
`Scion.Trials` under `SCION_TRIALS`.

## ITrialAdapter

**Namespace:** `Scion.Trials` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Trials` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
public interface ITrialAdapter
{
    IEnumerator Prepare(TrialSession session);
    bool Accepts(TrialRecipe recipe);
    IEnumerator Run(TrialRecipe recipe, TrialSession session);
    IEnumerator Teardown(TrialRecipe recipe, TrialSession session);
    string StateHash { get; }
}
```

A plain implementation handles `TrialRecipe`, the least specific type. `Accepts` must not throw.

## TrialAdapter\<TRecipe\>

**Namespace:** `Scion.Trials` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Trials` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
public abstract class TrialAdapter<TRecipe> : MonoBehaviour, ITrialAdapter where TRecipe : TrialRecipe
{
    public virtual IEnumerator Prepare(TrialSession s);
    protected abstract IEnumerator Run(TRecipe r, TrialSession s);
    protected virtual IEnumerator Teardown(TRecipe r, TrialSession s);
    public virtual string StateHash => null;
}
```

`Accepts` is `r is TRecipe`. The most derived `TRecipe` among accepting adapters wins (SCN203 on a tie).

## TrialAdapterAttribute

**Namespace:** `Scion.Trials` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Trials` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Assembly, AllowMultiple = true)]
public sealed class TrialAdapterAttribute : Attribute
{
    public TrialAdapterAttribute(Type adapter);
    public Type Adapter { get; }
}
```

## StaticTrial

**Namespace:** `Scion.Trials` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Trials` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
public abstract class StaticTrial : TrialRecipe
{
    public int SettleFrames { get; protected set; } = 3;
    public abstract IEnumerator Play(TrialSession s);
}
```

The non-generic base, so adapters can be `TrialAdapter<StaticTrial>`. The package registers `StaticTrialAdapter`,
which only calls `Play`.

## StaticTrial\<TItem\>

**Namespace:** `Scion.Trials` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Trials` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
public abstract class StaticTrial<TItem> : StaticTrial
{
    protected abstract IEnumerable<TItem> Enumerate();
    protected virtual string ItemName(TItem item);
    protected abstract IEnumerator Show(TItem item, TrialSession s);
    protected virtual IEnumerator Clear(TItem item, TrialSession s);
    protected virtual IEnumerable<TrialView> Views(TItem item);
    protected virtual void Measure(TItem item, TrialSession s);
}
```

## TrialView

**Namespace:** `Scion.Trials` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Trials` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
public readonly struct TrialView
{
    public static TrialView Screen { get; }
    public static TrialView Ui { get; }
    public static TrialView Top(Bounds bounds, float pxPerUnit, bool grid = false);
    public string Name { get; }
}
```

## IMatchCapture

**Namespace:** `Scion.Trials` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Trials` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
public interface IMatchCapture
{
    bool CanCapture { get; }
    int Seed { get; }
    int Players { get; }
    string SaveSetup();
    IEnumerable<(int Turn, int Player, string Data)> Commands();
```

Implemented by an adapter that can run arenas side by side; `TrialSession.Arena` tells `Run` which one it plays.

# Session API

`TrialSession` is the MonoBehaviour that runs the queue; `TrialRole` names a process's role in a co-op group.
Behavior and examples are on [TrialSession](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/session/); this page lists the signatures.

## TrialSession

**Namespace:** `Scion.Trials` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Trials` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
public sealed partial class TrialSession : MonoBehaviour
{
    public static TrialSession Current { get; }
    public static event Action Boundary;

    public string OutputRoot { get; }
    public TrialRecipe Recipe { get; }
    public string RecipeDir { get; }
    public int Round { get; }
    public bool InRecipe { get; }
    public int RunSeed { get; }
    public IReadOnlyList<TrialRecipe> Recipes { get; }
    public TrialRole Role { get; }
    public int Arena { get; }
    public static TrialSession ForArena(int arena);

    public void BeginCut();
    public void EndCut();
    public void Mark(string label);
    public void MarkImpact();
    public void Still(string name);
    public void MaskRect(Rect screenPixels, string why);

    public void Fail(string reason);
    public void Check(bool ok, string what);
    public void Note(string line);

    public void Probe(string key, double value);
    public void Sensor(string name, Func<long> read);
    public void Event(string name, params (string Key, object Value)[] fields);

    public IEnumerator WaitUntil(Func<bool> cond, string what);
    public IEnumerator WaitSeconds(float gameSeconds);
    public IEnumerator RunQueue(string only, int rounds, string outDir, Action<int> done = null);
}
```

Main thread only; calls from other threads are ignored and logged as errors. `Arena` is 0 outside the mosaic.

## TrialRole

**Namespace:** `Scion.Trials` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Trials` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
public readonly struct TrialRole : IEquatable<TrialRole>
{
    public static TrialRole Host { get; }
    public static TrialRole Client(int index);   // 1 to 3
    public bool IsHost { get; }
    public int Index { get; }                    // 0 = host
    public override string ToString();           // "host" or "client:1"
    public static bool TryParse(string text, out TrialRole role);
}
```

# Checks API

Recipes declare checks with `TrialChecks`; games add checks for every recipe with `ITrialCheck`. Results are
`CheckResult` values. All in `Scion.Trials` under `SCION_TRIALS`.

## TrialChecks

**Namespace:** `Scion.Trials` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Trials` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
public sealed class TrialChecks
{
    public TrialChecks NoErrors(params string[] allowRegex);
    public TrialChecks Deterministic(bool frames = false, bool pixels = true);
    public TrialChecks Marked(string label, int atLeast = 1);
    public TrialChecks Order(params string[] labels);
    public TrialChecks Frames(int min, int max);
    public TrialChecks ProbeIs(string key, Func<double, bool> ok, string why);
    public TrialChecks Gate(string id, params (string Name, object Value)[] options);
    public TrialChecks Skip(string checkId, string why);
}
```

Check ids: `log`, `assert`, `blank`, `magenta`, `px`, `determinism`, `marked:<label>`, `order`, `frames`,
`probe:<key>`, `gate:<id>`, plus custom ids. A wrong argument throws `ArgumentException` and fails the recipe.

## ITrialCheck

**Namespace:** `Scion.Trials` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Trials` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
public interface ITrialCheck
{
    string Id { get; }
    void Begin(TrialRecipe recipe, TrialSession session);
    void OnFrame(in FrameView frame);
    void OnLog(string message, string stack, LogType type);
    CheckResult End();
}
```

One instance per process; main thread; `OnFrame` must not allocate.

## TrialCheckAttribute

**Namespace:** `Scion.Trials` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Trials` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Assembly, AllowMultiple = true)]
public sealed class TrialCheckAttribute : Attribute
{
    public TrialCheckAttribute(Type check);
    public Type Check { get; }
}
```

## FrameView

**Namespace:** `Scion.Trials` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Trials` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
public readonly ref struct FrameView
{
    public int Index { get; }
    public int Width { get; }
    public int Height { get; }
    public ReadOnlySpan<byte> Pixels { get; }   // bottom row first, 4 bytes per pixel
    public string Layout { get; }               // RGBA8, ARGB8 or BGRA8
    public ulong Px { get; }
    public double GameMs { get; }
}
```

## CheckStatus

**Namespace:** `Scion.Trials` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Trials` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
public enum CheckStatus { Pass, Warn, Fail, Skipped }
```

## CheckResult

**Namespace:** `Scion.Trials` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Trials` · **Define:** `SCION_TRIALS`

```csharp
public readonly struct CheckResult
{
    public CheckStatus Status { get; }
    public string Reason { get; }
    public int Frame { get; }            // -1 = no frame
    public RectInt? Region { get; }      // pixels, origin bottom left
    public static CheckResult Pass();
    public static CheckResult Warn(string reason, int frame = -1, RectInt? region = null);
    public static CheckResult Fail(string reason, int frame = -1, RectInt? region = null);
}
```

`default(CheckResult)` fails the check. `Warn` and `Fail` need a non-blank reason.

# Fx API

`Fx` is the effects facade grafts call; `IFxSink` is what the game implements once. Both exist in every build.

## Fx

**Namespace:** `Scion` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Runtime` · **Define:** none

```csharp
public static class Fx
{
    public static IFxSink Sink { get; set; }
    public static string Source { get; set; }
    public static void Sound(string id, Vector3? at = null, float volume = 1f);
    public static void Shake(float amount);
    public static void Text(string text, Vector3 at, Color color, float seconds = 1.1f, int size = 12, string icon = null);
    public static void Flash(Component target, Color color, float seconds);
    public static void HitStop(float seconds);
    public static void Vfx(string id, Vector3 at, float scale = 1f);
    public static void Mark(string label);
}
```

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Sink` | The game's sink; null makes every verb a no-op. Set once at boot. |
| `Source` | The graft currently running, written by the slot dispatcher; `by` in telemetry. |

## IFxSink

**Namespace:** `Scion` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Runtime` · **Define:** none

```csharp
public interface IFxSink
{
    void Sound(string id, Vector3? at, float volume);
    void Shake(float amount);
    void Text(string text, Vector3 at, Color color, float seconds, int size, string icon);
    void Flash(Component target, Color color, float seconds);
    void HitStop(float seconds);
    void Vfx(string id, Vector3 at, float scale);
    void Mark(string label);
}
```

In test builds, Trials wraps the sink to record each call in `telemetry.jsonl`, then forwards it.

# Testing API

`Scion.Testing` is a NuGet package for `dotnet test` projects. It brings `Scion.Runtime` compiled for .NET (so
`Call<T>`, `Fx` and the attributes work outside Unity), Unity value types used by grafts (`Vector3`, `Color`), the
Scion analyzers, and a recorder for `Fx` calls.

## FxRecorder

**Namespace:** `Scion.Testing` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Testing` · **Define:** none

```csharp
public sealed class FxRecorder : IFxSink
{
    public IReadOnlyList<FxCall> Calls { get; }
    public void Clear();
}
```

Set `Fx.Sink = new FxRecorder()` before calling a graft; every verb is appended to `Calls` with its arguments and
`Fx.Source`.

## FxCall

**Namespace:** `Scion.Testing` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Testing` · **Define:** none

```csharp
public readonly struct FxCall
{
    public string Verb { get; }       // "Sound", "Shake", ...
    public object[] Args { get; }
    public string Source { get; }
}
```

## The package

```sh
dotnet add Tests/Orchard.Grafts.Tests package Scion.Testing --version 1.0.0
```

Projects that reference `Scion.Testing` are test assemblies: SCN110 does not apply to them.

## See also

- [Test grafts without Unity](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/testing/)
- [Fx API](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/api/fx/)

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Compare API

`ImageTolerance` (in `Scion.Runtime`) states how much two captures may differ. `Scion.Compare` (in the package and on
NuGet, no Unity needed) loads PNG and raw frames, builds masks, compares images with OKLab and HyAB and writes
heatmaps. JSON and PNG coordinates have the origin at the top left.

## ImageTolerance

**Namespace:** `Scion` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Runtime` · **Define:** none

```csharp
public sealed class ImageTolerance
{
    public ImageTolerance(float pixel, float maxRatio, int maxPixels);
    public static readonly ImageTolerance Default;   // (0.1, 0.001, -1)
    public static readonly ImageTolerance Exact;     // (0, 0, 0)
    public float Pixel { get; }
    public float MaxRatio { get; }
    public int MaxPixels { get; }                    // -1 = no limit
}
```

## Image

**Namespace:** `Scion.Compare` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Compare` · **Define:** none

```csharp
public sealed class Image
{
    public int Width { get; }
    public int Height { get; }
    public byte[] Rgba { get; }                      // RGBA8, top row first
    public static Image Load(string path);           // .png, or .raw with raw.json beside it
    public static Image FromRaw(byte[] raw, int width, int height, string layout, bool bottomUp);
    public void SavePng(string path);
}
```

## NormRect

**Namespace:** `Scion.Compare` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Compare` · **Define:** none

```csharp
public readonly struct NormRect
{
    public NormRect(float x, float y, float w, float h);   // 0 to 1, origin top left
}
```

## PixelRect

**Namespace:** `Scion.Compare` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Compare` · **Define:** none

```csharp
public readonly struct PixelRect
{
    public int X { get; }
    public int Y { get; }
    public int Width { get; }
    public int Height { get; }
}
```

## Mask

**Namespace:** `Scion.Compare` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Compare` · **Define:** none

```csharp
public sealed class Mask
{
    public static Mask Empty(int width, int height);
    public static Mask FromRects(int width, int height, IEnumerable<NormRect> rects);
    public static bool TryLearn(IReadOnlyList<Image> samples, ImageTolerance t, float cap, out Mask mask, out float unstable);
    public float Coverage { get; }
    public Mask Union(Mask other);
    public static Mask Load(string png);
    public void Save(string png);
}
```

`TryLearn` returns false (and no mask) when the unstable area exceeds `cap`; it never truncates.

## DiffStatus

**Namespace:** `Scion.Compare` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Compare` · **Define:** none

```csharp
public enum DiffStatus { Same, Within, Changed }
```

`new` and `stale` are CLI verdicts, not image statuses.

## DiffResult

**Namespace:** `Scion.Compare` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Compare` · **Define:** none

```csharp

    public int Pixels { get; }
    public PixelRect Bounds { get; }
}
```

**Namespace:** `Scion.Compare` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Compare` · **Define:** none

```csharp
{

    public static void WriteHeatmap(Image a, Image b, Mask mask, ImageTolerance t, string pngPath);
}
```

# Editor API

`ScionBuild` builds players the way the CLI does: test players on Mono with the test defines, final players without
them. It works from your editor scripts, from batchmode and through the open editor.

## ScionBuild

**Namespace:** `Scion.Editor` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Editor` · **Define:** editor only

```csharp
public static class ScionBuild
{
    public static readonly string[] TestDefines = { "SCION_SLOTS", "SCION_TRIALS" };
    public static BuildReport BuildTestPlayer(BuildPlayerOptions o);
    public static BuildReport BuildFinalPlayer(BuildPlayerOptions o);
    public static void TestFromCommandLine();
    public static void FinalFromCommandLine();
    public static string FromEditor(string mode, string outDir);
}
```

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `BuildTestPlayer` | Forces Mono, adds `TestDefines` for the build, restores backend and defines in a `finally`, writes `scion-build.json`. |
| `BuildFinalPlayer` | Builds with the project's backend; fails with SCN121 when a test define is set. |
| `TestFromCommandLine`, `FinalFromCommandLine` | Batchmode: `-scion-build-out <dir> [-scion-build-target osx\|win\|linux]`; exits 0 or 1 and prints `BUILD_RESULT`. |
| `FromEditor` | `mode` is `test` or `final`; returns the JSON of `build`. Used through the open editor. |

## ScionBuildEntry

**Namespace:** global · **Assembly:** written by the CLI into `Temp/Scion/` · **Define:** editor only

```csharp
public static class ScionBuildEntry
{
    public static string Run(string mode, string outDir) => Scion.Editor.ScionBuild.FromEditor(mode, outDir);
}
```

The CLI writes this stub to `Temp/Scion/ScionBuildEntry.cs` and runs it in the open editor through the
`com.unity.pipeline` command line. You never write it.

## See also

- [Build modes](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/build-modes/)
- [build test, build final](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/build/)
- [scion-build.json](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/files/scion-build-json/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Specs API

`Scion.Specs` is a NuGet package for specs projects (`specs.project` in `scion.json`). A spec is a `TrialSpec` that
defines its parts on a `SpecBuilder`; `trial run --spec` runs it. It references `Scion.Core` and runs balance and
metamorphic parts on the simulator in plain .NET.

## TrialSpec

**Namespace:** `Scion.Specs` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Specs` · **Define:** none

```csharp
public abstract class TrialSpec
{
    public abstract string Name { get; }
    public abstract string Target { get; }       // one sentence: what must be true
    public abstract void Define(SpecBuilder s);
}
```

## SpecBuilder

**Namespace:** `Scion.Specs` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Specs` · **Define:** none

```csharp
public sealed class SpecBuilder
{
    public BalancePart Balance(string name, int players, int matches);
    public VisualPart Visual(string recipe);
    public JudgePart Judge(string recipe, string head);
    public void Metamorphic(Metamorphic property, int matches, int players = 1);
    public void Metamorphic(string name, Func<ISimulation, int, bool> property, int matches);
    public CurvePart Curve(string name, int levels, int players, int matches);
}

public sealed class BalancePart { public BalancePart Expect(string metric, double? min = null, double? max = null); }
public sealed class VisualPart
{
    public VisualPart Expect(string metric, double? min = null, double? max = null);
    public VisualPart Gate(string id, params (string Name, object Value)[] options);
}
public sealed class JudgePart { public JudgePart Expect(string answer, double? min = null, double? max = null); }
public sealed class CurvePart
{
    public CurvePart ExpectAt(int level, string metric, double? min = null, double? max = null);
    public CurvePart Monotonic(string metric, bool decreasing);
    public CurvePart MaxStep(string metric, double step);
}
```

| Part | Metrics |
|---|---|
| `Balance`, `Curve` | `ISimulation.Metrics`: `win_rate`, `turns_mean` and the game's own. |
| `Visual` | Motion metrics (`hit_stop_ms`, `shake_peak_px`, `flash_ms`...) and the recipe's probes. |
| `Judge` | `score`, `noul`, or a choice's probability. |

## Gates

**Namespace:** `Scion.Specs` (also `Scion.Trials`) · **Assembly:** `Scion.Specs` · **Define:** none

```csharp
public static class Gates
{
    public const string TextOverflow = "text_overflow";
    public const string UiGrid = "ui_grid";
    public const string TextContrast = "text_contrast";
    public const string Photosensitivity = "photosensitivity";
    public const string ImageRegression = "image_regression";
    public const string TelemetryVsPixel = "telemetry_vs_pixel";
    public const string NothingChanged = "nothing_changed";
    public const string Palette = "palette";
}
```

## Metamorphic

**Namespace:** `Scion.Specs` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Specs` · **Define:** none

```csharp
public enum Metamorphic { Mirror, Permute, VisualToggle, SaveLoad }
```

- [Metamorphic tests](/scion/41664431a8f5/explore/metamorphic/)

# Core API

`Scion.Core` is a small assembly without engine references, for the game's rules core. It gives rules an explicit
extension point (`RuleModifier<T>`), declares tunables and probes, and lets Scion run the rules outside Unity
(`ISimulation`) for balance specs, the multiverse, metamorphic tests and the hunter. It ships in the package and on
NuGet with the same version.

## RuleModifier\<T\>

**Namespace:** `Scion.Core` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Core` · **Define:** none

```csharp
public abstract class RuleModifier<T> where T : struct
{
    public abstract Stage Stage { get; }
    public virtual int Priority => 0;
    public abstract void Apply(ref T context);
}

public sealed class ModifierSet<T> where T : struct
{
    public void Add(RuleModifier<T> modifier);
    public bool Remove(RuleModifier<T> modifier);
    public void Apply(ref T context);           // by Stage, then Priority, then type full name
    public IReadOnlyList<RuleModifier<T>> All { get; }
}
```

## Stage

**Namespace:** `Scion.Core` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Core` · **Define:** none

```csharp
public enum Stage { Base = 1, Add = 2, Mul = 3, Clamp = 4, Final = 5 }
```

## TunableAttribute

**Namespace:** `Scion.Core` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Core` · **Define:** none

```csharp
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Field)]
public sealed class TunableAttribute : Attribute
{
    public TunableAttribute();                        // bool tunables
    public TunableAttribute(double min, double max);
    public double Min { get; }
    public double Max { get; }
    public string Doc { get; set; }
}
```

On `static` fields of type `int`, `float`, `double` or `bool`. Numeric tunables need a range (SCN005).

## ProbeAttribute

**Namespace:** `Scion.Core` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Core` · **Define:** none

```csharp
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Field | AttributeTargets.Property)]
public sealed class ProbeAttribute : Attribute
{
    public ProbeAttribute(string key);
    public string Key { get; }
}
```

Values recorded at the end of each recipe as probes.

## Tunables

**Namespace:** `Scion.Core` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Core` · **Define:** none

```csharp
public static class Tunables
{
    public static bool Set(string key, object value);       // clamps to the range; false if unknown
    public static object Get(string key);
    public static string LobbyHash { get; }                 // hash of rule-layer tunable values
}
```

## ISimulation

**Namespace:** `Scion.Core` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Core` · **Define:** none

```csharp
public interface ISimulation
{
    void Reset(int seed, string setup);
    IReadOnlyList<string> LegalCommands(int player);
    void Apply(int player, string command);
    bool Done { get; }
    string Hash();
    IReadOnlyDictionary<string, double> Metrics();
    IEnumerable<string> Features();
}
```

Commands are serialized strings (the same `Data` as captured matches).

## SimulationAttribute

**Namespace:** `Scion.Core` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Core` · **Define:** none

```csharp
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Assembly)]
public sealed class SimulationAttribute : Attribute

    public SimulationAttribute(Type simulation);

```

Registering it raises the project to adoption level 3.

## Capabilities

**Namespace:** `Scion.Core` · **Assembly:** `Scion.Core` · **Define:** none

```csharp
public interface ISaveable { byte[] Save(); void Load(byte[] state); }
```

Implemented by the simulation for forking (`ISaveable`), divergence reports (`IInspectable`) and metamorphic

# Run Scion in CI

This recipe runs Scion in GitHub Actions with three jobs. A fast `dotnet` job needs no Unity license: analyzers,
strict graft checks, `gen --check`, unit tests and specs on the simulator. A Unity job builds the test player with
GameCI, runs the trials and uploads the run folder. A nightly job runs many rounds with `--check --jitter` to catch
rare non-determinism. Pull requests that change baselines must come with the approved files.

## When to use

- Every repository with Scion: the dotnet job costs under two minutes and catches most mistakes.
- Add the Unity job when you have a license for CI (GameCI documents the activation).

## Before you begin

- `scion.json`, the tool manifest and baselines committed (PNGs in Git LFS).
- A Unity license secret for the Unity job (`UNITY_LICENSE`, `UNITY_EMAIL`, `UNITY_PASSWORD`) set in the repository
  settings, never in files.

## Steps

### 1. The dotnet job

`.github/workflows/scion.yml`:

```yaml
name: scion
on: [pull_request, push]
jobs:
  dotnet:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with: { lfs: true }
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with: { dotnet-version: '10.0.x' }
      - run: dotnet tool restore
      - run: dotnet test Tests/Orchard.Core.Tests
      - run: dotnet test Tests/Orchard.Grafts.Tests
      - run: dotnet scion graft check --strict
      - run: dotnet scion gen --check
      - run: dotnet scion trial run --spec RulesHold
```

### 2. The Unity job

```yaml
  unity:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: dotnet
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with: { lfs: true }
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with: { dotnet-version: '10.0.x' }
      - run: dotnet tool restore
      - uses: game-ci/unity-builder@v4
        env:
          UNITY_LICENSE: ${{ secrets.UNITY_LICENSE }}
          UNITY_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.UNITY_EMAIL }}
          UNITY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.UNITY_PASSWORD }}
        with:
          targetPlatform: StandaloneLinux64
          buildMethod: Scion.Editor.ScionBuild.TestFromCommandLine
          customParameters: -scion-build-out .scion/builds/test
      - run: dotnet scion trial run --rounds 2 -j 2 --build .scion/builds/test
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with: { name: scion-run, path: .scion/runs }
```

### 3. Fail on unapproved changes

A run exits 0 when recipes pass, even with `changed` verdicts. To require that visual changes come with approved
baselines, fail the job when any id is `changed` or `new`:

```yaml
      - run: |
          dotnet scion trial show --changed --format json > changed.json
          test "$(jq .count changed.json)" = "0"
```

Linux baselines have their own platform folder; approve them once from a Linux machine or a CI artifact.

### 4. The nightly batch

```yaml
on:
  schedule: [{ cron: '0 3 * * *' }]
# same Unity job, with:
      - run: dotnet scion trial run --rounds 10 --check --jitter 20 -j 4 --build .scion/builds/test
```

## Reference

| Job | Needs Unity | Catches |
|---|---|---|
| dotnet | no | Analyzer errors, graft signatures, stale manifest, rule regressions, broken specs |
| Unity | yes | Failing recipes, determinism, visual changes |
| Nightly | yes | Rare non-determinism, timing-dependent bugs |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `unity_failed` | 3 | The license step failed. | Check the GameCI activation secrets. |
| `baseline_unreadable` | warning | LFS files not checked out. | `lfs: true` in checkout. |
| `capture_broken` | 3 | No GPU and no offscreen capture. | Keep the default headless mode; do not pass `--window`. |

## Examples

### Only the dotnet job on documentation changes

```yaml
on:
  pull_request:
    paths-ignore: ['**/*.md']
```

### Upload only failures

```yaml
      - run: dotnet scion trial show --failed --format json > failed.json
```

## See also

- [Verify determinism](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/verify/)
- [Baselines and approval](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/baselines/)
- [trial run](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/trial-run/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Capture every HUD state

The HUD has many states nobody looks at together: the turn banner, low health, four players, a status effect, a long
unit name. This recipe captures all of them with one `StaticTrial<HudState>`, at 360p and 720p, checks them with
gates (text overflow, contrast, grid), writes a labeled sheet, and lets the judge rank them for review.

## When to use

- Any change to HUD layout, fonts, colors or localization.
- As the input of a [UI review with the judge](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/ui-review/).

## Before you begin

- The HUD can be put in any state from data, without a battle (Orchard's `Hud.Apply(HudState)`).
- Modes declared: `[assembly: TrialModes("360p=640x360", "720p=1280x720")]`.

## Steps

### 1. Describe the states

```csharp
public readonly struct HudState
{
    public readonly string Name; public readonly int Players; public readonly int Hp; public readonly string Status;
    public HudState(string name, int players, int hp, string status) { Name = name; Players = players; Hp = hp; Status = status; }
}
```

### 2. Write the static trial

```csharp
public sealed class HudStates : StaticTrial<HudState>
{
    public HudStates()
    {
        Description = "Every HUD state at the current mode.";
        Tags = new[] { "ui" };
        Tolerance = ImageTolerance.Exact;
    }

    protected override IEnumerable<HudState> Enumerate()
    {
        yield return new HudState("idle", 1, 20, null);
        yield return new HudState("low-hp", 1, 3, null);
        yield return new HudState("four-players", 4, 20, null);
        yield return new HudState("burning", 1, 12, "burn");
        yield return new HudState("long-name", 1, 20, null);
        // ... 15 more
    }

    protected override string ItemName(HudState s) => s.Name;

    protected override IEnumerator Show(HudState s, TrialSession session)
    {
        Hud.Current.Apply(s);
        yield return null;
    }

    protected override IEnumerable<TrialView> Views(HudState s) { yield return TrialView.Ui; }

    protected override void Checks(TrialChecks c) =>
        c.Gate(Gates.TextOverflow).Gate(Gates.TextContrast).Gate(Gates.UiGrid, ("grid_px", 4));
}
```

### 3. Run both modes

```sh
dotnet scion trial run HudStates --mode 360p
dotnet scion trial run HudStates --mode 720p
dotnet scion trial show "HudStates@*" --image sheet
```

### 4. Rank for review

```sh
dotnet scion judge run <run> --heads readability,has_glitch
```

## Reference

| Output | Content |
|---|---|
| `<state>.ui.png` | One still per state, UI layer only. |
| `sheet.png` | All states, labeled, longer side at most 2000 px. |
| `checks[]` | `gate:text_overflow`, `gate:text_contrast`, `gate:ui_grid` with frame and region. |

Ids are `HudStates@360p` and `HudStates@720p`; each has its own baseline.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| check `gate:text_overflow` fails | 1 | A label is cut. | Fix the layout or the text; the region shows where. |
| check `gate:text_contrast` fails | 1 | Text below 4.5:1. | Change the color or add a backing panel. |

## Examples

### Only one state while fixing it

```sh
dotnet scion trial run HudStates --mode 360p
dotnet scion trial show HudStates@360p --image still
```

### Add a color-blind mode

```csharp
[assembly: TrialModes("360p=640x360", "720p=1280x720", "deuter")]
```

## See also

- [Static trials](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/static-trials/)
- [Gates](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/gates/)
- [Review a UI with the judge](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/ui-review/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Tune a hit effect

This recipe tunes Orchard's critical hit from "it works" to "it feels right" in one sitting. You loop the moment in
the test build, edit a draft graft with `graft watch` injecting every save, read the motion metrics, save the result
as presets, compare them blind with a judge duel, then promote the graft and approve the baselines.

## When to use

- Any feel work on one moment: a hit, a death, a pickup, a turn change.

## Before you begin

- A captured match of the moment (`knight-dies-to-crit`), or a recipe (`SlashHit`).
- Warm copies are not needed: the loop runs its own copy.

## Steps

### 1. Loop the moment

```sh
dotnet scion trial loop "CapturedMatch[match=knight-dies-to-crit]" --span 3..3 --window
```

### 2. Draft the graft and watch

```sh
dotnet scion graft new CritShake --after Orchard.Presentation.HitPresenter.Play
dotnet scion graft watch
```

Edit `scion/grafts/CritShake.cs`; every save shows up on the next pass.

### 3. Read the numbers

```sh
dotnet scion trial run SlashHit --grafts .scion/grafts/ScionGrafts_51c2.dll --motion
```

`metrics.json` gives hit-stop, shake peak and decay, flash length. Aim for the bounds of your spec (for example
hit-stop 50 to 120 ms, shake peak 4 to 12 px).

### 4. Save two feels as presets

`scion/presets/heavy.json` and `scion/presets/snappy.json` with the tunables you settled on.

### 5. Duel them

```sh
dotnet scion trial run SlashHit --grafts .scion/grafts/ScionGrafts_51c2.dll --variants heavy,snappy --motion
dotnet scion judge run <run> --heads hit_weight
dotnet scion judge vote --run <run> --head hit_weight
```

### 6. Promote and approve

```sh
dotnet scion graft promote CritShake
dotnet scion build test
dotnet scion trial run --rounds 2
dotnet scion trial approve --changed --reason "crit shake and hit-stop"
```

Approving `changed` needs a person at a terminal.

## Reference

| Step | Tool | Time |
|---|---|---|
| Loop and edit | `trial loop`, `graft watch` | Seconds per change |
| Measure | `--motion`, `metrics.json` | One run |
| Compare | presets, `judge run`, `judge vote` | Minutes |
| Ship | `graft promote`, `build test`, `trial approve` | One build |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| loop stopped by `error` | 1 | The graft changed the hash. | It touches rules; keep it visual. |
| `SCN113` | 1 | No slot for `HitPresenter.Play`. | Add `AnchorScope(typeof(HitPresenter))`, rebuild. |

## Examples

### A blend between the two feels

```sh
dotnet scion trial run SlashHit --preset "base + 0.5 heavy + 0.5 snappy" --motion
```

### Check photosensitivity before approving

```csharp
protected override void Checks(TrialChecks c) => c.Gate(Gates.Photosensitivity);
```

## See also

- [The live loop](/scion/41664431a8f5/explore/live-loop/)
- [The motion pack](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/motion-pack/)
- [Taste heads and feel presets](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/presets/)
- [From draft to final build](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/lifecycle/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# Audit level rooms

Level rooms break quietly: a prop floats, a door is blocked, a decoration from another biome slips in. This recipe
audits every room template with a `StaticTrial<RoomTemplate>`: two views per room (empty from above, and with units
from the game camera), probes for props and doors, custom gates that fail on the common breakages, and reruns of only
the rooms a change touched.

## When to use

- Games with authored or generated rooms, tiles or arenas.
- After changes to room data, prop prefabs or the placement code.

## Before you begin

- The game can build one room in an empty scene from its template (Orchard's `RoomBuilder.Build(template)`), the same
  code path the game uses.

## Steps

### 1. The static trial

```csharp
public sealed class RoomAudit : StaticTrial<RoomTemplate>
{
    public RoomAudit() { Tags = new[] { "level" }; SettleFrames = 5; }

    protected override IEnumerable<RoomTemplate> Enumerate() => RoomTemplates.All.OrderBy(t => t.Id);
    protected override string ItemName(RoomTemplate t) => t.Id;

    protected override IEnumerator Show(RoomTemplate t, TrialSession s)
    {
        yield return RoomBuilder.Build(t);
    }

    protected override IEnumerator Clear(RoomTemplate t, TrialSession s)
    {
        RoomBuilder.Clear();
        yield break;
    }

    protected override IEnumerable<TrialView> Views(RoomTemplate t)
    {
        yield return TrialView.Top(RoomBuilder.Bounds, pxPerUnit: 16, grid: true);
        yield return TrialView.Screen;
    }

    protected override void Measure(RoomTemplate t, TrialSession s)
    {
        s.Probe(t.Id + "_props", RoomBuilder.Props.Count);
        s.Probe(t.Id + "_doors_open", RoomBuilder.Doors.Count(d => d.Reachable));
    }
}
```

### 2. Custom gates

Register `FloatingPropGate` and a `BlockedDoorGate` as `ITrialCheck` ([Gates](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/gates/) shows the
first). Others worth writing: a prop clipping another prop, a prop from a foreign biome, an invisible blocker on the
navigation mesh, a room that does not match its template's size.

### 3. Run and review

```sh
dotnet scion trial run RoomAudit -j 6
dotnet scion trial show RoomAudit --image sheet
```

### 4. Recapture only what changed

```sh
dotnet scion trial run RoomAudit --changed
```

`--changed` takes the ids that were `changed` or `stale` in the last run; for static trials, the stills that changed
are listed in `compare.json`.

## Reference

| Output | Content |
|---|---|
| `<room>.top.png` | From above with a 1-unit grid. |
| `<room>.png` | The game camera with units placed. |
| `sheet.png` | Every room, labeled. |
| probes | Props and reachable doors per room. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| check `gate:floating_prop` fails | 1 | A prop is above the ground. | Fix the prefab pivot or the placement. |
| check `gate:blocked_door` fails | 1 | No path through a door. | Move the blocking prop. |

## Examples

### A judge head trained on past room reviews

```sh
dotnet scion judge new room_quality --question scion/judge/questions/room_quality.json --view full
dotnet scion judge run <run> --heads room_quality
```

### Only one biome

```csharp
protected override IEnumerable<RoomTemplate> Enumerate() => RoomTemplates.All.Where(t => t.Biome == "orchard");
```

## See also

- [Static trials](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/static-trials/)
- [Gates](/scion/41664431a8f5/evaluation/gates/)
- [Checks](/scion/41664431a8f5/trials/checks/)

# Troubleshooting

Each entry starts from what you see, names the usual cause and gives the fix. Run `dotnet scion doctor --level 3`
first: it catches most setup problems with a hint. Error codes link to [Error and warning codes](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/).

## No copies start

**Symptom.** `trial run` ends at once with `build_not_found` or `player_crashed`.

**Cause.** No test build at the discovered path, a build from another machine (paths in `scion-build.json`), or a
macOS quarantine flag on a downloaded build.

**Fix.** `dotnet scion build test`; or `--build <path>`; on macOS, `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine <app>`.

## Every verdict is stale

**Symptom.** All ids are `stale` after switching machines or Unity versions.

**Cause.** Images are compared per platform (OS, graphics API, size, capture), and the baseline has no folder for
this platform, or Unity, fps or player args changed.

**Fix.** The hash is still compared, so `stale` with the same hash is safe. A person approves once on the new
platform: `dotnet scion trial approve --changed --reason "baselines for linux-vulkan"`.

## editor_open when building

**Symptom.** `build test` exits 3 with `editor_open`.

**Cause.** The project is open in Unity and `com.unity.pipeline` is not installed, so the CLI cannot build through the
editor and cannot start a second one on the same project.

**Fix.** Close the editor, or install the pipeline package and build again.

## SCN113 when injecting

**Symptom.** `graft inject` reports `SCN113: HitPresenter.PlayCritical has no slot in this build.`

**Cause.** The test build has no slot for that method: no promoted graft on it and no `AnchorScope` covering it.

**Fix.** Add `[assembly: AnchorScope(typeof(HitPresenter))]`, `dotnet scion build test`, inject again.

## SCN120 on a test build

**Symptom.** The build fails with `SCION_SLOTS needs a JIT backend (Mono)`.

**Cause.** The test defines were set in Player Settings and the project builds with IL2CPP.

**Fix.** Remove the defines from Player Settings; build tests with `dotnet scion build test`, which sets Mono and the
defines only for the build.

## Empty captures in batchmode

**Symptom.** Exit 3 `capture_broken`, or black `window.png`.

**Cause.** A player started by hand with `-batchmode` and without offscreen capture, or a camera that renders only
to the screen.

**Fix.** Let the CLI start players, or add `-scion-offscreen`. Cameras with a target texture of their own need to be
captured with a `TrialView`.

## Ports already in use

**Symptom.** `no_free_port`, or co-op clients that never connect.

**Cause.** Another server holds ports, or `port_arg` is missing, so every group uses the game's default port.

**Fix.** Set `trials.port_arg` to the game's port flag; close stray servers (`dotnet scion trial serve --stop`).

## px_unstable warnings

**Symptom.** `px_unstable` and `px_changed` verdicts that come and go.

**Cause.** Something visual is not deterministic: particles started before the recipe, an animator on unscaled real
time, a shader reading `_Time` from a non-redirected source.

**Fix.** Keep `Control = DeterminismControl.All`; run `--rounds 3 --check` and read `determinism.tsv`; mask only what is
random on purpose.

## Frame count off by one

**Symptom.** `frame_jitter: ["CoopTurn 212/213"]`.

**Cause.** The Netcode tick runs on the real clock.

**Fix.** Turn on `SCION_NETCLOCK` with `netclock_assemblies` ([Netcode clock](/scion/41664431a8f5/determinism/netclock/)).

## Low memory

**Symptom.** `low_memory` warnings, copies killed by the OS, `player_crashed`.

**Cause.** `-j` above what free memory allows (about 550 MB per copy for Orchard).

**Fix.** Lower `-j` to `doctor`'s `suggested_copies`, or use warm copies or the mosaic.

## A recipe passes alone and fails in the queue

**Symptom.** `trial run SlashHit` passes; `trial run` fails it.

**Cause.** State leaks from an earlier recipe: a static, `Time.timeScale`, a pool, a scene left loaded.

**Fix.** Reset it in the adapter's `Teardown` or on `TrialSession.Boundary`.

## See also

- [Error and warning codes](/scion/41664431a8f5/reference/errors/)
- [What to do next](/scion/41664431a8f5/agents/next-action/)
- [doctor](/scion/41664431a8f5/cli/doctor/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# FAQ

Short answers to the questions people ask first. Each links to the page with the details.

## Questions

### Does Scion ship to players

Only as direct calls. The final build calls promoted grafts directly (call mode): no slots, no injection, no trials,
no lab code, no reflection. A final build with test defines fails (SCN121). See [Build modes](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/build-modes/).

### Why does the test build need Mono

Slots are replaced while the game runs, which needs a JIT. IL2CPP compiles ahead of time. The test build is Mono; the
final build can be IL2CPP.

### Do I need Netcode or URP

No. Neither is a dependency. Scion knows how to redirect their time reads when you list them in `ScionSettings.json`,
and co-op trials work with any networking that takes command-line flags.

### Which platforms

The editor and the CLI run on macOS, Windows and Linux. Test builds run on the desktop platforms. See
[Requirements](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/requirements/).

### Why not Harmony or MonoMod

They patch at run time, which IL2CPP does not support, and their errors appear only when the code runs. Scion weaves
at compile time: errors come with file and line, and final builds have plain direct calls.

### Can grafts change rules

No. Grafts are visual; rules change in the core through `RuleModifier<T>`. See
[Grafts are visual only](/scion/41664431a8f5/grafts/visual-only/).

### How much does an agent spend

The CLI returns compact JSON (about 1.5 KB) with a `next_step`, and images are paths, not content, so an agent reads
only what it needs. The project index is under 2 KB. The judge runs locally and costs nothing per image.

### Does Scion call AI models

No. The CLI, the MCP server and the judge never call a hosted model. Agent evaluators answer through files.

### Does it work offline

Yes. After installing the package, the CLI and (optionally) the judge's eye model, nothing needs the network.

### What is the license

Apache-2.0. See [License](/scion/41664431a8f5/help/license/).

### Where do I report a bug

On the GitHub repository's issues, with the output of `dotnet scion doctor --level 3` and the run's `report.md`.

## See also

- [What is Scion](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/overview/)
- [Requirements](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/requirements/)

# Changelog

All notable changes to Scion are listed here, newest first, in the [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/)
format. Scion follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html); what counts as a breaking change is
on [Versioning and compatibility](/scion/41664431a8f5/contribute/compatibility/). The same entries are in the package's
`CHANGELOG.md`.

## [1.0.0] - 2026-10-13

First stable release.

### Grafts

- `[Before]` and `[After]` with `Priority` and `Observe`; compile-time weaver (ILPostProcessor on Mono.Cecil) with call
  mode for final builds and slot mode for test builds.
- `ref Call` and `ref Call<T>`: `Skip`, `Return`, `Result`, `Skipped`, `Tag`.
- Anchors: `[Anchor(Id, Doc)]`, `[assembly: AnchorScope]`, `Anchors.Id`, `anchor list` and `anchor show`.
- Live injection: `graft build`, `graft inject` (merge or isolate), `graft restore`, `graft disable`, `InjectReport`.
- Draft lifecycle: `graft new`, `graft check`, `graft promote`, `graft watch`.
- `Faults`, the `Fx` facade with `IFxSink`, `[Tunable]` with presets and blends.
- Diagnostics SCN101 to SCN114, SCN120, SCN121, SCN130, SCN131.

### Trials

- Recipes, adapters, `TrialSession`, checks and `ITrialCheck`; variants with `[Vary]` and `Variants()`, modes and
  seed ranges.
- Static trials with views and sheets; co-op groups of 1 to 4 players; captured matches (F9); the mosaic.
- Parallel copies with shards, warm copies with `trial serve`, `trial run`, `show`, `approve`, `diff`, `eval`, `loop`.
- Baselines per platform with perceptual image comparison, masks and learned unstable masks.
- Specs (`TrialSpec`) with balance, visual, judge, metamorphic and curve parts.
- Diagnostics SCN201 to SCN203.

### Determinism

- Virtual clock, screen, random and real-time waits in test builds; `[WallClock]`; `DeterminismControl` for
  particles, animators, UI Toolkit and physics; `SCION_NETCLOCK`.
- `--check`, `--jitter`, `determinism.tsv`; `scion diagnose` with SCN301 to SCN307 and adoption levels.

### Evaluation and the Judge

- Gates: text overflow, UI grid, contrast, photosensitivity, regression, telemetry versus pixels, nothing changed,
  palette.
- The motion pack and metrics; blind A/B comparisons; file-based evaluators.
- The Judge: eyes and heads, `judge list`, `show`, `new`, `vote`, `train`, `run`.

### Exploration

- The multiverse, the live loop, bisect, metamorphic tests, the rare-moment hunter, guided search, balance with the
  simulator.

### Standard and core

- `Scion.Core`: `RuleModifier<T>`, `Stage`, `ISimulation`, bots and capabilities; analyzers SCN001 to SCN005.

### Tools and agents

- `dotnet scion` CLI with JSON envelopes and schemas; `init`, `new`, `uninstall`, `doctor`, `build`, `index`,
  `guard`, `gen`, `mcp`.
- Claude Code plugin with the skill and hooks; MCP server with docs tools; `llms.txt` and Markdown pages.
- `Scion.Testing`, `Scion.Compare`, `Scion.Specs` and `Scion.Core` on NuGet.

## See also

license and the same `NOTICE`. Third-party code and models keep their own licenses.

- Notice: `NOTICE` in the package, to keep with redistributions.
- You may use Scion in commercial games. Final builds contain only Scion's runtime attributes and generated
  dispatchers, under the same license.

The judge's eye models are downloaded separately and keep their licenses; check each model card before
redistributing heads trained on them ([Models and licenses](/scion/41664431a8f5/judge/models/)). Heads trained on your own votes and
captures are yours.

# Architecture

This page is for contributors and for anyone who needs to know how Scion works inside: which assemblies exist and
what each does, how data moves from a build to a verdict, what the weaver generates (the ABI that injection depends
on), and how the package is tested. For using Scion, start at [What is Scion](/scion/41664431a8f5/start/overview/).

## How it works

### Components

Scion has code Unity compiles into the game (runtime), code that runs in the editor at build time, and .NET tools
outside Unity. Folders ending in `~` (`Tools~`, `Tests~`, `Documentation~`) travel with the package and are ignored by
Unity's importer.

| Component | Assembly | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Runtime | `Scion.Runtime` | Graft attributes, `Call`, `Fx`, `Faults`, `Anchors`; under `SCION_TRIALS` the virtual clock, screen and random. |
| Injection | `Scion.Injection` | Slots, `Injection`, `InjectReport` (`SCION_SLOTS`). |
| Trials | `Scion.Trials` | The session, recipes, adapters, checks, capture, static trials, co-op, mosaic (`SCION_TRIALS`). Its pure logic (flags, shards, writers, checks) has no `UnityEngine` and is tested with `dotnet test`. |
| Control | `Scion.Control` | The control server for warm copies and live injection. |
| Core | `Scion.Core` | The engine-free rules API: `RuleModifier<T>`, `ISimulation`, tunables, probes. |
| Editor | `Scion.Editor` | `ScionBuild`, build guards, `scion-build.json`. |
| Weaver | `Unity.Scion.CodeGen` | The `ILPostProcessor`. Only `ScionWeaver.cs` touches Unity's ILPP API; the model, resolver and emitters are plain Mono.Cecil, shared with the CLI. |
| CLI | `Scion.Cli` (dotnet tool) | Every command; reads builds with Mono.Cecil and never loads them. |
| Analyzers | `Scion.Analyzers` | Roslyn analyzers with the weaver's ids and texts; loaded by Unity through the `RoslynAnalyzer` label. |
| Compare | `Scion.Compare` | Image comparison, masks, heatmaps, its own PNG reader and writer. |
| Testing | `Scion.Testing` | `FxRecorder` and `Scion.Runtime` for .NET. |
| Specs | `Scion.Specs` | Specs, gates ids, metamorphic properties. |

### Data flow

1. Unity compiles the game; the weaver rewrites anchors (call mode or slot mode) and writes the determinism scan.
2. `build test` produces the player and `scion-build.json` (build id, slots, recipes).
3. `trial run` starts copies with `-scion-*` flags; each `TrialSession` plays its shard and writes `q<i>/`.
4. The CLI merges copies, compares with `scion/baselines/` using `Scion.Compare`, and writes `summary.json`.
5. `graft build` compiles drafts with Roslyn against the build's assemblies and the same emitters as the weaver;
   `graft inject` sends the DLL over the control protocol; `Injection` swaps slots at the next boundary.

### The generated ABI

Injection depends on names the weaver generates. They are fixed by `Anchors`:

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `__ScionGenerated` | The generated type in each woven assembly. |
| `D_<id>` | The dispatcher of an anchor side (call mode). |
| `F_<id>` | The slot field of an anchor side (slot mode). |
| `__Restore` | Restores every slot to the promoted grafts. |
| `AbiVersion` | 1; a constant in `Anchors` and in every `__ScionGenerated`. A DLL of another ABI is refused (SCN131). |
| `Anchors.Id` | The id format shared by the weaver, the CLI and the injection. |

### Diagnostics in one place

`DiagnosticIds.cs` is the single catalog of SCN ids, severities, messages and hints. The weaver and the analyzers
compile it; the runtime and the CLI repeat only the id, and a parity test checks every id used exists.

### Tests

```sh
cd Packages/me.jandson.scion/Tests~
dotnet test Scion.Tests.slnx
```

| Project | Covers |
|---|---|
| Weaver tests | Weaving real assemblies with Cecil, call and slot mode, diagnostics, redirects. |
| Analyzer tests | Each SCN analyzer with positive and negative cases. |
| Trials tests | Flags, shards, filters, writers, checks, adapter choice, without Unity. |
| CLI tests | Commands against fake builds and run folders; envelopes validated against the JSON Schemas. |
| Compare tests | Metric, masks, learned masks, heatmaps. |

Play-mode tests in Unity cover capture, offscreen rendering and the control server.

## Key terms

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ILPP | `ILPostProcessor`: Unity's hook to rewrite compiled assemblies. |
| Call mode, slot mode | How anchors reach grafts in final and test builds. |
| ABI | The generated names and `AbiVersion` that injection relies on. |
| Pure logic | Code without `UnityEngine`, compiled twice: by Unity and by `dotnet test`. |

## Guarantees and limits

- The weaver never weaves assemblies named `Scion.*` or `Unity.Scion.*`.
- Redirect targets (`Clock`, `VirtualScreen`, `SeededRandom`, `VirtualWaitForSecondsRealtime`) stay in `Scion.Runtime`
  forever, because assemblies such as Unity UI do not reference other Scion assemblies.
- Renaming a redirect target is never silent: SCN114 and a test fail.
- The CLI never loads game DLLs; it reads them with Cecil.

# Versioning and compatibility

Scion follows Semantic Versioning: within 1.x nothing documented breaks; breaking changes wait for 2.0. This page says
exactly what "documented" covers, how each surface evolves, and which pieces must have the same version.

## Surfaces

| Surface | Within 1.x | Breaking change means |
|---|---|---|
| C# API (public types and members) | Members may be added; none removed or changed. | Removing or changing a signature. |
| Weaver ABI (`Anchors.AbiVersion`) | Stays 1. | A new ABI number; DLLs of another ABI are refused (SCN131). |
| Player flags (`-scion-*`) | Flags may be added; none removed or changed in meaning. | Removing or redefining a flag. |
| File formats (`schema_version`) | Optional fields may be added; readers ignore unknown fields. | `schema_version: 2` and a `v2/` schema folder. |
| CLI output (envelope and command fields) | Fields may be added. | Removing or renaming a field. |
| Exit codes and error codes | Stable; new codes may be added. | Changing what a code means. |
| SCN ids | Never reused; new ids may be added; severities may be lowered, not raised. | Raising a warning to an error. |
| Verdicts (`same`, `within`, `px_changed`, `changed`, `new`, `stale`) | Stable. | Adding or redefining a verdict. |

## Versions that must match

| Pair | Rule | When they differ |
|---|---|---|
| CLI and package | Same version. | `doctor` warns `version_mismatch`; injection may fail with SCN131. |
| Graft DLL and test build | Built against the same `build_id`. | SCN130. |
| `Scion.Testing`, `Scion.Compare`, `Scion.Specs`, `Scion.Core` and the package | Same version. | Tests may compile against members the game does not have. |

The CLI's NuGet version is the package version; local development builds use a `-dev` suffix.

## Deprecation

A member to be removed in 2.0 is marked `[Obsolete]` with the replacement in the message for at least one minor
version, and listed in the changelog under "Deprecated".

## Supported Unity versions

Each release states its minimum Unity version in `package.json` (`unity: 6000.3`). A minor release may raise it only
when the previous Unity is out of Unity's support.
